...are set together into a unity: accordingly the Earth and the Water are separated from the other two <margin>A</margin> and also made into one. These are the two double <term>Yliastri</term> <note>the primeval, undifferentiated substances</note>: The Air is for itself, the Fire also: The Earth and the Water are also likewise.

Thus God created the center of His realm materially, and then set it in the Three Firsts <note>the *Tria Prima*: Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt</note> threefold, from which everything grows forth forever: and without these three nothing can grow in the four Yliastri: and when they grow, they are elements, and thus lose their name Yliaster further, and are called elements.

### VIII.

These four elements are separated in their place and essence, none mixed with another, but set apart, like a carver throwing away pieces from a statue that make his image unformed. Thus there are four elements, but only Three Firsts: three in the Air, three in the Fire, three in the Earth, and three in the Water: and everywhere there is only one Three Firsts; that is, a <term>Mercury</term> in all, a <term>Sulfur</term> in all, a <term>Salt</term> in all: but divided in their properties. What is growing herb, leaf, and grass, has come into the Earth: What is mineral, into the Water: What is Cold and Warm, Day and Night, into the Fire: What is Air, into the <term>Chaos</term> <note>here referring to the atmospheric space or "gaping void" of the air</note>: and all three are one thing, each in itself: and is just like a stone that lies there, and is divided into four parts: from one a statue, from the other a pot, from the third a bowl, from the fourth a boundary stone, and they are all stone, and one stone, but divided into four.

Of these Yliastri there are four and no more, they are also enough: Thus God has set the world in a foursquare, and let it be enough with that, though He might well have made eight. He created one part of nourishment in <margin>B</margin> the Air, the second in the Fire, the third in the Earth, the fourth in the Water: thus everything is there. Now it behooves us to philosophize further of these four, to treat them in the name of the elements, and of their <term>Potentijs</term> <note>original Latin: "powers" or potencies</note> and <term>Actibus</term> <note>original Latin: "actions" or operations</note> which they have: and to begin with the Air, and thereby to complete the philosophy in the Water, as far as the birth of insensitive things is contained within.

### IX.

The element Air is ordained for nothing further than solely to be a house for the other three elements, to hold the same, each in its chamber, thus. The Air encloses everything mortal within it, and separates it from the eternal, just as a wall separates its city from the land: And holds the world together, like a dam holds a pond: And is just like a thing where nothing is outside the egg that belongs to the egg, or in the egg that belongs outside: Thus the heaven is a shell that separates the world and the heaven <note>referring to the physical atmosphere versus the celestial realm</note>, just like a shell [separates] the egg and that which is outside: And is a skin in which the whole world is a body, and therein the Earth is contained and kept. Now, however, the Air is further the heaven, that is the skin, that is the shell, that is the wall, that is the dam, out of which nothing may go, and that which is outside thereof, nothing may come in. And it is also the Air, the breath, from which all things have life: For he is the Air, and gives the Air that nourishes the three elements, and man in his life. For where this Air were not, we could not live: Then no element would proceed, no wind could blow, no rain, no snow, no sun shine, no summer nor any water flow, no earth bear fruit: This same power comes from the Air, and is drawn to themselves by the three elements. Just as in us the lungs draw the same to themselves every moment, so also the Earth, the Water, and Fire. It is a great error to think that the winds are from the Air: For they go into us like poison, not <margin>C</margin> like life: It is only the first element that gives us the Air: The Fire gives the wind.

### X.

This element also gives the power that the Fire hangs upon it and does not fall, and is a chain that lifts and carries without any material or visibility: This happens through its <term>Chaos</term>, which lies between the skin and the Earth. And is a <term>medium Interstricium</term> <note>original Latin: "intervening middle space"</note>, and goes from heaven down to the Earth: therein floats the Fire, therein float the Earth and the Water. And in the same way as the yolk in the egg is held by the <term>Clar</term> <note>the egg white or albumen</note> so that it does not touch the shell: so the Chaos holds the globe so that it does not fall in any direction. This Chaos is invisible and appears green, and is the untouchable <term>Clar</term> and <term>Albumen</term> <note>original Latin: "egg white"</note>, and yet has the power that it lifts, so that the Earth stands apart and cannot move. Like the <term>Vitellus Oui</term> <note>original Latin: "yolk of the egg"</note> in its white, so the globe of Earth and Water floats in this air: As a ship is sustained upon the sea, so is that also sustained. This is the great <term>Albumen</term>, the wonderful clear substance, which carries such a globe of Earth and Water, and is invisible: It also carries the <term>Firmamentum</term> <note>the starry heavens</note>, and stands in it, just as the <term>Semen Cucumeris</term> <note>original Latin: "cucumber seed"</note> in its <term>Mucilagine</term> <note>original Latin: "mucilage" or slimy coating</note>: Just as the <term>Semen Generationis</term> <note>original Latin: "seed of generation"</note> in the <term>Sperma</term> <note>original Latin: "reproductive fluid"</note>: Just as a piece of meat lies in its <term>Sultz</term> <note>aspic or jelly</note>, so the stars lie in it, and have their course in this clear substance, like a bird in its flight: And they are not otherwise held than in the same way as the examples show, which hold that which is in them: Only with the difference that the Chaos is distinguished from the white, from the sperm, from the mucilage, in that it is untouchable and subtle; otherwise in all power and might equal to the others mentioned.

<header>ON THE ELEMENT OF AIR.</header>

<margin>A</margin>
### XI.
To speak of the power of this element, it is further known that the Air, and its <term>Chaos</term> <note>here meaning the vast atmospheric space</note>, and its heaven, stand in such a rotundity <note>roundness or sphericity</note> that no one within it can truly determine what is bottom or top, and it is like this: In an egg that lies there, it is impossible for one inside (if it were possible to be inside) to know which part belongs to the top or the bottom. For the rotundity ensures that no height or depth can be perceived. Thus we are within the shell, such that we do not know which is down or up, and we walk upon the entire globe toward heaven, and everything is both a height and a depth. The reason for this is that the roundness of the globe and the heavens allows such a thing, and it is so placed into the mortal body that all things should grow in <term>Trivial Lines</term> <note>vertical lines or axes of growth</note>; not only man in his walking, but all trees, all veins, and all springs. For just as God created the circle of the globe and the heaven, He also created the half-circle, the diameter, the meridian lines, and found the trivial lines, circles, and fractions. For therein lies Geography, Cosmography, and Geometry. Through the elemental Geometry of the Air, the structures of the Fire are maintained—that is, the Sun, Moon, and all stars; those of the Earth—trees and the like; those of the Water—minerals and others. There is the true ground of all Geometry, in which lines man stands, and therein looks swiftly toward heaven. Of this Geometry, God alone is the Master, the Stonemason, and the Geometer. Nothing falls out of these lines, nor does anything walk beside or out of them; neither water nor fire, neither earth nor trees, neither man nor beast. Instead, everything moves within the Geometry of the Air, into which God has fashioned them, just as a stonemason carves his figures on a tower or the like.

<margin>B</margin>
### XII.
Now, to know further of the philosophers regarding the <term>Three Firsts</term> <note>Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt</note> and how they exist in the element of Air: the <term>Three Firsts</term> <note>original: "MS. S. S.", standing for Mercurius, Sulphur, Sal</note> are the element of Air, and are prepared so that they yield an atmosphere and fulfill the element of Air. Initially, the heaven is nothing but a white <term>Sulfur</term> <note>original: "SS"</note> coagulated with the spirit of salt and clarified with <term>Mercury</term>, and the hardness of all this element is in this skin and shell, fabricated therein. Thereafter, the second of the Three Firsts is further transformed into two parts: one is the Chaos, and the other is the Air, and it happens thus. The Sulfur resolved itself through the spirit of salt into the <term>Liquor of Mercury</term>, which is a fluid in itself, and is distributed from the heaven down to the earth; it is the <term>heavenly white</term> <note>original: "Albumen Cœli," a reference to the egg-white-like substance of the firmament</note>, and is the <term>intermediate space</term> <note>original: "Medium Interstitium"</note>, and is clear and chaos, subtle and <term>diaphanous</term> <note>transparent</note>. For all thickness and dryness and subtle nature has been resolved, and never remains as it was in itself. The Air is thus: the third remnant of the Three Firsts of the Air has passed into an "air," just as when wood burns and turns into smoke; so this passes into an air and remains in its atmosphere until the end of the elements, and has become a Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt that are consumed from substance into an air, no different than wood becoming smoke. And it is nothing but a smoke of the Three Firsts of the element of Air. Thus, nothing more arises from the element of Air than what has been mentioned. Many of the ancients and also the moderns, and even those living in my time, want to attribute the winds to the Air and place their origin in the mobility of the heavens. This is all nothing; for the heaven does not move—it is the Air in itself, and it issues from the element just as smoke issues from wood. He who wishes to well understand how the motion is, let him read of Fire in its powers, which gives more meaning than is contained here.

<margin>C</margin>

# SECOND BOOK
# OF THE PHILOSOPHY OF THEOPHRASTUS,
# ON THE GENERATIONS
# OF THE ELEMENTS:
## ON THE ELEMENT OF FIRE.
### FIRST TREATISE
### i

<image-desc>A square woodcut decorative initial 'A' featuring a kneeling figure in a landscape with hills and a distant town or tower.</image-desc>

Just as it stands regarding the element of Air in terms of place—how the elements are set, the Air initially, and then the Fire—these two now surround the entire globe. However, as to how the element of Fire stands and exists, we wish to philosophize further upon that, and it is as follows.

From the <term>Yliaster</term> <note>the primordial, undifferentiated matter</note> were separated first of all the Air and the Fire; afterward, those same two were separated from one another. First the Air, as it stands in the First Book; thereafter the Fire was ordered. In this separation, two elements came apart from each other: the Air and the Fire. From...

<meta>Vol. II.</meta>

<summary>Paracelsus explains that the element of Air acts as a spherical container for the world, governed by divine geometry that dictates the growth and placement of all things. He describes the chemical transition of the Three Firsts into a "smoke-like" air before beginning his discourse on the element of Fire.</summary>

<keywords>Element of Air, Element of Fire, Tria Prima, Mercury, Sulfur, Salt, Geometry, Yliaster, Cosmology, Paracelsus, Spherical World</keywords>

--- Page 38 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Four Elements from the previous page, transitioning from the properties of the Air to the Book II, which focuses on the Element of Fire (the Firmament).</meta>

<header>86 PHILOSOPHY, BOOK II.</header>

<margin>A</margin>
From the Air the heavens were made; from the Fire, the firmament. Just as in the Air there is only the <term>Chaos</term> <note>The vast, empty space or medium</note> and nothing else: so also in the Element of Fire there is Heat and Cold, Light and Darkness. And everything that the Globe and the Air lack is preserved within the Element of Fire. And the Element of Fire is not so named because it knows nothing but burning—as many have claimed—for that which burns is not the Element of Fire. Rather, that which burns, and that which is its opposite—freezing—both belong to it. The Element of Fire does not consist only of the <term>Complexion</term> <note>The temperament or elemental balance</note> of Hot and Dry, but also of Cold and Wet, which also comes from the Element of Fire. Therefore, those act ignorantly who seek the Element of Fire within the elements of Water or Earth. Although these elements may produce something hot in their complexion, this heat does not constitute the Element. The Element is not called an element because it is a fire, but because the entire firmament stands within it. Therefore it is an element from which shall come the Day, the Night, the <note>original: "Weiss Candor"</note> White Brightness, the <note>original: "Rot Candor"</note> Red Brightness, the rains, the weather, the <term>Tempestates</term> <note>Storms or seasons</note>, the winds, and all <term>Impressiones</term> <note>Atmospheric phenomena</note>. It is a place and one part of the four parts of creation, which is why it is called an Element. For just as the Earth gives Heat and Cold and is the <note>Latin: "Elementum Terræ"</note> Element of Earth, so also is the Fire to be understood.
However, the distinction must be known: that material fire <note>The fire we use in kitchens or forges</note> is called an element, though it is actually no element at all. For it does not come from the Element of Fire; rather, it is like the Element of Fire in the place belonging to the Sun. Similarly, water is like the Element of Fire in the place where it rains. The material fire that we use is found within the four elements and is called <term>TRISTO</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for the internal, vital heat or 'sulfur' within matter</note>, and it exists in that way. The Element of Water must have the Element of Fire within it for its operation; this same fire remains in the Element of Water and reveals itself in steel and stones that are within it. It is also in the Element of Earth and reveals itself in its fruits.
<margin>B</margin>
In the Air it is likewise: and thus it is to be understood of the others, that each has its *Tristo* within it, as is shown in <note>Latin title: "De Natura Rerum" (On the Nature of Things)</note>. Therefore, the Sun may manifest its element in wood, igniting and burning it. This happens through the same power by which the Element of Fire moistens the Earth with rain; in that same manner, it also burns wood. And just as the Element of Fire moistens the Earth—which is its power and property—so it also ignites wood and the burning-mirror in the Sun. Thus, material fire comes upon the Globe just as rain falls upon the Earth; both come from one Element, though separated into their specific kinds. But the fire that comes out of stones and metals entered them from the Sun, in its <term>Ares</term> <note>The formative spiritual force in nature</note>. Just as the Earth is nourished by the Sun, so one element nourishes the other. For the Salt of the <term>Three Firsts</term> <note>The primary principles: Salt, Mercury, and Sulfur</note> could not coagulate if the Element of Fire were not within it; Mercury could not provide the body if it did not have the Element of Water within it; likewise Sulfur without its <note>original: "Terrestritet"</note> Earthiness. And the Air is without <note>Latin: "Materia"</note> matter, intangible and <note>original: "Corporalisch"</note> bodily; therefore it cannot provide a body like the other elements, but it works along with them, as the others do.

### II.

Now that the separation of these two elements, Air and Fire, has occurred, there follows the order of the same, which is as follows: Initially, in the division, the Sun, the Moon, and all other stars were ordered. Nothing else is the Element of Fire except these very things. With what power and nature they are further endowed, beyond what we indicate here, may be found in *On the Nature of Things*.
<margin>C</margin>
But it is important to know here that this element—that is, the firmament—is nothing other than the stars. And what they bring forth upon the Earth—snow and rain, wind and hail and other things, cold and heat, day and night, summer and winter, and the like—all come from the Element of Fire, like a child from its mother or an apple from its tree. This Element of Fire is placed within the Element of Air. For just as Water and Earth are in one globe, so Fire and Air are mixed in one, each without damaging the body of the other. And they stand in the Air, standing freely, without hanging, without a floor; but just as birds fly in the air, so is the Sun's path in the heaven, which is to say, in the Air. For just as man 
<margin>Also called Gnomus.</margin>
is ordered to walk upon the Earth, the bird in the Air, the fish in the Water, and the <term>Gnarus</term> <note>A term for the Gnomus or Earth-spirit</note> in the Earth: so also the four elements are ordered—one lies, another flies, one thus, the other so—and they have no fixed seat or place. Each star has its own path, none like the other. For just as among men on Earth no one walks exactly like another, yet it is all one walking; so it is also with the stars. And as they are not equal to one another in their nature, so it is with the stars—so manifold is their kind and their being. Therefore, concerning them, nothing further is

<header>ON THE ELEMENT OF FIRE.</header>

<margin>A</margin>
# SECOND TREATISE.
->ON THE SUN, LIGHT, DARKNESS,<-
->AND NIGHT.<-

**As** was previously stated in the First Treatise, the primary <term>Yliaster</term> <note>In Paracelsian philosophy, the Yliaster is the primordial matter or "star-matter" from which all things were created</note> is composed of all colors, bright and beautiful in a mixture, from which the four elements were separated. Whatever has been assigned to the Element of Fire and organized under it will be treated hereafter. Initially, however, the first element, <term>Air</term> <note>original: "Aer"</note>, was drawn from the Yliaster, and after that the Element of Fire; from this, the separation occurred. First, the white <term>Brightness</term> <note>Latin: "Canditor"</note> was taken out, and from it a measure and Matter was made: that is the Sun. In this Sun is the entire Element of Fire’s white <term>Radiance</term> <note>Latin: "Candor"</note>, and furthermore, in the whole element, there is no other white radiance. The red <term>Transparency</term> <note>Latin: "Diaphaniter"</note> was also drawn out and entered into the stars. This consists of the moon and other stars, and they are divided into many pieces. Just as the white radiance is gathered into a single globe, so are the stars divided into many pieces regarding the red <term>Radiance</term> <note>Latin: "Candorem"</note>.

From this follows day and night: for the reason that because all white radiance is gathered into one globe, the day exists only where that globe is. Where the globe is not, there is no white radiance; there is night and darkness. For the red radiance gives no light compared to the white radiance. It should also be known that in the Element of Fire there are two natures: Hot and Cold. All heat is in the white radiance, and all cold is in the red. All the fire that is hot is contained entirely within the Sun, and nowhere else in the firmament; all other cold is in the stars, and not within the Sun. From this it follows that summer comes from the Sun, and cold comes from the stars.

<margin>B</margin>For in the Sun there is <term>expulsive heat</term> <note>Latin: "Calor expulsivus"</note>, and in the stars there is <term>expulsive cold</term> <note>Latin: "Frigus expulsivum"</note>, as follows: The Sun casts its heat out from itself through its rays upon the globe. Just like a wind coming out of a hole, or like a stalk growing out of the earth onto the earth: so the heat goes out from the Sun upon the globe. For heat is the Sun’s fruit upon the globe, and it has no other fruit. From this it follows that the Sun has two effects: a greater and a lesser heat, thus: It divides its heat in two ways, whereby the cold stars are allowed to manifest their cold; and it happens like this. For us Germans, when the Sun is at its highest, its heat is greatest for us: for then is its autumn and its harvest. In winter, there is its cold: not because the Sun stands low—for it is the same old Sun that could always give heat through its rays—but its harvest is not at that time; rather, it is its fallow month. For all fruits are either in the fallow or in the harvest. But that it is hot beneath us, in Ethiopia and elsewhere, when it reaches the <term>Antarctic Pole</term> <note>Latin: "Antarcticum Polum"</note>, and cold for us: this is because it is harvest time in that place, and for us it is the fallow period. Thus, it lies fallow more or less. For all things that are to bear fruit must rest and sleep. If this fallow period did not exist for the Sun, then its heat would be the same for us in winter as in summer.

But since the Sun now lies fallow, the harvest and autumn of the cold stars are arranged so that the entire year is never without fruit. For thus falls the snow, thus blows the <term>North Wind</term> <note>Latin: "Boreas"</note>; after these follow the <term>East Wind</term> <note>Latin: "Eurus"</note> and the <term>South Wind</term> <note>Latin: "Auster"</note>, which are the Sun’s companions. Thus the winter and summer, night and day, and the year are created. From their course from one harvest to another come the <term>Year of the Sun</term> <note>Latin: "Jahr Solis"</note> and the <term>Year of the Stars</term> <note>Latin: "Jahr Stellarum"</note>.

<margin>C</margin>In this, it is further to be known that dryness and moisture run alongside, as follows. Dryness is in the heat, which is to say, in the Sun; and otherwise there is no dryness in the entire Element of Fire, except for what the Sun has within itself. Moisture is in the cold, which is to say, in the cold stars, which are those of the red radiance, and it is like this. Moisture cannot endure in heat, for heat consumes all moisture and desires to be dry; cold does not stand in dryness, for what is cold resolves and dissolves itself when the heat coagulates. Thus the Element of Fire is divided into two parts: in one is dryness, and it is in the Sun; in the other is moisture, and it is in the cold. And if the cold should seem to dry things out, as might be observed, it is just like a dryness; just as when one sweats in the sun, it is a foreign moisture, so this is a foreign cold. Now it is true that a moist body on earth may be dried by the stars, but not through a dry nature; rather, through their cold they may coagulate it so that it seems to be dry. Thus their dry nature is to be understood, like frozen water. Similarly, the Sun also affects moisture: through its heat it melts wax so that it dissolves, and likewise with <term>tallow</term> <note>original: "Vnshlet"</note> and the <term>Agate</term> <note>original: "Agapas", likely referring to a type of stone or "achates"</note>. How does this concern the foundation? Not at all, except as an example for you. Thus there is dryness in the stars: that is snow, that is <term>drizzling sleet</term> <note>original: "Rislen"</note>, that is frost, these are <term>hailstones</term> <note>Latin: "Grandines"</note>, these are <term>lightnings</term> <note>Latin: "Fulgura"</note>, and similar metals and stones that come from them. But what kind of dryness is its snow, which does not remain dry? What kind of dryness is its lightning, which does not remain? What kind of dryness is its metal, which returns again to its primary matter? And other things of the sort. Likewise of the Sun: what is its moisture? It does not remain. For what is it that makes the agate moist? It does not leave it so; it makes it dry again, and thereafter it never becomes moist. Just like fire, which makes wood dry so that it never becomes moist again—that is, the ash. But what does the star do? It moistens the <term>Salpalla</term> <note>A paracelsian term for a specific mineral or salt-like substance</note>, which will never again become dry, but remains moist. They make

...the rain, which remains moist and never becomes dry; it passes out of the vessel and goes wherever it will, yet it is still moist, still wet. Thus, whatever is dry stands in the heat, and whatever is moist stands in the cold; dryness never becomes moist, and moisture never becomes dry. Just as lime remains lime, glass remains glass, water remains water, wine remains wine, and other such examples.

**In** order that the Element of Fire may be further understood, we will first describe the Sun, which is as follows: All heat is drawn into a <term>Magdalion</term> <note>A Latin term for a globule, mass, or "pill-shaped" body; here referring to the concentrated sphere of the Sun</note> and is rounded; within it is all white <term>Candor</term> <note>Latin: brightness or radiance</note>. Thus, the white radiance and the heat form one *Magdalion*, made from fiery white <term>Sulphur</term>, in a <term>corpus</term> <note>Latin: body</note> of the noblest <term>Mercury</term>, above all other elements, and <term>Coagulated</term> <note>Solidified or thickened</note> by the most subtle <term>spiritum Salis</term> <note>Latin: spirit of Salt; one of the three alchemical primes</note>. In these three Primes <note>The "Three Primes" or Tria Prima are Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt—the fundamental building blocks of matter in Paracelsian alchemy</note> the Sun stands, so dry and hot that no moisture has a place there, but is instead consumed. Just as fire consumes wood, so the Sun consumes moisture. Thus, it should be understood that the daily water of the rain, the <term>Globul</term> <note>The earthly sphere or globe</note>, and everything that comes from the other three elements is consumed and taken away by the Sun, so that the water does not become too much. It is the "Death" of the washing-nature and of the sea, of the Rhine and the Danube, the Nile and the Tiber. For through its heat, they are consumed so that they do not gain the upper hand. For death is in all things, solely so that they do not become too much, but remain in measure. Thus, Man has death, which is invisible; dryness has death, which is water; water has death, which is fire. And it is not that what the fire consumes goes to another place, but it passes away entirely in its form. But the <term>spiritus</term> <note>Latin: spirit</note> remains; the Sun consumes it, and it is the true Death that takes away the other three elements and consumes them entirely—even the human in the earth and the bear in his hole.

<margin>B</margin>
**N**ow, to philosophize further concerning the Sun: it takes its course from <term>Providentia divina</term> <note>Latin: Divine Providence</note>, which knows one thing and all things well—where it should stand and how it should stand. It gives place and position, shape and form, way and path. It has ordered it so that the Sun shall walk its circle around the globe for no other reason than for the "Autumn and Harvest" of the Sun. For in this course lies nothing other than day and night, summer and winter, light and darkness—given to one land and taken from another, and so in alternation. In its course, no wind is created; rather, it moves like a sphere on the earth, from which no wind comes; or like a ship on the sea, which of itself creates no wind. Thus, the Sun also gives no wind. Accordingly, it takes no heat from its movement: for if a sphere were to roll for a hundred years, it would become no hotter of itself. If it is hot, it must have been hot beforehand. Thus, the Sun is a creeping sphere, formed like the <term>Auribus</term> <note>Latin: "ears." This may be a metaphorical reference to the protruding rays or "handles" of the sun's path, or a transcription error for "Orbibus" (spheres)</note>, in the essence of its course and its nature. It diminishes the heat—that is, through its <term>Broch</term> <note>Likely "refraction" or "breaking" as the sun sets or moves</note>—but its shine does not; that remains the same in every way. For that is the reason it is a fixed *Magdalion*, which will remain so from the first point to the last, in one form and manner, regarding its light, <term>Sulphur</term>, <term>Salt</term>, and <term>Mercury</term>. They have but one "Year" in their strife <note>original: "sriter"</note>; that lasts from the first <term>Yliaster</term> to the <term>extremum Yliastrum</term> <note>Latin: the final or end-state of the primordial matter</note>, in which a new world will be; and it is one year, the <term>Annus Solis</term> <note>Latin: Year of the Sun</note>. Likewise, all stars have this fixity, and it is the <term>Annus Ignis</term> <note>Latin: Year of Fire</note> or <term>Annus Stellatus</term> <note>Latin: Starry Year</note>, and it contains the time of the world, until its "daughter" <note>likely referring to the end of the current age or the beginning of a new cycle</note>.

<margin>C</margin>
**B**ut to speak further of other stars, in which the cold stands, as well as the red radiance—the Moon, planets, and others—the cause is this: In the red radiance, there is a different "break" than in the Sun. Specifically, as in the Moon, which does not merely "break" but dies away and passes; there a seed alone remains, from which a new moon grows. And its nature is such that its seed takes its growing power from the Sun. For everything that grows, grows out of the Sun through its heat—that which is <term>Elemental</term>—and without it, nothing grows. Since the <term>Fabricator</term> <note>Latin: the Maker or Creator</note> created the Moon to pass away, to wax and to wane, He granted a following to Nature and ordained that the Moon, as a seed, unites with the Sun, and from that the growing power arises. Then, when it grows to its highest power and size, it wanes again. For the reason that whatever is to grow must also wane. And just as a human wanes through illness and passes away, so the waning of the moon is its "illness unto death," and it passes, leaving only an eternal seed. It is the <term>Firmamental Phoenix</term> <note>A reference to the mythical bird that dies and is reborn from its own ashes; here used to explain the Moon's cycle</note>, from which a new one always springs. So it is with other stars as well. And they are composed of the Redness of <term>Sulphur</term>, <term>Mercury</term>, and <term>Salt</term>, and it is a "Coldness" of Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt. The other stars are also from these three Primes, but placed into many parts. For the reason that the cold of the Element of Fire is divided into many thousands of <term>gradus</term> <note>Latin: degrees</note> and into many essences and natures. Thus, out of certain stars, winds grow over the entire globe; out of others, rain, snow, and the like. Therefore, they are of many kinds, so that many types of nature and power proceed from them onto the earth, which otherwise could not occur if it were but one *Magdalion* like the Sun, which has only one essence: heat. But in the stars are many cold natures; for coldness generates far more <term>Egections</term> <note>Outward manifestations or "discharges" of nature</note> than heat. A hot person is healthy; a cold person has many "new essences" within them—one person having more than twenty. Therefore, because coldness is the nature that is the counterpart to the Sun, with so many strange kinds, the Element of Fire was thus divided into many stars, so that each power stands and exists for itself, without the interference of another essence. For from them proceed warm winds, warm rain, other warm storms, <term>Himmelitzen</term> <note>Heat lightning or flashes in the sky</note>, <term>Dracken</term> <note>Literal "dragons"; a historical term for fireballs or meteors</note>, <term>Lancen</term> <note>Literal "lances"; a term for streaks of light or meteor trails</note>, and the like; yet all of this is a cold fire without any burning. But that which is hot...

## CONCERNING THE WINDS.

<margin>A</margin> Likewise, the wind-stars stand in a ring around the <term>Globe</term> <note>The Earth</note>, which continually have their harvest and autumn: and they stand in the circle of the <term>Zedoch</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for the firmamental circle or the path of the stars</note>, and they encompass the Globe, above and below. Just as the firmament moves in a circle around the Globe, and the Globe lies round within it: so the stars stand in the circle of the *Zeboch* <note>Likely a variant spelling of Zedoch used in the text</note>, and meet the *Zedoch* of the Globe in its center. Then, when the winds blow, they strike out to two sides, downwards and upwards: that is, beneath the <term>Arctic Pole</term>, and the other part toward the <term>Antarctic Pole regions</term>. These wind-stars are the true wind-stars: for the reason that they come to us *annually* <note>original: *annuatim*</note> and have their year, which is the *Year of the Winds* <note>original: *Annus Ventorum*</note>. The other wind-stars, above us and below us, do not follow the year, but blow sometimes here and sometimes not, and also hit only one land, wherever it may be. But the true wind-stars follow their year, always, over and over, across the entire globe, and are without hail, without lightning, without showers—they are celestial and the like: they are solely wind-stars over the whole Globe. There are many of them, surrounding the whole *Zedoch*, like the <term>Galaxa</term> <note>The Milky Way</note>, and the <term>Deneas</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for a specific sidereal force or spirit</note> is toward the *Galaxa*. Regarding these stars of elemental nature, it is to be known that they are all wet, and that is their way. From ancient times they have had four names, which we will now let remain, though not with the ancient interpretation. They are as follows: <term>Boreas</term> <note>The North Wind</note>, which are all those stars lying toward the North <note>original: *Mitnacht*, literally "midnight," a common German term for the North</note> through the whole *Zedoch*: and it is reckoned dry and cold, but it is not dry: rather it is cold and *congealed* <note>Frozen solid</note>, that is, its <term>Nessy</term> <note>Paracelsian term for an elemental, vaporous moisture</note> is congealed, which is why it appears dry. The <term>Zephyrus</term> <note>The West Wind</note> are those stars lying toward the West <note>original: *Occasu*</note>, and they are all moist and cold, but not congealed: therefore *Boreas* is reckoned dry compared to it, because of its congelation.
<margin>B</margin> The other stars in the *Zedoch*, <term>Eurus</term> <note>The East Wind</note> and <term>Auster</term> <note>The South Wind</note>, are entirely cold: but as soon as they depart from their stars, the Sun warms them, through whose *rays* <note>original: *Radios*</note> they must pass, and they are recognized as warm, which, however, they are not by their own nature. *Eurus* is called dry, and is not dry: but the moisture that it has in it is consumed by the Sun, except for that which is within it, which the Sun cannot take from it. *Auster* is called moist, and is moist: for the reason that the Sun does not take as much of its moisture as it does from *Eurus*: that is because of the sea, which gives the Sun enough moisture to consume, so that *Auster* arrives to us in its moisture, upon the lower and upper Globes. But how the wind goes out from the stars is explained by the *reason* <note>original: *Ratio*</note> that just as the Sun gives its heat to the world: so in these stars there is no other nature or property than the wind alone, which is thus *decocted* <note>distilled or "cooked down"</note> from <term>Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt</term> <note>The Three Primes of alchemy</note> and goes out according to its <term>Adech</term> <note>The inner spirit or formative power that directs natural processes</note>. Their wind is daily, every hour, blowing over the whole world, and is gentle: therefore their winds should be recognized when the other wind-stars are explained.

## CONCERNING THE TEMPERATE STARS
### Concerning the Zedoch.

<margin>C</margin> The other wind-stars, as they stand in the firmament, are thus. Every star has within it a coldness that makes wind: for the mother of all wind is coldness alone. But now the coldness is such that some make wind along with rain, some along with snow, some with hail, and the like. Therefore, it is to be known that all the winds that stop and subside do not come from the *Zedoch*, but are gathered here and there from particular stars, as will then be found in their chapters, recounted one after another; and the birth of them all is that through their coldness they give birth in time to an *excretion* <note>original: *Egestion*</note>, of which there are many kinds. But as for wind, it is so that the stars have <term>Emunctoria</term> <note>Organs or passages for the evacuation of waste/vapors</note>, so that what they give birth to within themselves, they may cast out. Thus, when the winds are born, they are cast out, according to what the wind is, to the place where the *emunctorium* looks or goes, and it lasts as long as that same *excrement* <note>original: *Egest*</note> lasts. But the *Zedoch* stars, those same ones go daily into their *excretion*, and they make the wind of the world to temper the heat of the Sun, and to disperse the frost of the cold earth. For they mitigate on both sides, the heat and the cold: and this is the highest *temperament* in summer and in winter. If they were not there, the <term>Chaos</term> <note>The atmospheric space or "air" between heaven and earth</note> would freeze just like water. For water freezes because these *Zedoch* winds do not enter into it, therefore it freezes: but they pass through the *Chaos*, therefore they do not let it freeze. And they exist for no other reason than that they contain the tempering of both seasons in the year, to mitigate all excessive abundance from which harm might come to the earth.

## CONCERNING THE DEW.

Out of all the stars, as far as the heavens encompass within themselves the entire firmament, there is a nature in them all that they sweat daily, at every point and every hour, and it happens thus. The stars draw to themselves the heat of the Sun, just as the fruit of the earth also receives the same: that same Solar heat causes the stars to *dissolve* <note>original: *resoluiren*</note> in their coldness: and it is solely a *dissolution* <note>original: *Resolution*</note>, like a cold stone that sweats, and it takes itself from the vapor that is within themselves, taken from *Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt*. This vapor is in all *elemental bodies* <note>original: *Elementirten Corporibus*</note> of the four elements. For just as a human *clears* <note>original: *Emungirt*</note> <term>phlegma</term> from the nose, with natural...

However, in the winter and during the time of the cold harvest, it freezes and becomes a frost. This is nothing other than the "sweat of the stars" <note>Early modern natural philosophy often viewed the stars as living or quasi-biological entities that produced physical excretions</note> from the entire firmament, which sweats downward in this way: just as boiling water sends steam up toward heaven and leaves its residue above, so the stars cast their moisture downward.

<margin>A</margin>
### CONCERNING MISTS. <note>original: *DE NEBVLIS*</note>

Mist is also nothing but this vapor; it differs only in that it is "unripe" <note>original: *nicht zeittig*; meaning it has not fully matured into dew</note>, having been cast out from certain stars. When it comes upon the earth like the frost, it resists both the earth and the water and becomes like smoke. This happens because it cannot fully resolve itself into dew or frost. Therefore, one part falls as dew, while the other part becomes mist, for it is an incomplete dew that is not yet mature. Sometimes it draws toward the ground and vanishes if it is subtle; but if it is still coarse and unprepared, it rises back into its own region where it is consumed by the sun. This remains the case unless a rain-cloud is mixed and united with it; then it becomes rain, and such rains are more subtle than other rains. They fall often and bring much rainy weather. This occurs because those stars are watery by nature, and therefore they cannot transition into dew, but only into such mist. Where they bring fair weather, the reason is that the mist is subtly prepared and vanishes upon the <term>Globe</term> <note>The Earth</note>.

<margin>B</margin>
# THIRD TREATISE. <note>original: *TRACTATVS TERTIVS*</note>
## CONCERNING STORMS. <note>original: *DE TEMPESTATIBVS*</note>
### Prologue on the stars of storms, and how the primary matter for creating storms exists within them.
### *The Origin of Storms.*

Just as it has been said that there are certain stars that produce wind, so there are other stars that produce tempests, as contained in the first treatise regarding the "Conjunctions and Nature of the Stars." But how and in what way this happens is as follows. Initially, when the storm-stars begin to <term>emungire</term> <note>From the Latin *emungere*, "to wipe the nose"; here meaning to expel or cleanse themselves of waste matter</note>, it happens that the <term>Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt</term> <note>The *Tria Prima*, or three primary alchemical principles believed to compose all matter</note> within them cleanse themselves of the abundance that does not belong in the star through their <term>Adech</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for the "inner agent" or formative power within a celestial body</note>. This occurs because every star has a specific nature within itself, and they give off fruit according to the nature of the Element of Fire.

### I.
### CONCERNING CLOUDS. <note>original: *DE NVBIBVS*</note>

In the same manner that there are stars from which the winds come, there are also stars from which the clouds and rain come, and in this way: When the rain-stars rise at their appointed times in their circle above the Globe, they give off their <term>Egest</term> <note>Excretion or outflowing waste matter</note> according to their kind. Thus, the Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt within the star are of a watery nature; they have nothing else <margin>C</margin> in them but this watery nature for which they were ordained. Now, when this <term>Egest</term> begins, it first becomes a smoke that goes out from the stars down to the "third region" <note>The middle layer of the atmosphere in ancient and medieval meteorology</note>, where it becomes visible. This smoke is then a cloud, which is large or small depending on whether there are many stars or much is being cast out by them. From this, it follows that there are many colors in the clouds—white, gray, and many others—because the Sulfur and Salt, together with the <term>Liquor of Mercury</term> <note>The fluidic or metallic essence of the alchemical principle of Mercury</note>, come together from various stars and mingle with one another. It is then their nature to stand still; but because of their lightness and because they are nimble, the wind that reaches them moves them to follow its path. It is also true that more clouds come from certain places than others, because there are more "cloud-stars" in those places than in other ends. Namely, by the <term>Zephyrus</term> <note>The West Wind</note> and <term>Auster</term> <note>The South Wind</note> are the most stars of wet clouds, and by <term>Boreas</term> <note>The North Wind</note> and <term>Eurus</term> <note>The East Wind</note> are the dry clouds. Also, the warm cloud-stars are by Eurus and Auster, and the cold ones by Zephyrus and Boreas. This is not the fault of the winds or the sea, but rather that those same stars have their course in that specific place. And when they cast out their <term>Egest</term> and it becomes a cloud, the winds then drive them over the sea onto the Globe. Therefore, those same winds, which stand by the stars, are called "dry" or "wet" according to the stars, yet it is not the nature of the wind itself.
Similarly, there are also many stars that stand directly over the Globe and create clouds; therefore, a cloud often arises over a specific land and does not come from across the sea, but from the very land where the cloud stands.

<margin>A</margin> And they are also sometimes driven over the globe into other lands. Such clouds are many and of various kinds; yet they are only dry clouds, of which we speak here. ## II.
### On Rain.

<margin>B</margin> Toward the West and the South <note>original: "Zephyro vnd Austro"</note> are the rain-stars; there are few toward the North and the East <note>original: "Septentrione vnd Euro"</note>, yet some are there too. They consist powerfully of Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt <note>The three primary alchemical principles of all matter</note>. When they cleanse themselves <note>original: "Emungieren"; a term for clearing out waste, like blowing one's nose</note>, their waste goes out, which is prepared by the *Adech* <note>In Paracelsian philosophy, a creative or formative power that directs nature</note> to be dissolved, and is ordained to become rain. This waste is initially a vapor, much like smoke, which is why at first it is a mass of clouds. This <margin>fol. 163. South:</margin> cloud creates its own wind, which goes out through its vents <note>original: "Emunctoriis"; anatomical term for excretory organs</note>, which commonly lead toward the East or the North; therefore, the South and West winds are recognized as the wet winds and rainy weather, yet they are not the weather itself, but rather its neighbors. At first, one cloud is like any other, full of Salt with a little Sulfur and a little Mercury. It travels thus in its region, creating rain before the wind for some time or hours. Because Salt is of a dissolving nature, the Salt begins to resolve itself in the air, outside of its star, and becomes water. Whatever is thus dissolved falls down upon the globe drop by drop. For just as it falls, it dissolves from the cloud one after another, much or little. Therefore, small drops often fall, and sometimes large ones, according to the strength of the dissolution; sometimes for a long time, depending on how many clouds there are. Sometimes there is a cloudburst, which comes from the dissolution happening too quickly, becoming unified and falling all at once. Thus the *Adech* ordains that it be dissolved into drops, distilling down from the firmament <note>original: "Marmel"; likely a reference to the crystalline or marble-like spheres of heaven</note> drop by drop. So subtle is the way of nature; no rain-cloud gives any water unless the dissolution is first within it, which happens so gradually that only one drop after another falls from the matter. Such rains last as long as the stars are there producing waste. Those who rightly recognize the nature and property of these stars, and the power of their Salt, know the day and hour of their coming and going, their beginning and end, whether much or little, with a greater understanding than those who call themselves astronomers.

## III.
### ON SNOW.
<note>original: "DE NIVE"</note>

<margin>C</margin> The snow-stars stand above us, and for the most part they come out of the *Linea Lactea*, which you call the Galaxy <note>original: "Galaxa"</note>. For in the Galaxy is the greatest part of the snow-stars; these have their cleansing in the winter, for the reason that their excretion occurs through the cold. Just as the effect of rain is caused by the warmth of the air, so conversely the snow-smoke is caused by the cold of the upper air. However, many snow-stars cleanse themselves in the summer: if they have cold winds, they drive the stars into this effect; just as some rain-stars do in winter during warm breezes, where the waste is brought forth before its time. Initially, when the snow-stars go out, it becomes a white foam and spreads out widely, falling downward toward the sphere, where it lies until it is ready. It is a white Sulfur, which coagulates through its Salt and Mercury—which is what snow is—and thus falls down piece by piece upon the earth. For just as there is dissolution in rain, so there is coagulation in snow. And it is not that snow comes from the rain-stars; rather, it has its own stars which are of the nature of snow. For no rain congeals in its own regions. But the snow-stars cannot always keep their waste so that it remains congealed; the reason being that often in winter or at other times, such snow-clouds are dissolved by warmth and turn to rain. Sometimes a rain-cloud comes beneath it and breaks the snow-cloud in its operation, dissolving it with itself, or snow and rain fall together. If the cold in their regions does not allow the snow to dissolve, the rain falls as is its nature, and the snow falls as is the will of its *Adech*.

## IV.
### On Graupel.
<note>original: "Risslen"; refers to sleet, small hail, or soft hail pellets</note>

<margin>D</margin> The origin of graupel comes from the snow-stars in this way: If in summer, or at such times when there is warmth, the snow-stars are first driven out by cold into a snow, and if that same snow cannot become perfect in its effect—meaning it goes into dissolution too early because of the warmth of the *Chaos* <note>The atmosphere or "great void" between heaven and earth</note>—then a rain would come of it. But if the North Wind <note>original: "Boreas"</note> enters in and catches it, he coagulates it and makes grains of it, as large as the snow-drops should have been. And when they are thus coagulated, they fall down. Therefore, it is important to know that no graupel comes from any rain-star, for they do not take on coagulation in their regions; they must be snow-stars alone.

### V.
## On Thundering.

(Thunder is born within its own stars, which consist of Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt, situated along that path. These stars, when they cast out their waste product <note>original: "Egest"; refers to the "excrement" or byproduct of a celestial body's process</note>, create a powerful mixture of these Three Primes <note>Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt—the foundational elements of all matter in this worldview</note>.)

Thunder originates in this way: When the "thunder-stars" cast out their waste, it consists of a material Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury. This material is thrown out into its own region. It then dissolves; first, the Sulfur attacks the Mercury and the Salt, attempting to form a mixture and become a single thing. However, the Salt and Mercury cannot tolerate the material Sulfur-like nature acting upon them. For Sulfur is at its hottest, and the Salt is saltpeter <note>nitre</note>; indeed, the best saltpeter is formed from the rain they produce. Since these Three Primes must come together and unite, it does not happen without a "wonder-work" <note>a miraculous or extraordinary natural event</note>. This conjunction of the Three Primes comes from a single star, exiting without being united; it is the task of the <term>Adech</term> <note>a formative, creative power in nature that directs the growth and movement of elements</note> to unite them within the clouds. When the Adech performs this, it ignites the Sulfur, and the Mercury and saltpeter along with it, with a "cold fire," as is the nature of the stars in this generation. And as the Sulfur takes in the saltpeter and Mercury, a sphere is compacted together. If the saltpeter in this sphere is coarse and "unripe," it will not remain within the Sulfur, and it shatters the sphere apart. This shattering makes a "crack" or "bang" that echoes through the clouds for many miles, as if the sound were traveling continuously through its own substance. This is nothing other than the path of the thunder; wherever the thunder goes, that is where the saltpeter has broken the limit. Many such spheres <margin>B</margin> may be produced by a single star, all of which shatter one after another in rapid succession as they are cast out from the star, depending on whether there are many or few of them. And as soon as this thunder has occurred, a wind follows, either before or after. This is because the conjunction of these three opposing Primes, before it occurs, creates a great <term>impetus</term> <note>a driving force or violent surge</note> of wind, which only arrives during the conjunction when they press severely against one another. Then the saltpeter resolves itself, dissolving the Mercury and Sulfur with it, and they turn into rain. These are rapid rains, because a rapid resolution of the saltpeter occurs there.

### VI.
## On the Bolt.
<note>The "Strahl" refers to a lightning strike or "thunderbolt," often thought of as a physical object or stone falling from the sky.</note>

However, if there were a "bolt-star"—that is, a fiery Sulfur—then that star casts out its fiery waste already coagulated within the star, and it emerges coagulated into its region. But the coldness of the rushing winds and of the <term>Chaos</term> <note>the atmosphere or the space between heaven and earth</note> is antagonistic to it and resists this waste. It follows that these Three Primes shatter themselves due to the cold and moisture of the outer clouds, which also run along from their own stars. For wherever a bolt is hatched, a rain-cloud always precedes it, and within that cloud lies this matter. When this rain-cloud wishes to dissolve into rain, it moistens this matter, which is fiery. And as soon as the sulfur <note>original: "(SS.)"; likely shorthand for "Sulphur" or "Spiritus"</note> feels the moisture, it shatters apart. Then, the flash first descends to the earth from the Sulfur. It strikes far in a circle around itself—above, below, a whole ring around its center. As soon as the flash becomes wet, it is extinguished. In that extinguishing, the sphere shatters, and it "claps" a thunder, as described above. Many of these often come one after another, depending on whether the stars cast out many or few. <margin>C</margin> It is also to be known that the Mercury is often so hardened and compacted with the Sulfur and Salt that it does not shatter, but remains entirely as one mass. It is fiery and powerful in its operation, and through the moisture of the clouds—if even a single drop touches this fire of the Three Primes—it strikes entirely down to the earth, or out into the heavens, depending on whether the moisture touched it from below or above. If it hits the top, it strikes downward; if it hits the side, it strikes to that side, or the other side; as it is struck in the circle, it follows that line down. It strikes into the earth with such an impetus that it shatters walls, snaps trees, splits rocks in two, and often, if it hits a pond, it blasts all the water out of the place. It strikes horses and men dead, and penetrates several hundred fathoms into the earth. There is no faster action in the heavens. This is the great power of Mercury, which can tolerate fire much less than saltpeter can, and strikes a thousand times more fiercely than saltpeter. It is simply a coagulation of these Three Primes, struck down by the moisture of the clouds while in a state of powerful fire.

### VII.
## Cold Bolt, Sleet.

In the same way, cold bolts and sleet <note>original: "Schawer"; can refer to heavy showers, hail, or sleet</note> are formed, except they do not stand in fire. The cause is that the rain extinguishes them and takes away the fire. Such a cold bolt also strikes down like the fiery one, for Mercury cannot tolerate moisture either. When it reaches the earth, it is often found, and it is a "Berylline matter" <note>a clear, glassy, or crystalline substance</note>, because the liquor of Mercury and Saltpeter is clear, with a white or gray sulfur, sometimes black,

For such stars that cast out this matter create great clouds, great winds, and rapid operations with many flashes of lightning. It often happens that many flashes occur before a thunderclap follows, because many masses are coagulated so hard within themselves that they are not broken apart so quickly in that speed. Therefore, as often as a "test" <note>an atmospheric discharge</note> occurs, a celestial flash precedes it.

Many celestial flashes also happen in fair weather. The cause is not the same as with hail and the lightning strike; rather, there is much Sulfur in certain stars, and when it is cast out, it burns away without any harm under a clear sky. These are merely the <term>Egest</term> <note>waste or excrement of the stars</note> of pure Sulfur, occurring more by night than by day. For the sun burns up this sulfur from the stars, which otherwise comes down at night and burns itself out. It is merely a vapor of Sulfur in which there is no heat. Sometimes gentle thundering also comes this way, without harm, from "gentle" stars.

# FOURTH TREATISE.
<note>original Latin: "TRACTATVS QVARTVS."</note>
### i.
## CONCERNING THE RAINBOW.
<note>original Latin: "DE IRIDE."</note>

The Rainbow <note>Iris</note> is a star that stands powerfully alone in Salt—that is, it has its body formed from Salt. It rises with the water-stars, but it gives no water itself; however, it exists within the path and circle of the water-stars. When it wishes to <term>purge</term> itself <note>original: "emungiren"; literally to blow one's nose, used here to mean the shedding of celestial waste</note>, it throws out the spirit of salt without a physical body into the "middle space" <note>the atmosphere</note>. As it lies within that space, it stretches itself out into a circle with many colors, consisting of only one element, which is Fire. For the colors it possesses come from the spirit of salt, which produces brown, pale yellow, green, etc. This is not a gathering of the four elements, as some influential people claim; rather, such is the nature of the Rainbow. Just as every other star gives its "impression" <note>influence or manifestation</note> according to its creation, so this Rainbow gives the Celestial Arch out of its own power, without any other elements. They often come during fair weather and bring no rain; the reason is that this Rainbow has its own path independent of the water-stars. Sometimes they appear with rainy weather, for some move along with the water-stars, appearing early or late in the day according to their course, and just as well at night—though the colors cannot be recognized then due to the shadow of the earth and the darkness.

<margin>C</margin>The reason they appear in summer is that the Rainbow-star cannot reach "ripeness" in winter time, but only through the sun, just as thunder is also brought to ripeness. Therefore, they come and rise in their proper seasons. Regarding those that appear in winter: the cause is that a Celestial Arch was born in the summer but was not cast out, and thus remained beyond its time, just as some thunder and lightning and the like do. Its form and its divided colors are all from the innate nature of its *Adech* which lies within the Rainbow-star. Therefore, concerning what the other ancient philosophers and the moderns hold regarding the Rainbow, it should be regarded as a "wiped-away" <note>erroneous or superficial</note> nature; their assertions and theories have never been proven by any true philosophy.

### ii.
## THE SPEAR.
<note>original Latin: "LANCEA." Refers to meteor-like streaks or "fire-spears" in the sky.</note>

The origin of Spears comes from the sulfur-stars. When the star wishes to purge itself, it throws off its <term>putrefaction</term> <note>decay or waste matter</note>, which cannot remain within it. For all stars are constant and remain; but whatever is born out of them that is destined for decay is cast out from them. Thus the sulfur-star, from which the Spear is born, is a sulfurous body, and it generates within itself a shining thing, similar to itself in color; for it always resembles that from which it comes, while it is still within that star's heat. Therefore, when the star casts this out, it cannot be seen by day, only by night. It is cast out as a lump in one piece, but in falling, it stretches out so that it resembles a spear; sometimes it is called a "spear," sometimes a "star-bolt." For it has a material substance and is a physical thing. As soon as it hits the earth, it sits still like a jelly, or spawn, or like a <term>mucilage</term> <note>likely referring to "star jelly" or Nostoc, a gelatinous substance traditionally thought to fall from the stars</note>. It is then consumed by the sun, out of which a "fixed" and harder sulfur grows...

### III.
### CONCERNING FLYING
### DRAGONS.
<note>original Latin: "DE DRACONIBVS VOLAN- tibus." Here, "dragons" refers to meteors or fireballs.</note>

The origin of natural dragons comes from the "Body of Sulfur," but mixed with much <term>Mercury</term> and <term>Salt</term> <note>the "Three Primes" of Paracelsian alchemy: Sulfur (soul/fire), Mercury (spirit/fluidity), and Salt (body/solidity)</note>. They are also formed within the "sulfur-stars," but they differ from the "Lances" <note>streaks of light mentioned on the previous page</note> in that, as soon as they emerge from the star, they remain in the same size and shape as when they were thrust out, compacted together. However, they are so hot within themselves, due to the Sulfur, that the Mercury and Salt cannot remain still; instead, they tremble in their flight as if they were a living animal moving itself. This is caused by the "wildness" <note>reactive energy</note> found in the saltpeter, the Mercury, and the Sulfur when heat is present. It shoots out sideways because the <term>Emunctorium</term> <note>original: "Emunctorium," a biological term for an excretory organ or vent</note> of its star faces sideways. It then sights the <term>level surface of the earth</term> <note>original: "planitiem der Erden"</note> and so shoots straight out, horizontally, sometimes for thirty or forty miles, more or less. And when it falls down, it is nothing but a crust or burnt foam, and it lies on the surface of the earth like <term>Usnea</term> <note>a type of lichen or moss</note> on an oak tree. This foam will silver any copper it touches, due to the nature of the Mercury contained in these "dragons." And if it is thrown into a fire, it bursts like a gun and gives a "piping" <note>sharp or whistling</note> crack.

### IV.
### Concerning Stationary Projectiles.

It also often happens that a discharge <note>original: "Egest," meaning excrement or waste</note> goes out from certain stars just like the star itself, but remains in the heights of the middle region <note>the atmosphere</note> and does not fall upon the globe, staying aloft instead. This is because many discharges are of a nature that does not sink to the ground but remains high up, just as the upper clouds do. Such discharges can be recognized because they do not fall but hover; they are made of a shining Sulfur that is merely a smoke formed into a body, and thus in its own time is consumed like other clouds. They are also sometimes driven from one place to another by the course of the wind and the star's vent. Many of these stationary "star-shots" are mistaken for new stars, which then vanish over time. Sometimes it happens that such a "star" travels a path every night for a time, and by morning is back where it started to travel again. The reason is that the vent is positioned in the direction it travels; in the first pass, the "star" goes until it is consumed, whether by night or day, and afterwards a new discharge falls out and travels just like the old one. Thus, often for many weeks, a new discharge falls out every night, earlier or later, at the place where that same star stands.

### V.
### CONCERNING LITTLE FROGS, BLOOD,
### & MILK.

<margin>Wind.</margin>
In the same way, there are also certain stars that cast out their waste like spawn <note>original: "laych," like fish or frog eggs</note>, and these fall upon the earth. From this matter grow worms, frogs, toads, and many kinds of similar beetles. This discharge is a foul Sulfur and Mercury, and a hot "spirit of salt"; its <term>Adech</term> <note>the internal formative power or "unseen architect"</note> is the ruler of such <term>putrefaction</term> <note>the process of decay that Paracelsus believed generated life</note> from which such animals grow. For all kinds of species that are on earth have a corresponding star in heaven; even "changelings" <note>original: "Wechselbalg," referring to hybrids or abnormal births</note> are all born from the stars. For there are two kinds of snakes: the true snakes, which are created to be snakes, and "star-snakes." The same applies to all other animals. When such discharges go out, many wonderful effects result. Some are like blood—this is a red, dissolved Sulfur—and when it is <term>coagulated</term> <note>solidified</note> like * (wine), it becomes a Sulfur that burns. Sometimes a white Sulfur falls, like milk, and through its congelation it becomes "fixed" <note>stable</note> and does not burn. Other colors often appear as well. Sometimes it falls as a thick water, like white oil, with a stench; this also yields a fixed Sulfur. Regarding those that are the true discharges of putrefaction: they sometimes form their animals within the stars and fall down as such; sometimes they form in the regions of the "Middle Interstice" <note>the atmosphere</note>; and sometimes only upon the globe, depending on their nature. Many and various such putrefactions are found on earth, all of which are born from the <term>dung of the stars</term> <note>original: "Stercus der Sternen"</note>, which stars are otherwise of such a nature.

# FIFTH TREATISE.
## Concerning Metals from the Heavens, Minerals, and Stones.

---

<margin>A</margin>
### I.
### CONCERNING METALS.

The metals that come down from above take their origin from the seven planets. Of these seven planets there are many: just as there are many Suns, many Moons, many Marses, many Mercuries, many Jupiters, many Saturns, etc. And they are called "seven" because they produce seven types of metals; each type is categorized under one planet. And these are not the ones that astronomers name—for they are in error, practicing according to their own theories—so that they assign them to the metals in a way that does not harmonize at all with the reality of things. From these seven types of planets come the seven metals, and they are formed of the <term>Three Primes</term> <note>Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury—the basic building blocks of matter in Paracelsian alchemy</note> just as in the element of Water. The only difference is that these celestial "Three Primes" are volatile and not fixed in their species. Therefore, whatever such metals are found, they do not withstand the assays <note>tests for purity and stability</note> of the lower, earthly metals. Conversely, the earthly metals do not withstand the assays of the celestial ones; nor do they have the same malleability, flow, or hardness. Even their color gradients are not the same, but differ in every distinction from one another. Thus, such a volatile nature and power exists in the element of Fire that within the seven types of stars, there is all metallic action and matter; and in the same way, it falls down from them upon the earth, like rain and other such discharges. Many such metals lie beneath their stars: some in Asia, fewer in Africa, and far fewer in Europe. For those specific stars do not touch our soil, and therefore that material does not reach us.

<margin>B</margin>
However, all grains—whatever native metals exist among the seven that are rough on the outside—come from the stars and not from the element of Water. Among all metals that are coagulated without fire and formed in a round shape, like the shape of peas, all of them (whatever metal they may be) have come down from the seven stars, whether they lie upon the surface or not. For the earth covers them, as do the floods. And where they are found, one finds no "vein" or "root" <note>the underground source typical of mined metals</note>, but rather they are kidney-shaped. For their origin comes from the stars, and they are all "native" <note>pure metal found in nature, not needing to be smelted from ore</note>. This is because in the element of Fire there is no coarseness to mix in; therefore, the star purges it and coagulates it pure and whole. They exist in their mixture just as metals do in the element of Water—with <term>Sulfur</term>, <term>Salt</term>, and <term>Mercury</term>—except that the fiery metals do not have the aqueous "fixation" <note>stability and permanence</note> in them, and the aqueous metals do not have the "fixation" of the firmament.

<margin>C</margin>
### II.

Now, when the Three Primes in the "metallic star" have completed their effect—such as when the composition in the Star of the Sun has mixed the Mercury of the Sun with the Sulfur of the Sun and the Salt of the Sun—then the <term>Adech</term> <note>a Paracelsian term for the internal formative power or "unseen sculptor" that shapes matter</note> digests it into a perfect metal and creates the form of its gift. Then the star casts it out, hot and molten as if from a smelting furnace, and in falling it shatters and coagulates in the cold, falling as globules. Likewise, the Star of the Moon makes a composition from the Mercury of the Moon, the Salt of the Moon, and the Sulfur of the Moon; and when this has reached its effect, it casts it out just like the Sun. So also do Saturn, Mars, Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter. And it is to be noted that among these seven types of the seven stars, each one alone possesses its own "Three Primes" of a metal; it is not like in the element of Water, where seven metals lie within one <term>Ares</term> <note>the "primeval separator" or source of material growth</note>. Therefore, the names of the seven metals apply to the seven metals that fall from the stars, and not to those of the earth. In the same way, many "liquors" <note>liquid discharges</note> fall down from the stars that are not coagulated. When the earth is moistened by them, a luster arises, similar to <term>Cachymia</term> <note>an immature or "half-grown" metallic ore</note>, Talc, or sometimes <term>Marcasite</term> <note>a shiny mineral, often iron pyrites</note>, and yet it is not quite perfect and not identical to them. Thus it is to be noted that the upper metals are far above the lower ones in quality, purity, and nature—more so than the lower ones—and are in all things more worthy of praise.

### III.
### CONCERNING STONES FROM THE HEAVENS.
<note>original Latin: "DE LAPIDIBVS E SVPERNIS."</note>

In the same manner, there are also other stars that cast out gems and garnets and other forms of stones from themselves. For the Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt are powerful in the element of Fire regarding the birth of gems. There are many stars that consist of Rubinic Sulfur, many of Sapphiric Salt, many of Emeraldine Mercury. For there are stars that contain the primary copper-elements of <term>Vitriol</term> <note>a sulfate mineral</note>, some of <term>Alum</term>, some of Salt. Therefore, various rains of this kind appear when they are prepared and opened. From such stars come the blue Sapphires, for there the Salt is the "body," and it coagulates entirely with the clear spirit of Sulfur and spirit of Mercury. In the Emerald, Mercury is the "body," and it has a copper-like nature in it, but not the copper "body"; therefore, it does not have the metallic body of copper, but it has the color of copper. For in this way, all colors of gems that come from the element of Fire are found; according to the nature and essence of the Three Primes, the colors remain unified as in metals. For instance, in copper there is only Red; but those same Three Primes, when they do not have the metallic "body," become green. Likewise with silver: when the metallic "body" is not present, it becomes Blue.

<margin>A</margin> ...from Iron, Red / from Lead, Red / from Jove <note>original: "Ioue"; referring to Jupiter and its corresponding metal, Tin</note>, Yellow-White / from Gold, Brown / from Mercury, Yellow. 
Similarly, when Salt alone predominates, it produces many colors, as seen in certain stones: 
Brown, Blue, and those both well and poorly colored. Conversely, whatever comes 
from Mercury alone appears in many colors: Yellow, Red, and others; from Sulfur: White, Red, Yellow, Black, and 
Gray. Such stones are the least common; only those of a metallic nature are the most noble. Thus 
the <term>Emerald</term> <note>original: "Smaragdus"</note> is a copper-stone, the <term>Carbuncle</term> <note>a glowing red gemstone</note> or <term>Jasper</term> <note>original: "Iaspis"</note> is a gold-stone, the <term>Ruby</term> <note>original: "Rubinus"</note> and <term>Chalcedony</term> <note>original: "Calcedon"</note> are 
iron-stones, the Blue <term>Sapphire</term> <note>original: "Saphyr"</note> is a silver-stone, the White <term>Sapphire</term> is a stone of Jove <note>Tin</note>, and the <term>Hyacinth</term> <note>original: "Hyacinthus"; likely Zircon</note> is a Mercury-
stone. Now, just as these stones are born in their stars that stand beside the planets, so 
they are cast out, just as the metals are cast out, and thus they are found upon the heights of the Earth 
in many forms and ways, according to how they were born.

### IV: CONCERNING CRYSTALS AND BERYLS.

But concerning <term>Crystals</term> and <term>Beryls</term>, and also <term>Citrines</term>, it is to be known that they are born from 
the <term>Snow-stars</term> <note>original: "Schneesternen"</note>, from which the snow comes, and in that manner. In Snow-stars there is 
such a power of <term>Congelation</term> <note>the process of thickening or freezing into a solid</note> that they are of a twofold nature: that is, they sometimes contain snow and 
freezing within them, and they are double stars. Where there is such a star, which possesses a power of 
congelation alongside its nature as a snow-star, it easily produces a Crystal, Citrine, or Beryl. 
The reason is that when the snow falls and its coldness accompanies it, and it finds a place on the globe where 
Boreas <note>the North Wind</note> predominates and the sun or summer-like nature does not rule strongly, it 
coagulates the water that travels with the snow into a stone. If it seizes and releases that same water along the way while 
the snow is falling—because of the great cold within it—little stones are formed from it before it 
<margin>B</margin> reaches the globe; there, little grains are found, large and small, according to how it seized the snow 
during the snowfall. But if this does not happen so quickly, and it reaches the ground, then the 
cold drives all the water that lies in the snow (and is not itself snow) together into a center toward the 
bottom of the earth. And as soon as it brings them together, it coagulates them into an ice; but it does 
not melt again like other frost, for the reason that it has become snow-water, which does not 
resolve itself back <note>into liquid</note>. Other waters that freeze there—even if they were snow-water—would melt 
along with the snow; but this should not happen in that place. Instead, the water shall be 
drawn out of the snow, and the snow remains. This occurs solely through the snow-stars, in which the 
power of congelation also resides, so that when they come to a place on Earth where the snow remains 
without melting, they continue until the end of their <term>Intention</term> <note>original: "Intens"; the active period of their influence</note> and operation. In such snow, the stones—
such as Crystals, etc.—are found both clear and cloudy, according to how the <term>Mercury</term> and <term>Salt</term> 
have clarified and purified themselves and exist in their own right. Such Crystals, Beryls, 
and Citrines are also often found in places and regions where there are no snow-fields; the reason for this is 
that they were coagulated in the upper regions and fell down already coagulated. They are nothing but 
congealed snow-water; it takes its form and edges and shape according to whether the Salt within it is subtle 
or coarse.

### PROLOGUE TO THE SIXTH TREATISE.
## Concerning the Impressions of FATE.

<margin>C</margin> i.
Now that we have spoken of the element of Fire, how all its operations come about and 
what they produce, there follows after this another operation, which in some parts is 
similar to and resembles those same elemental operations, and in some parts 
comes from them. Although they are not of the element's nature, but are instead <term>Forewarnings</term> <note>original: "Præsagia"</note>, 
we wish to show them here so that the influence and the stars may be better 
recognized, and so that the stars, about which we have philosophized, may in no way work within us. 
The stars, however, that work within us are those of which we speak, and we call them **FATE** <note>original: "FATVM"</note>, 
according to the philosophers, and not as some others interpret Fate. However, so that Fate may be well recognized, 
it is thus: every human being has a spirit that dwells outside of him and 
sets its throne in the upper stars. 
This same spirit employs the whims of its master; it is the one who shows the 
forewarnings to him and follows after them, for they remain after these. These spirits are called **FATE**.

ii.
So that Astronomy may also be recognized, note this: what it indicates concerning the natural 
action of the weather from the nature and course of the stars may well be true, provided they 
rightly recognize them and experience their outcome, origin, nature, and essence. But to 
practice and give forewarnings otherwise from this, the good people will hardly be spared by Fate. 
For it is so: there is a Fate in the Ascendant <note>the zodiac sign rising on the horizon</note> that indicates what shall be, 
and not the star itself. But Fate plays therein with the good men who 
imagine themselves to be powerful in the might of the stars. For example: they want to know the 
birth of children and the future of their lives;

It also introduces the concept of Fate (Fatum) as an external spirit dwelling in the stars that communicates omens to humans.</summary>
