# BOOK IV OF PHILOSOPHY
<note>original: "PHILOSOPHIÆ LIBER IV."</note>

### CHAPTER VI.
## Sulfur.

<margin>A</margin>
Accordingly, the nature of **Sulfur** emerges exactly as it is in itself, and it looks most like its own physical "body," just as Antimony resembles its Mercury. It also retains the nature and essence of sulfur within it. It occasionally mixes among the minerals—much like the "plants" <note>the author often compares minerals to plants growing in the earth</note> mentioned before—because it is somewhat similar to them. For this reason, a Sulfur is often found to be "gold-like" <note>likely referring to iron pyrites or "fool's gold"</note>, or within a **pyrite** <note>original: "Khiß" (Kies)</note>, or something similar, because of the mixing within the **Trivial Lines** <note>The "Trivial Lines" (Trivial Linien) refer to the predetermined paths or "veins" in nature along which substances are directed to grow and develop</note>. This often happens with Antimony as well.

### CHAPTER VII.
## Entali.
<note>Entali refers to a specific alchemical preparation of salt, or possibly fossilized dentalium shells used as a source of mineral salt</note>

Likewise, **Entali** is nothing other than Salt itself, being most similar to its "First Matter." And just as Antimony takes its body from Mercury, and Sulfur from Sulfur, so does Entali take its body from Salt. But in no way does it unite with metals; this is because Salt seeks no further purification beyond remaining in its own matter. This Entali is well-colored and "shot through" by the power of the Salt, which is ordained to be formed in this way. It lies in the **Yliadum** <note>The primordial "chaos" or raw material of the world from which all things are born</note> like a mineral, similar to a "fixed" saltpeter that is stable and enduring in water, and it retains the matter and essence of Salt within it.

### CHAPTER VIII.
## Yellow Amber.
<note>original: "Carabe Citrinum"</note>

<margin>B</margin>
**Yellow Amber** takes its origin after the coarse, hard types mentioned before have come from the Resinous matter. From this, the **Archeus** <note>the internal "master chemist" of nature that directs growth</note> draws out the subtle nature from among the "Three Firsts" <note>The Tria Prima: Sulfur (the soul/combustibility), Mercury (the spirit/fluidity), and Salt (the body/solidity)</note>: the body from Sulfur, the **coagulation** <note>the process of hardening</note> from Salt, and the **compaction** <note>the structural density</note> and **Resin of Mercury**. It is pure and clear because it contains only the clarity of these three first principles. Thus, it emerges into the Yliadum and hardens; from this, **Yellow Amber** <note>original: "Agtstein"</note> is formed. Although it may be mixed and sometimes appears more white, this is because the "whiteness of Sulfur" runs through it, and thus two or three colors mix together, producing "flowers" <note>mineral patterns or crystalline growths</note> according to the nature of their stems; in this way, they harden together. Whatever comes from the "Amber-flowering" is a good Amber, for it should not lose its "flowers." However, where it loses its flowers, it has become too much like a stone. For every stone that does not have these flowers was hardened too early, before it reached maturity. That substance is not true Amber, but rather its "flowers" well-scattered. For it is a Resin that flows from the nature of its **diaphanous sulfur** <note>transparent or light-passing sulfur</note>; it is a stone when cold due to the power of the composition of Mercury and Salt.

### CHAPTER IX.
## Black Amber.
<note>original: "Carabe Nigrum"; likely referring to Jet or a similar black mineral resin</note>

**Black Amber** is a "black sulfur," but otherwise identical to the Yellow in its generation. However, it possesses a "harder spirit" than the Yellow, so that it produces a great deal of **shale** <note>original: "Schiffer"</note> where it lies. This is because there is much within it that cannot become Amber and instead becomes stonework. It has more of a stony nature than any other "Resinous Fruit." For this reason, it often turns itself entirely into stones, which is to say it departs from its true nature and makes itself into a stone, so that it loses its ability to flow in the fire 

<margin>C</margin>
and all such qualities, becoming just like a piece of shale. It also frequently attaches itself to stony **liquors** <note>mineral-rich fluids</note> and hardens with them; then many black grains are found, like garnets. This is because it contains the stony matter in all three first principles and lies embedded within it. All black stonework of a coarse type is of the nature of Black Amber and originates here, but it breaks apart through the mixing of other matters, whereby it "over-stones" itself out of its own true nature.

### CHAPTER X.
## Corals.

**Corals** take their origin from the three Resinous principles, such that a redness and a white "fixed" nature remain from the Sulfur. The Archeus separates these out like a seed—that is, in the form of little grains—and casts them into the Yliadum. This occurs most often in the sea, because its Trivial Lines originally fell into the sea; it grows in such places. However, if it remains elsewhere in the "Globe" <note>the earth</note>, it withers and nothing comes of it. But when it enters the sea, it begins to grow in that Yliadum, and from the little grain, a tree grows, just as from a seed. As it grows and ages, it hardens through its own "salt-spirit" and the passing years. This happens by its own power within its allotted time. It takes the nature of its essence from the Archeus of the **Element of Water** <note>original: "Elements Aquæ"</note>, which has its own specific "growth" in all fruits. Sometimes this allows silver to grow wonderfully, or gold in strange forms. In this way, Nature plays in her mastery, rejoicing in her Master and her power. Just as **Plumosum** <note>likely "Sal Plumosum" or feathered asbestos/alum</note> and others grow, so there is a special growth in Corals from the seed, which from the three first...

# THE BOOK OF PHILIP THEOPHRASTUS
## PARACELSUS
### CONCERNING THE
# GENERATION
## OF MAN.
<note>original: "DE GENERATIONE HOMINIS"</note>

### Preface.

<margin>B</margin>
Now that we are to **philosophize** <term>concerning the Generation of Man</term> <note>original: "de Generatione Hominis"</note>, we wish to take a perfect human being as our model and describe his trials from that starting point. This is the meaning of the following chapter regarding "free seed": just as a man is born from it, so was he also born from his father, and so on backwards to the first. Although it would be proper to first look at the father of all offspring, because that first man was not born—which we cannot conceive—but was rather a creation, we wish to intersperse our **philosophy** of the child's conception with the essence of the "Created One." We shall speak of him as a creation, which requires no further report here. However, certain archetypes also occur to us which move us to philosophize that there was more than one father in the first creation of humanity: such as a specially created father of the <term>One-eyed</term> <note>original: "Monoculorum"</note>, a special one of the <term>Gnomes</term>, and a special one of the Two-footed <note>standard humans</note>. For **Philosophy** does not allow that a Two-footed father should give birth to a <term>Cyclops</term>; rather, one should understand the opposite to be true. For only like clings to its like, and nothing clings to its unlike. Thus, we will leave these arguments to their own work here in this **Philosophy**, and intend to further investigate and clarify the basis of how one is born from another. In doing so, we shall describe the manner in which the conception of children has been ordained and established by God.

<margin>C</margin>
Now we shall take the Two-footed ones as our example for you. And just as the birth of these occurs, so it is with the other "sects" <note>here meaning types or species of beings</note> who are not Two-footed. Although there are many forms among these sects, the forms are divided among us, as is Nature in its internal essence. We will show you the reasons <term>why we propose the example of the Two-footed</term> <note>original: "cur Bipedis exemplum proponimus"</note>. It is not because we belong to such a sect, or because they are better known to us than the others, or because they inhabit the largest part of the world—no, not for any of those reasons. But this is the reason: we consider how CHRIST was born as a Two-footed human. We consider that the other sects are not perfect in their form, but are somewhat flawed. In the Two-footed form, nothing is lacking. This is not to say that those who are <term>One-eyed</term> lack sight, or that the <term>Cyclopes</term> lack the ability to run; rather, they are equal to all other sects in their essence—considering themselves perfect and pleasing to themselves, just as the Two-footed do. Yet a distinction might be found: they were created this way because of their form, and not because of a different kind of soul. And because life and reason do not depart from them any more than from the Two-footed, we allow them to run alongside us toward eternity, and consider their eternal part to have no blemish despite their form. However, as for being a "misgrowth" <note>or "monstrosity"</note> in creation, we shall speak no further. We must consider that just as misgrowths have grown in the mixed course of nature, so too were there such things in the original Creation.

Lest our undertaking be extended too far, we wish to present other indications as an introduction to our purpose. We shall set aside the various lineages and sects of men in whom the Eternal resides (as we have described) despite their different forms. Instead, we shall report that there is something in the water that also possesses the Eternal and is shaped like us, such as <term>Sea-wonders</term> <note>original: "Meerwunder," likely referring to merfolk or sirens</note> or another form such as we have. Because we perceive and recognize that there is a world in the water, this causes us to not want to call our world "the" world, but rather, for certain reasons, the "fourth part of the world." For it cannot be denied that there is also a world in the Earth, likewise in the Air, and in the middle of the Heavens. But so that we do not disrupt the intent of this book with those three other concurrent worlds, we will take no further notice of them here. Instead, we shall take up only the birth and the conception of the children of our own kind, and conclude with that.

<margin>Ꝛ</margin> The conception of this people in the first quarter of the world—the Two-footed—will be our model. After that, we also wish to show the sensitivity of those in the other quarter...

### BOOK.
## CONCERNING THE GENERATION OF MAN.
<note>original: "DE GENERATIONE HOMINIS"</note>

<margin>A</margin>
**S**o free and clear/ without any compulsion/ God has created the seed of man/ so that it lies still and hidden within the human/ so that he is in no way or manner burdened by it/ nor compelled. And understand the seed of man in this way/ from which the other human is born: That it is exactly like a grain-seed in the field/ which is as good as dead/ and still/ without any action. Thus the whole human is a seed/ and in the action of seeding is dead/ and not fruitful/ for so long/ until a joining occurs/ like the field with a seed.

<margin>B</margin>
Thus we say of the generation of humans/ that there is nothing/ that is then a generative power within man. And every human/ be it woman or man/ is without seed/ and has no seed within them. And this is said because/ no grain grows without its seed/ no tree grows without its seed: And that same grain or seed/ from which all plants grow/ are essential within the mothers <note>the "mothers" here refers to the nurturing elements or the source-matrices of nature</note>/ these carry and work within them/ and the seed and the growth are one thing. But in humans, such is not the case: For man has no seed within him/ which is essential to him/ or formed into his nature/ or united with his nature. Otherwise, in all growing things, the seed is united with its mother/ only in sentient things is it not/ these have no union in the seed/ with their mother. As we have previously indicated/ that the generation of all growing things is a communal union of two kinds: As one/ where nature and the seed are in one essence/ and the other not/ but only the essence of nature without the seed: Of which we wish to give a further report/ from non-sentient growths/ what they increase and bear: And also provide an example from the generation of man/ and it is thus.

The man has no seed in him that may give birth to his own kind: Likewise the woman does not either. Therefore the blind, so-called physicians speak wrongly/ who fill large books <term>concerning sperm</term> <note>original: "de Spermate"</note>, for they lie/ that it is sperm/ which they then call sperm. But so that we do not fill and lengthen our chapter with those same blind <term>followers of Paracelsus</term> <note>original: "Paracels-leutten"; Paracelsus often critiques his own students or those who claim his name without understanding his deeper philosophy</note>/ we wish to lead you briefly to the text of our purpose: Whereby you shall finally know/ that there is no sperm at all/ neither in women nor in men. Upon such a foundation we begin our text.

<margin>C</margin>
We complete the described indication thus. God has given to all things/ which do not have a sentient spirit/ that they multiply themselves out of their own innate seed: So that in the seed is the property/ which dwells with their nature/ grows/ goes up and down. As the tree is not without the power of its seed/ but the power/ from which the tree grows/ is always with and in it/ and is not to be separated from it/ nor divided: Thus also in all grass/ grain/ seed/ etc. But such is not in man/ man has only the nature within him of his life/ and what belongs to all the instruments of his life/ for which reason he was created as a man/ and ordained. But the spirit of the seed/ which shall make another human out of him/ that is not and does not grow within him/ it is also given and created/ as in trees and in other growths. Thus man may not rejoice in this/ nor be burdened/ that he has the sperm within him/ but he lives without any sperm. You should understand this from us in this way/ that we open the foundation/ that the essence of the seed and the nature of man are not created together in the human/ but only the essence of nature in life/ and for life/ and nothing of the sperm with him/ etc.

We can think of no greater guidance/ than the great folly of the earthly gods <note>a sarcastic reference to arrogant scholars or authorities</note>/ who cast in an unfathomable argument/ thus/ that as the non-sentient is made/ so also the sentient is constituted: Following this opinion/ in the same way as if man were like a tree/ and the seed grew in him like an herb. Thus they conduct a teaching/ that might more be called a joke than a teaching.

You should also remember/ everything that casts a reflection of its creation/ that same thing is without attached seed/ which the inexperienced physicians call sperm/ though sperm is no seed at all/ nor does it become any seed. Sperm is a cleansing of the kidneys/ in the same way that the snot of the nose/ is the cleansing of the brain/ and the wax of the ears is <term>cholera</term> <note>here referring to a type of "bitter" or "yellow" excretion, not the modern disease</note>. Therefore I wonder/

<meta>This page continues the "Book on the Generation of Man," following the introductory distinction between human seed and the biological processes of other creatures. The author focuses here on the psychological and spiritual origin of human seed, rather than a purely physical one.</meta>

<header>ON THE GENERATION OF MAN. 65</header>

<margin>A</margin> Let it be known that ignorant physicians say—when a discharge <note>original: "Roß"; likely referring here to a morbid or excess fluid flow</note> passes into an <term>excretory duct</term> <note>original: "Emunctorium"; a term for an organ or canal that carries off waste, like a sweat gland or lymph node</note> of the sperm—that it is also sperm, or <term>choler</term> <note>yellow bile</note>, or the "refuse of rumors." But such a duct is merely a channel through which all subtle fluids—those arising from the excess of the whole body—pass out. These do not belong to the seed, but rather to the health of the body.

However, so that we do not stray from our text, take note: that which the physicians call "sperm" is not the true seed, but as mentioned, a cleansing. Following the indication with which we began the text: everything that is recognized as an <term>external object</term> <note>original: "Gegenwurff"; refers to the sensory stimulus or object that the mind perceives and reacts to</note> is something without an innate or attached seed. This exists only in the "perceptive growth" <note>referring to living things with senses</note>. Whether a creature has reason or not, it possesses the quality of its "external object" insofar as it does not belong to the object itself. It is ordained by God that irrational animals understand the external object, and the rational human does the same. You should understand these external objects in this way: God has placed a free will into the seed of the perceptive being. Thus, every perceptive animal, if it so desires, may have the seed or not. He has placed it within the will of perceptive animals, neither compelling nor burdening them as He does with other growths <note>such as plants</note>. And although the will is a rational growth—because man is the most noble—insofar as he is an animal that follows the external object, he lacks reason in that specific moment.

Now, as we have indicated concerning the bearing of children, you should know that we wish to pursue and delve deeper into our primary purpose, letting all other animals go and saving them for a separate book. But regarding the human, we shall proceed in this form and say this: whether he wishes it or not, he possesses the seed. For God has created him so for many reasons (which do not fit into this specific philosophy) so that man shall be free: if he has desire for it, he has seed, and vice versa—unforced, standing free, and un-coerced. However that may be, let us move past this talk to avoid confusion, and recount the text according to our purpose: first, how a man may produce a seed or not; then concluding with how it proceeds; and finally, how it grows in its formation.

<margin>B</margin> However, so that the beginning may be recognized—how man is ordained by God for the seed and left to his own will—it is thus: God has given man the <term>Phantasy of Delight</term> <note>imagination driven by desire</note> and craving. He has given this so that it may become a "Matter." This matter is the seed of which we make mention here. So that you may understand this easily and well, take note: when the delightful and craving Phantasy is generated in man by man, and placed in his <term>Speculation</term> <note>deep contemplation or mental focus</note>, and he wishes to think on it and permit it, the seed has now grown within him. But it has not been released, nor is it yet in any action, as the seed ought to be. This Phantasy of Delight arises from Speculation: for Speculation creates a Phantasy, completes it, and forms it. This Speculation takes its cue from the external object. For instance, when a man sees a beautiful woman, she presents an external object and a cause for his Speculation. And as he thinks with his reason on the cause of her creation, he then grants permission to the Will and creates a Phantasy. This is now an external object of one human toward another, which creates the Phantasy for him. For he cannot create the Phantasy from himself alone, unless he has an external object personally or imaginatively envisioned. For God created the birth of man in this way, and it stands between both people, each being envisioned by the other: the man by the woman, and vice-versa. Thus, a complete Phantasy is formed in both of them. For one person alone has only a half-phantasy, but the two together have a whole phantasy, for God has ordained it so.

<margin>C</margin> Since Phantasy is the "Mother of the Seed," and by no means is it the physical nature of the human, it is easy enough to understand that the seed depends on the free will of the human—be it much, little, or none at all. For so long as he does not have the external object, as mentioned, he has no Phantasy, and thus no seed. How this seed arises from the Speculation of the human you should understand from us in this way: know that Phantasy makes the seed, and Nature does not.

Observe that God has given the <term>fluids of the body</term> <note>original: "liquoribus Corporis"</note> a specific power: when a man ignites them through his Phantasy, they become a seed. This fluid lies quietly distributed throughout the whole body of a human, just like wood. When wood is held to a fire, it ignites, burns, and becomes a fire itself. So too is the Phantasy in man: it is so created by God that it makes the human into what the Phantasy is. If the Phantasy is angry, the whole body is angry; if it is greedy, the whole body is likewise. Therefore, the seed of man is to be understood in the same way: the <term>Fluid of Life</term> <note>original: "Liquor Vitae"</note> is like wood in its nature, and the Phantasy is the fire that ignites it—like wood becoming fire—to be what it is predestined by God to be: a seed. With this, we conclude this speech and say that the external object creates the Phantasy, and the Phantasy creates the seed, and Nature does not.

So that we do not forget how the seed becomes complete in a "Center" where it shall then go into formation, it happens thus: The <term>Matrix</term> <note>the womb</note> is ordained by God to have a magnetic and <term>amber-like</term> <note>original: "Agsteinische"; referring to the static-electric properties of amber</note> nature and quality, to draw the seed of the man to itself. Just as a magnet draws iron, which is also ordained by God for that purpose, or as <term>amber</term> <note>original: "Carabe"; a Persian-derived term for amber</note> draws silk. For if the womb did not have such an attractive power, it would not become pregnant and would receive no seed from the man. This attractive power of the Womb works thus: as soon as a woman has formed her Phantasy, the formation immediately lies as a complete seed in one part of the womb. It does not remain in the body as it does in the man, but comes hastily into the mother-womb. Then she receives the...

P H I L O S O P H Y

<margin>A</margin>
The mother, through the attractive power within her, draws in the male seed; she is not susceptible to this more than once <note>meaning, conception occurs in a single moment of attraction</note>, and just as often as there is a new <term>Imagination</term> <note>original: "Phantasey"; in this context, it refers to a creative, formative power of the mind and desire</note>, so too is there a new magnet. This is the cause of conception: when the magnet is correctly perceived and applied to such magnets. Thus the seed enters the <term>Matrix</term> <note>the womb</note>, and there is no other cause. Therefore, the imaginations are designed to respond to the <term>External Object</term> <note>original: "Gegenwurff"; the stimulus that sparks the imagination</note>, providing a cause for the imagination according to the purpose for which it is predestined, and then it is set and kept there like a grain in a field, etc.

Now, while the seed lies in the womb, it may either thrive or rot. Just as a grain in a field bears no fruit if it is not fertilized, or is not sufficiently fertilized, so it also happens many times to the seed that it lies dormant and spoils due to the unhealthiness of the mother—matters which we leave to the books of medicine.

However, to speak of the <term>Formation</term> <note>original: "Formierung"; the developmental process of the fetus</note>, know that all the limbs and parts that are in the entire body—blood and flesh, bone, veins, marrow, etc.—originate from each individual seed. And when every individual seed is gathered into one, yet remains distinct from the others, each has its own effect on its corresponding part: bone upon bone, flesh upon flesh. And as such a thing exists in the whole body, so the names are distributed during the formation, by the power of their created nature, which was so designed by God that it lies in the mother and shall become a human. These seeds in a human are gathered from both parents into one person; and whichever parent’s limb-seed prevails in the growth of the form, that part is formed accordingly. And even if the child does not look exactly like either parent, the cause is the total mixture of both together, which act equally, resulting in a middle ground between them.

<margin>B</margin>
But so that you understand the distinction between children—what it is that makes a male or a female—know this: it lies in the Imagination. If the woman is stronger in her Imagination than the man, and more firmly "ignited" <note>aroused or spiritually focused</note>, this produces a female. The same is to be understood regarding the man: the strength of the Imagination sits at the top. They can never have an exactly equal Imagination; one must always be stronger than the other. No health or craft can change this. But if some limbs in the body do not give their seed, those same limbs will not grow on the child. However, if a seed falls twofold—and especially if all seeds fall twofold for someone—two children are produced. The only cause is that the seeds fall unevenly, or miscarry, or two unequal seeds come together, or the seed of one limb falls twofold, or falls incorrectly in another place. Or when the "head-seed" falls twofold and all others fall singly, then a twofold head is produced. But when two children are born grown together, it is because the seeds fell twofold but were not correctly separated by Nature. One could write a long description of such various births, but this is not necessary for the wise.

Now that the form of children has been shown, take further note of their growth. God has granted and ordained forty weeks for the child to grow in the mother's womb, setting a goal just as He does for grapes and wheat; everything has its goal. Initially, Nature begins to set and arrange the form—that is, to arrange the seed in its proper place where it belongs. Once such order has been established, it then begins to grow and strengthen each limb: the seed of the bones becomes bone, the seed of the veins becomes veins, etc., until every limb stands and exists as it should. At this point, Nature ceases her work; she acts no more upon the child, leaving it entirely in its own being. The reason is that the child is perfect, and Nature can make nothing more of it, for her work is finished. After this comes the Grace of God, as is fitting for the Godhead, to complete His creature so that it reaches the end for which it was ordained, and He gives it Life. Thus the child lives and becomes stronger and stronger, until it gains such strength that it can endure the Earth and tolerate the air of the world. Once that is achieved, the hour of birth has arrived.

<margin>C</margin>
Thus a child is born, who then increases in growing nature and quality.

To describe the complete human being, however, and not just the child: note that in Life lies all human necessity, everything that belongs to a human. And as soon as God gives the human Grace—that is, Life—the human receives the soul, as well as sight and hearing, the spirit, etc., and everything a human should and must have: reason, wisdom, foresight, etc., as pertains to a human, though all are weak and faint. All of these, as they are within them, grow along with Nature. And the stronger the limbs become, the stronger these qualities become as well.

But lest we only burden ourselves with the birth of man, we also wish to give an indication of the state of man—namely, in what way man is set above cows and calves, which our friends and kinsmen raise and milk. First, to give instruction, let this be our model: that man in himself is nothing. For that which he has that is mortal makes him a man. Therefore, a man <term>absolutely understood</term> <note>original: "absolutè verstandẽ"</note> is a calf. But we do not wish to dwell on the <term>term</term> <note>original: "termino"</note> but on the foundation, and speak of the interior of the human, which concerns the Light of Man. So let us leave the human in his frailties and fragile things that he has about him. But there is something inside the human that is not in the calf; that is what we wish to present to our patrons. In this Philosophy, we describe the human; for the human and the cat both have a philosophy, but the noblest Philosophy is to contemplate the Eternal. For what use to us is the sight of a cat, or the wagging of a dog? Or what should be understood of outward show or titles? For that is a mortal and baseless philosophy when it comes to the true mark. # ON THE GENERATION OF MAN #
<note>original: "DE GENERATIONE HOMINIS"</note>

<margin>A</margin> ...is to contemplate the most noble and highest <term>Philosophy</term>, and by no means to depart from it. But what is it that has a firm foundation, and not a collapsing foundation that the moths eat away?

We have made mention and proposed to you that we wish to let go of the mortal things that man carries upon himself, and instead contemplate only that which is within him and does not die. That very thing we regard and hold to be the highest Philosophy. Now, as we undertake to write of such things—not as a mere whim, as is the opinion of the <term>Logicians</term> <note>Scholastic philosophers who relied on formal logic rather than direct observation of nature</note>—it is necessary, and more than necessary, that we describe nothing here unless it were well-confirmed by your own teachings. But our excuse for not regarding their teachings is this: their "soups and meat" are over-boiled and entirely evaporated. By this we mean they are completely nullified in our thinking; great subtle speeches and much clever ingenuity are found among them, but the path that lies before their eyes is entirely rough and unplaned. Thus, when we consider what the **State of Man** is, it is an honor and a fundamental duty for us to know where lies and truth are mentioned and where they lie entangled. For the state of man is solely the essence of his Art, Reason, Wisdom, etc., and everything that pertains to the height of humanity.

However, so that we may bring you enlightenment and may powerfully "philosophize," and not look upon the teachings and fictions of a stubborn, subtle writer (as fleeting spirits are prone to do), we wish to give you a clear and good report of **Man's Reason**, of his thoughts, wisdom, teaching, art, foresight, state, etc., and also show from where each one comes and springs. For through this teaching, we shall be sufficiently satisfied with the ground of Truth and with the "fleeting airs" of the internal bodies of the mortal frame. But there is the **immortal body of man**, to which God has given his Reason, Sensibility, Wisdom, Teaching, Art, Essence, etc., and everything that is above mortality. Therefore, if a man were to come with highness and wisdom out of his external body, <margin>B</margin> all that same wisdom and reason which man uses is eternal with this body, as an **Internal Man**; for man may live [truly], and not merely as an external being. For such an internal man is eternally clarified and truthful; and even if he does not appear perfect to the mortal body, he nevertheless appears perfect after the departure of the same. That which we have now recounted is called the <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>original: "Lumen Naturae"; the innate source of wisdom and reason provided by God to understand the world</note>, and it is eternal. God has given this to the internal body, so that it may be governed through the internal body, and that according to Reason. Thus, everything that man does, and ought to do, he should do out of the Light of Nature. For the Light of Nature is Reason alone, and nothing else. Therefore, he who wishes to be a **righteous Physician** <note>original: "Artzet"</note> must believe and practice medicine out of his Reason—that is, out of the Light of Nature—and not without that Light. For the Light is that which gives Faith. For Christ wants you to believe with your conscience, and not without it; and a "certain faith" is not a bold whim, which is not pleasing to God. If you wish to use an Art, use it according to the Light of Nature, and not in a "fleeting" manner; for God has given every man enough Light, upon which he is predestined, so that he cannot err.

It is a great thing to pursue through the Light of Nature: that God provides everything man does within the Light of Nature, so that he should live according to Reason and not otherwise. For Reason is in man, but his will is fragile and inconstant.

However, so that we may describe the origin of the **Internal Man** or Body, mark our words: all internal bodies are but *one* body, and a single thing in all men. But it is distributed according to the well-ordered numbers of the body, one differently than the other. And when they all <margin>C</margin> come together, there is only one Light and only one Reason; so that, if we wished to live perfectly, we would all live equally in one Reason, not in two or three, etc.

Regarding this, know that when man is conceived or born (as we have physical bodies), he is endowed with the perfect Light of Nature; it is the same on the first day as on the last, always perfect in itself. But the reason it *appears* imperfect is caused by the weakness of the <margin>*</margin> numbers <note>likely referring to the physical proportions or "instruments" of the body</note> and the un-grown strength which the Reason is entitled to have in its instruments wherein it lies. Upon which you should note that a child requires no "pulling" <note>or "training/forcing"</note> toward Reason, <margin>Souls.</margin> for it will not be "given" to him [from the outside]. He should only be drawn toward **Understanding**; Reason he has himself. **Understanding** <note>original: "Verstand"</note> is a knowledgeable Reason that has been fulfilled. But as you heard in the previous chapter regarding the Light of Nature, note that Nature—out of the innate essence from **Adam** and **Eve**—has an innate Reason, Wisdom, and Foresight, etc. This, however, refers to the physical and not to the Souls; it is for maintaining the body with its Reason, and what is necessary for its own sustenance. This comes out of a light of the Spirit, which is Nature alone; it is such a Reason as the **beast** <note>original: "Viech"; animal</note> has, which protects its body and also seeks what its body needs out of the Light of Nature. From such Light of Nature comes a special Foresight, but it is in the body and is also fulfilled in the body. Likewise, a special Wisdom is also in the body and remains in the body; likewise, a Reason is there.

Now, as has been shown, all of that is physical; we let that stand as it is and will instead treat the **Spirit**. Since we have described the physical things which we must have for our body and how they arise, we shall now further recount the following concerning Spirits, in which the State of Man resides—as you have heard, these are infused and given to the child. Note now which ones are infused. First of all, the **Soul**, which carries...

<header>PHILOSOPHY</header>

...forever the burden or joy of mankind. For this purpose were given **Reason**, **Prudence**, <margin>A</margin> and **Wisdom**; these three shall govern and guide the body, so that the yoke is not placed too heavily upon the neck of the soul. To these three is given the **Spirit**, that is, the **Understanding**, from which Reason is governed, as well as Wisdom and Prudence. From this comes the order of life, and everything proceeds from the **Light of the Spirit**, just as Nature follows the **Light of Nature**. Now, as has been said, note that man exists in sensory perception, as the Light of Nature demonstrates, and as mentioned above, an intrusion may happen to that very Light. And you should understand it thus: that there are certain external spirits that give man cunning and subtlety—that is, to the **fleeting senses**—which serve for praise, honor, subtlety, sensuality, reason, wisdom, and prudence. This is not from the spirit or the teaching of Nature, but from evil spirits, all of whom provide a delusion, a **waking fantasy**. Just as when a man sleeps and dreams, so do they create a fantasy and a "reason" in a man while he is awake. And this serves only for one's own honor, fame, and praise, etc., and the like. Although these spirits have not entered inside, it is nonetheless a mirror in which man sees himself, from which he takes a lesson for his own countenance, to behold himself. For when he fantasizes, his fantasy meets its **reflection** <note>original: "Gegenwurff," a Paracelsian term for an objective counterpart or opposing image</note> from the spirits, so that his fantasy sees a reflection there. Then, whatever he loves, he gathers and draws to himself. But in such a case, the Light of Nature and the Light of the Spirit are not in control; fantasy alone is master, which is established from fantastical thoughts in the reflection that appears to him like a dream. Thus, as recorded above, you should know that in three things the <unclear>connection</unclear> hangs: In the **Light of Nature**, for the sake of the body's preservation; and in the **Spirit**, as in the three faculties: **Wisdom**, **Prudence**, and **Reason**. But to govern the body, according to <unclear>order</unclear> as for the determined personal benefit.

Thus God has ordained for man that one person gives understanding and <margin>B</margin> **knowledge** to another, and that man uses these for himself out of his own Light. This happens for this reason: since man is not always perfect in his **cells** <note>The author uses "cells" (Zellen) to refer to the functional compartments of the brain or mind where different faculties reside</note>, he is deficient in understanding and knowledge. Therefore, God has ordained that one person teaches and instructs another in understanding and knowledge, so that his reason may be heard. But if the cells and instruments of every man's internal body were pure and perfect, and none had turned out poorly, then no man would need a **schoolmaster**. For every person would be clever enough to speculate, know, and experience what is otherwise taught, and even better. But since that is so rare, and the physical instruments darken the reason, so too is the understanding darkened. And know this: that in man, understanding and knowledge occupy a different cell than the cell of Reason; he for whom that cell is clear and pure is a perfect man.

However, so that we may approach the end of our undertaking, we wish to recount that God has given to the **inner man** all art, wisdom, and reason that belongs to eternity, so long as he is alive. Thus, note that God has provided for the body, as we have mentioned, and set it in three perfect parts, perfect in itself. But we must consider even more our heavenly part, which is the Spirit in man, good and evil angels, the **visitation** <note>original: "bestitung," referring to spiritual assistance or the presence of guiding spirits</note> of man, and the like.

Although we have established three births and growth cycles of man, we will now report on his **State**, in which he stands between the time of growth and his breaking apart <note>death</note>. You should understand that there are two states to consider: the physical state he possesses, and the eternal state he possesses. From these two follows the interpretation: the physical contains the eternal, just as a host maintains a guest. But we will let the eternal be for now and contemplate the physical, as follows. <margin>d</margin> That which sustains the body is **Life**, which only God Himself can interpret and no man. But life is placed in four things: in <term>Humors</term> <note>the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>, <term>Complexions</term> <note>the metabolic temperament of the body</note>, <term>Natural Species</term>, and in Gifts. The four **Humors** are the four juices in the **marrow** <note>original: "Medullis"</note>. But so that we do not forget the nature of man—such as **Sanguine**, **Melancholy**, **Choler** <note>original: "Sanguine, Melancholia, Cholera"</note>, etc.—it is like a child who is the middle point between father and mother. In the first human [Eve], all unfaithfulness existed; therefore unfaithfulness is innate in everyone, descended from the first seed down to us. In the first man [Adam] was seriousness; in the woman was joyfulness—that was the true solution. In Adam was honorableness, and in the woman unhonorableness; from this, nature was formed in man from his heritage, from his parents.

But that man is **complexioned**, as the so-called <term>Physicians</term> <note>original: "Artzet"</note> say: **Sanguine**, **Melancholy**, **Choleric**, **Phlegmatic**, etc. Four colors are given to man: four in Adam and four in Eve, yet they are only four of one kind: **Brown**, **White**, **Black**, and **Red**. In Eve, they were pure, beautiful, clear colors. From these four colors arises the color of every man's body—like a scale as he touches upon it—towards Red, White, Black, Brown, etc. In man are also the four <term>Complexions</term>, such as cold, moist, etc. These take their beginning thus: In Eve there was a **Complexion** that was **Cold and Dry**, but in Adam it was **Warm and Moist**. These are now the two contrary complexions, but from their mixing, two more were born. Thus, from the dryness of Eve and the heat of Adam, a complexion arises that is **Dry and Hot**. Likewise, from the moisture of Adam and the coldness of Eve, two more are born from the two complexions of Eve and Adam; in this way, the heat of Adam overcame the cold of Eve, and the dryness overcame all the moisture, and likewise the reverse in others.

<margin>A</margin> But that one person is much more inclined to steal than another is for this reason: that everything honorable was in Adam, and the opposite of honor—dishonesty—was in Eve. These qualities descended through the "scales" <note>A metaphor for the weighing or balancing of inherited traits.</note> into the seed, and according to what portion each person has received from it, so he is in his nature. For sometimes the thieving nature has prevailed, sometimes the whorish, sometimes the gambling, and so forth.

Therefore, we should not be troubled by the teachings and writings of those ignorant and inexperienced in astronomy <note>Paracelsus often critiqued traditional judicial astrology which claimed the stars controlled human fate.</note> who attribute all such things to the stars, when they should instead look to themselves. Man is a creature unto himself, just as the Earth, Air, and others are; none has the power to rule the other or to drive them toward fortune. The Moon stands free, the Heavens and the Earth are free. Man uses the Earth, and the Earth also uses the Heavens; the Heavens also use the Earth. The Heavens drop their waste upon the Earth, including whatever breaks within them; Man does the same, and the Earth gathers it all into itself.

But lest we forget our health and sickness, we wish to provide you with an introduction: that man does not inherit these from the "first seed" <note>Meaning Adam's original biological makeup.</note> alone, but from the errors of those who have come from that first seed. And there is no other cause than this: that all things are ordained by God into fragility, as is mentioned in <term>concerning Conception</term> <note>original: "de Conceptione."</note>.

First, it shall be an argument for us to establish in the description of mankind: what it is that carries them and what they nourish themselves upon. First, you should know that the Earth carries us, as does the Air, and that which grows out of the Earth is what nourishes us. However, this is different for the Nymphs <note>In the Paracelsian system, Nymphs are elemental spirits belonging to the element of water.</note>, for they use neither the realm of the Earth nor the Air. Regarding this, I shall first introduce an argument as to what it is they eat, and thereafter, what easily sustains them. Now, to settle this matter, my argument regarding food is this: the Nymphs are those of whom <term>CHRIST</term> says: <margin>B</margin> *“All people who are not of this sheepfold, but of this world of ours.”* <note>original Latin: "Omnes homines qui non sunt de hoc Ouili, sed ex hoc mundo nostro." A variation of John 10:16 regarding "other sheep."</note> Not that we wish to exclude the other three worlds, but rather to include them, for there are three kinds of sheep, besides ourselves, of which there is only one Pastor and one Shepherd. Therefore, we do not trouble ourselves with those book-writers whom they call "Holy," as if he were the only one, etc.

# B O O K
# OF METEORS BY PHILIP
# THEOPHRASTUS PARACEL-
## sus, most excellent Philosopher and Physician.

<margin>C</margin> <image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'A' with a woodcut background depicting a seated scholar within an ornate frame.</image-desc> Now, when God willed to create the Earth, and in His Divine Wisdom brought it forth according to how and in what way it should be, He divided it into four parts. Thus, there are four "Bodies" <note>original: "Corpora." These are the four elements: Earth, Water, Air, and Heaven/Fire.</note>, which four bodies shall be the Mothers of all things that should belong to that which He would create in His image—that is, <term>ADAM</term>, which is Man. Since this purpose was concluded in God, the four bodies were created: namely Heaven, Earth, Water, and Air. For as the Scripture says, He first created the Heavens, then the Earth, and subsequently the others likewise.

Now know at this time that these four bodies alone are Mothers, in such a way that they bear the fruits and assist them, so that Man may nourish himself. As an example: the Earth bears its fruit; Man nourishes himself from that fruit, and not from the Earth itself. Likewise, the Heaven is a vacant Body in itself, from which alone fruits go forth to sustain Man. How the Heaven shows and gives its fruits, I will present in this book. And I have indicated this chapter only so that it is known that the Heaven is a body for itself, without any other, and gives its fruit to Man just like the Earth.

Of the Book of METEOROLOGY <note>original: "METEORORVM"</note>

### CHAPTER I.

-># CONCERNING THE * ELEMENTED FATHER, AND<-
-># The * Elemented Mother.<-

<margin>* Or, Of the Elements.</margin>
<margin>Temperate.</margin>
<margin>Regarding the body: Qualities, not Temperaments. Those born are tempered, but not the Mothers <note>Paracelsus refers to the Elements themselves as "Mothers" that give birth to physical things.</note>.</margin>
Now know further, that it has been said of the four elements that there are four, and man must have these: and they are divided into the four <term>Temperaments</term> <note>original: "Complexiones," referring to the Galenic theory of the four bodily humors.</note>. But it shall not be as the ancients have written—namely, that the Earth is cold and dry—for that is not so. Rather, in some places it is cold and dry, in some cold and moist, in some hot and moist, and also hot and dry. But it is an Element, which is to say, it is a Mother of fruits. And that is an Element: a Mother of the things that sustain man, and not because of the Temperaments. So it is also with Water; it is said to be cold and moist, yet it is many times hot and dry, or cold and dry, etc. For Water is not created solely to be cold and moist, but it must certainly be wet; the rest does not matter. Yet this wetness is often dry and hot in its power, even though the body is wet in its physical nature. The Earth is dry so that the fruit out of it and in it may have its progress. Thus also the Heavens are not of one Temperament, but of many: it is not a Fire, though it is considered a Fire. It is the Fire in this way: that [the fire] comes from it. Its fire is sometimes water, sometimes fire, sometimes cold, sometimes warm, etc. You should know and understand this much: that the Elements are solely Mothers, and are not to be forced into one Temperament, but into many. For as the thing is that grows from it, so also is that which made and gave birth to it—just as the <note>original: "Flāmmula, Solatrum von Solatro"</note> Spearwort or Nightshade comes from its own kind.

<margin>B</margin>
Now note this. The Earth shall carry man and his dwelling, as well as stone, rock, sand, and all plants. From this it follows that it must be an Element that is compacted and firm, so that it may carry such things. From this it follows that it is hard, for it must be tilled with the plow. Now, Water must be wet so that fish may swim in it—which cannot happen in the Earth—and it shall provide salt and stone. Now, all such things must be wet in their <term>First Matter</term> <note>original: "Materia prima," the formless primal substance from which all things are created.</note>, and from that wetness come into a <term>Coagulated state</term> <note>original: "Coagulatum."</note>. But what comes from the Earth has a seed, a body that is dry: such as seed, roots, trees, and all else are of dry First Matter that is compacted. In Water, however, there is nothing in the First Matter that is a compacted body, but rather everything is a <term>Liquid</term> <note>original: "Liquor."</note>. This then has its Mother from the element of Water, and in the element of Water grow the "final matters" <note>original: "ultimæ materiæ."</note>, whose beginning is liquid and moist. Now, the third body is the Air. This same Element must also have another body, such that this body is not moist like Water, nor firm like the Earth. For this reason: all things that grow from the elements have their entrance into the body of the Air, just as a fish is in the Water. Man is placed into the <term>Airy Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus Aëreum."</note> to walk within it, just as the fish is in the water; so also are all trees and what grows there. Therefore, it is necessary that the Air be a <term>Chaos</term> <note>Paracelsus uses "Chaos" here to mean a formless, transparent atmosphere or void.</note>, not an Earth, not a Water, but <term>Transparent</term> <note>original: "Perspicuum."</note>, <term>Diaphanous</term> <note>original: "Diaphanum."</note>, untouchable, and invisible, so that what is tangible may be within it, and what is visible may be seen through it; it is just like glass.

<margin>C</margin>
So know further that the Heavens are likewise a body that is not compacted, not firm like the Earth, not wet like the Water, and not transparent like the Air. Instead, it has a special body with a different essence, so that the Heavens are not <term>Earthly</term> <note>original: "Terrestre."</note>, and yet they are a compacted essence—though not earthly-compact. It is thin and pervasive like water, and yet no water; it is clear and see-through, and yet not as the Air. Rather, it is a body like a smoke, which distinguishes itself in its essence and <term>Physicality</term> <note>original: "Corporalitet."</note> from all other bodies. That is, it is not like a stone or wood or earth, nor like a water, nor like the air; instead, it is a body that has no mixture at all with the others. Thus the Heavens are a body that can best be understood through the image of smoke. For it must be so for this reason: what grows from it is also thus—they are bodies and not bodies, they are compact and not compact, they are pervasive like water and yet not water, they are untouchable like the air and yet not the air. Such is the Sun, which is a body as mentioned, the Moon, and all the stars. Now, it is without a Temperament, and it is the Element of Fire, and a Mother from which the fire grows and springs. Just as fire has a physicality to it, so also do the Heavens, and so also the stars that take their nature and essence from the Heavens. Therefore, know of the Heavens that this same body is a special part and an Element of Fire; and whatever fire is meant to do, the Heavens do it, for they give it and it grows out of them.

So also know henceforth of the colors of the Heavens. The Earth has a color through and through, blackish, and whatever other colors there are come from a mineral. Water also has a color through and through; whatever other colors there are come from a mineral. Now, the color of Water has no name; it is not white, it is not gray, nor blue, nor green, and yet it may be counted among all of them or seen as something similar. The Earth also has a color; it is not black, it is not brown, etc., and yet it is something like them. So it is also with the Air, where one sees a pure color,

through <note>catchword: "durch"</note>

He describes the unique physical properties of each element, likening Air to a transparent void (Chaos) and the Heavens to a subtle, smoke-like body.</summary>

### The First Chapter.

<margin>A</margin>The transparent <term>Chaos</term> <note>The "Chaos" here refers to the primordial state of matter or the atmospheric space between the elements.</note> is not white, nor brown, nor yellow, etc., and yet it is somewhat like these colors. In the same way, the Heaven is colored: it is at once green, blue, and brown, and yet it is none of these colors, though it may be seen as such. For the elemental bodies are such that no "perfect" <note>Meaning distinct or pure.</note> colors may be called by name. But whatever comes forth from them has its own clear, understandable, and namable colors. The elements themselves do not have perfect colors, but are as described. For not just one color grows from them, but many colors. Therefore they are composed of many colors, as many as come out of them. As from the Earth comes green, red, blue, black, etc. So also from the Water come all colors. Likewise from the Air and from the Heaven. Therefore they are *collected colors* <note>original: "Colores collecti"</note>; mixed together into one from all kinds of colors. And the mixture gives no color—that is, it can give no color with a clear, understandable, or known name.

Now, likewise, observe also the Heaven and its fruits through this example. You see that what grows out of the Earth has its tangible foot and root in the Earth, such as trees and grass, etc. Now, however, the stars are the fruit of the Heaven, and belong to the Heaven, but they do not take root in the Heaven; they stand beneath the Heaven for all to see without any support or attachment. This is the very opposite of the Earth. The one gives its fruit with roots, the other without. The one stands upward, the other hangs downward. The one gives its fruit toward the heights, the other downward. It is also the same in the Water, as the fish provide an example; they stand on nothing and have no feet, but they swim in the Water. In the exact same way, the stars also swim in the Heaven, in the body of the Heaven, which is to be understood just like the Water: and they have the order of their swimming as God created them—high, low, far, near, fast, slow, etc. 

<margin>B</margin>Which I leave to <term>Astronomy</term>; it is not necessary to mention it here, except to understand that the Heaven is a body that can carry a swimming thing like water, and yet it is not water, but dry; and that which swims in it is dry. It is not "swum" in the sense of being in water, and yet it is swimming. It has not walked or run, for there are no feet, nor anything upon which they might step. Rather, it is such a wondrous work of God, and an element that contains all the others and encloses them together in a <term>rotundity</term> <note>Roundness or spherical shape.</note> and circle.

Now, you should also have such an understanding of the stars. They have grown out of the Heaven and remain in it in a flying manner, like a bird in the air, according to the order and circle as God created them and as it pleased Him. Now, they have grown once, and so they remain forever and ever. The trees and fruits of the Earth perish and become something else again; but the stars perish only once and never come back—that is, at the end of the world. Otherwise, everything that lies in other elements is eaten by rust, moths, and death. Only the stars of the heavenly element remain, but their "fruits" come and go, such as rain, snow, etc. Now they have for the most part one color, which is fiery. Just as the Earth shows green as its primary color, and yet has other colors too; as does the sun, which is also special in its color. Now, although the colors are fiery and are the fire, the right element: yet they are not "wood-fire," but the element. For there is a distinction between Fire and the element of Heaven, as *Fire* and *Heaven* <note>original: "Ignis vnnd Cœlum"</note>. Fire is not an element; Heaven, however, is an element. Fire is a material that cooks and breaks, and brings things into <unclear>vlaitam</unclear> <note>Possibly "ultimate" or "dead" matter.</note> matter; it is like Death. Fire and Death are the same: Fire consumes everything and takes it away, and Death does the same. Therefore, it cannot be an element, but rather a "Death"—a visible death, a sensible 

<margin>C</margin>death. Just as the other death is invisible, which no one sees nor has seen. And as Fire takes away and consumes, so also Death takes away man and whatever has life. Thus Death and Fire will stand at the same degree. And the Fire that is an element is the Heaven with its fruits, which are the stars.

Regarding Fire, you should know that it has been reckoned to be an element, to be one of the four, which cannot be. For Earth proves itself as an element, the Water also, and the Air also. Now see: where is the fourth element? Namely, Fire cannot be it. For it gives man nothing "elemental," gives no fruits, can have no fellowship with man, nor man with it. Rather, it only concerns us as far as the nature of Death, which separates soul and body from one another. Thus, the fourth element must be the Heaven. For the Heaven has fellowship with man, and man cannot be without it; he must have it. Without Fire, he may well be, and live without Fire. Therefore, since he can be without Fire, Fire is no element, but rather the Heaven, which gives day and night, summer and winter, and increases all fruits, and assists the other elements. Therefore it is the element, and it should not be called the *Element of Fire* <note>original: "Elementum Ignis"</note>, but rather the *Element of Heaven* <note>original: "Elementum Cœli"</note>. Just as there is an *Element of Earth*, an *Element of Air*, and an *Element of Water*. Thus the Heaven is the fourth element, and the first element. For the Scripture says that God first created Heaven and Earth as the first element. That is, the Heaven first: for see, in the Heaven the other elements are enclosed within the outer Element of Heaven. For before the wine exists, the barrel must first be there.

<summary>This page argues that Heaven, not Fire, is the true fourth element, describing stars as its "fruits" that swim in a dry medium and distinguishing the creative power of the Heavens from the destructive nature of fire.</summary>

# Of the Book of METEORS

Thus, the Element of Heaven is the first element, followed by the Earth: just as the barrel comes first, and then the wine.

->### CHAPTER II.<-

->## ON THE FIRST MATTER OF HEAVEN<-
->### and the Stars.<-

You have already understood the Body of Heaven and what kind of body it is. For the Earth has a specific body, as does the Water, and the Air; likewise, the Heaven has its own specific body. Now, however, you should know that all four bodies of the four elements are made from nothing; that is, they were made solely through the Word of God, which commanded "Let it be" <note>original: "FIAT"</note>. Even though this is so, the "Nothing" from which "Something" arose has become a substance and body, just as they now appear. This same body of all four elements is divided into three species <note>The author is referring to the "Three Primes"—the three fundamental types of substance that make up all matter.</note>: so that the word "Let it be" became a threefold body, divided into three kinds of bodies. For the Earth consists of three parts—that is, three kinds—and the Water is also threefold in its body, as is the Air, and the Heaven. It is just as if someone took gold, silver, and copper and made many different instruments from them, where none were like the others, yet each would be the same in substance though not in <margin>B</margin> form. Though it also differs within the elements themselves. Thus, the four elements are not one single body. For the Air is one body, the Water another, and the Earth another: and so too the Heaven. It is as if four drinking vessels were made of the same material. Yet this example only serves to show that you should understand that the Earth has three kinds of bodies, as do the Air, the Heaven, and the Water. And just as you see that wood is one body, metal another, stone another, and fungus another: so too are the four bodies of the elements divided from one another. It is like taking lead and making from it <term>Red Lead</term> <note>original: "Minium," a bright red pigment made from lead oxide.</note>, and <term>White Lead</term> <note>original: "Cerussam," a white pigment made from lead carbonate.</note>, and glass, and a <term>Spirit of Saturn</term> <note>A chemical preparation, such as lead acetate, derived from lead (Saturn being the alchemical name for lead).</note>. Now see, these four are all lead, and yet none of them is exactly like lead once it is made, but each is different. I only wish to show here that three species have come from the Word, and those same three species are divided into the four elements, each into a specific and different body, according to what was required of those elements for their office <note>Their natural function or duty in the universe.</note>.

Now no one should wonder at this philosophy—that there are three kinds, yet they are divided into four elements. For if we rightly consider the number, God took Three for Himself, and made all things from Three, and placed all things into Three. For the origin of this number is from God first; that is, the beginning is Three in the Godhead <note>A reference to the Holy Trinity.</note>. Now the Word was also threefold, for the Trinity spoke it, and the Word is the beginning of Heaven and Earth and all creatures. Thus, by the number, we are reminded of the Trinity in the three species. Henceforth all things are set in three, and there is nothing on Earth that does not consist of the three species, and it is brought back into three bodies again, so that it is visible and proven that every creature may be divided into three pieces, each to its place. What is said of the four <margin>C</margin> things—that is, the four elements—suggesting that every thing contains all four elements within it: that is not true. Rather, a thing has a "complexion" <note>The specific balance of qualities like heat or moisture.</note> within it and nothing more, and it can have no other element in it than what it received from its "mother." For example, every herb has only one element, which is Earth; every stone has only one element, which is Water. Furthermore, it has a complexion within it: Cold and Moist, Cold or Dry, Warm or Moist, or Warm or Dry. Yet that complexion is not the element itself; rather, the "mother" is the element—the Water or the Earth. As an example: man is made from the <term>Slime of the Earth</term> <note>original: "Limo Terrae," the primordial dust or mud from which Adam was formed.</note>. But the element is not the slime; rather, the human is the <term>Fifth Essence</term> <note>original: "Quintum Esse" or Quintessence, the pure substance that transcends the four elements.</note>. But he returns to the element; that is, he goes back into the element, but with such a distinction as is shown between the element and the flesh. Thus, you should understand in this paragraph that the elements are divided into three parts alone, and those three parts are the <term>First Matter</term> <note>original: "Materia prima," the fundamental substance from which all things are formed.</note> of the elements. But the First Matter of Water is different from that of Earth, or Air, or Heaven. For the number Three gives only three species at the foundation, which Three make a perfect body, as is found in all bodies through the art of nature.

Therefore, now note this number Three: that every art that exists in nature and is born from it should seek no more than three species. Just as the number in the Godhead, which stands immovably at Three, can be neither less nor more. And any art that seeks more is false and errs against nature, seeking in her what is not there. These Three are the <term>First Matter</term>, and they have only one name: just as God is one, so is the <term>First Matter</term>. And as there are three Persons in the Godhead—the Father, the Son, and the Spirit—so in this place each species is distinct for itself, according to its function.

<summary>This page explains that all four elements (Heaven, Earth, Water, Air) were created by God's Word from nothing and are fundamentally composed of three distinct "species" or substances. It argues that all natural things are governed by this divine number three, reflecting the Trinity, and that each creature originates from a single "mother" element rather than a mixture of all four.</summary>

-># The Second Chapter. 73<-

<margin>A</margin> For just as there is an Office of the Father, an Office of the Son, and an Office of the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Officium Patris, Officium Filij, Officium Spiritus Sancti"</note>: so too are there three types of offices in the Three Primes <note>original: "Tribus primis"; these are the three fundamental substances of alchemical philosophy: Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury</note>, which are nevertheless called by one name, the **First Matter** <note>original: "prima Materia"</note>. And the **First Matter** remains within that number. Furthermore, the **First Matter** was divided by God into four parts—that is, into the four Elements—and brought into four essences, separated by God Himself, in this way: whatever was in the **First Matter** belonging to the Earth was separated into the Earth, into the Air, into the Water, and into the Heaven. And each was formed into its predestined shape. The Earth as an earth with its own office, likewise the Water as water should be, and the Air and the Heaven the same. As was shown in the example of Lead, everything comes from one Body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, but four bodies, none of which is like the other, are brought there through the art of nature. God is far more wonderful in His work, being above all nature: as He proved there, namely: making the Heaven wonderful, the Earth, the Water, the Air, all of which are separated into four types of bodies, taken from one Matter, which is then threefold, and which comes from the Word.

<margin>B</margin> Now these first three are three pieces, namely: **Fire, Salt,** and **Balsam** <note>original: "Ignis, Sal, vnd Balsamus"</note>. These are three things, and every Body is made of these three: not only the Elements but also their fruits that come from them. For instance, the Earth in its Body is threefold: Fire, **Salt**, and **Balsam**. And whatever grows out of it is likewise in these three species: like a tree, whose Body is **Fire, Salt, Balsam**; likewise the herbs. So too is the Water; it is also **Fire, Salt, Balsam**. And whatever grows from the Water is likewise nothing other than **Fire, Salt, Balsam**: such as all stones and metals, whose mother is the Water—that is, the Element. Likewise the Heaven is also Fire, **Salt**, and **Balsam**. Whatever its fruits are, they are also thus: that is, the Sun is Fire, **Salt, Balsam**; the snow, rain, and the like are comprised of these three bodies under one Body. Therefore, the art of nature learns to bring forth nothing more from the fruits than Fire, **Salt**, and **Balsam**. And through Art they are separated from each other, so that the Fire is separate, the **Salt** is separate, and the **Balsam** is separate; neither less nor more can be found. I recount all of this so that **Meteorics** <note>original: "Meteorica"; the study of atmospheric and celestial phenomena</note> may be more easily understood. Otherwise, it is well recounted and explained with greater understanding in **Philosophy**. Now you should know that these three first—Fire, **Salt**, and **Balsam**—may also be called by other names, as I mention in **Philosophy**: Fire as **Sulfur**, **Salt** as itself, and **Balsam** as **Liquid Mercury** <note>original: "Liquor Mercurius"</note>. These three—**Sulfur, Balsam,** and **Mercury**—are those called the **First Matter of things** <note>original: "prima materia rerum"</note>. This is now enough said of the beginning as an introduction to **Meteorics**. And I point out this **First Matter** so that the fruits of the Element of **Heaven** <note>original: "Coeli"</note> may be more easily understood: how the **Celestial impressions** <note>The influences or phenomena generated by the stars and heavens</note> are born and what they are in their nature. This is also for the sake of the virtues and powers within them, so they are better known to a physician and more understandable to a **meteorologist**. For just as the Earth is useful to man, so too is the Heaven useful to him. Every Element was created for man’s sake; therefore, he should recognize it well.

<margin>C</margin> Furthermore, it is necessary that we know concerning the elements what an **Element** <note>original: "Elementum"</note> is and what it is not. Understand first this example: A human has a large body and many types of being in the body. But that which is the human is a soul and a spirit, and it is small. The reason we call the Body a human is because the human is in the Body, and the soul is not without the Body, but they are together. The eye is large on a human, but the power that sees is a small quantity compared to the eye. Thus the Earth is called an element, though it is only a bare Body, but the Element **Earth** is within that same Body and is invisible: just as the spirit of man is also invisible. In the same way, the Heaven that we see is a large Body; the element within it is a small spirit compared to the greatness the Heaven has. Man speaks from his mouth; it is not the Body that speaks, the spirit speaks. Likewise, the Earth bears fruit; not it, but the Element within it gives the fruits. Thus the four elements are **Corporal** <note>Physical or bodily</note>: but in essence and nature, they are spirits. And God is wonderful in His creation: He is not like a carpenter who makes a house from a Body and cares nothing for the spirit. That same Body is without the spirit, therefore it gives no fruit; it is dead, it is never alive. For the spirit is alive, and Life is the spirit, and Life and the spirit work all things, yet they are one thing and not two. Therefore know, when it is said "that comes from the element," understand it comes from the element and not from the Body. The tongue speaks, yet it speaks nothing: for the spirit is in it that speaks; the flesh by itself does not. But through such mixing and union, the Body is thought to do all things and is regarded as the element itself, though it is only a Body and not the spirit. Just as flesh and blood are not the man, but the spirit is the man. Thus there are four souls or spirits: one the Earth, the second the Water, the third the Air, the fourth the Heaven.

Based on this, understand further that all things and fruits grow out of the Earth: and what grows out of it also has the Element Earth as its mother. Namely, it has a Body, and in the Body, the **Spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum"</note>. The **Spirit** is the true thing; the other is nothing. The **Boxwood** <note>original: "Buxus"</note> has a taste; that same taste is its **Spirit**; the rest is the Body. **Musk** <note>original: "Bißem"</note> has its soul in its scent <note>The original uses "Geschmack" (taste/flavor) here, but in the context of musk, it implies its sensory essence or aroma.</note>; if that is lost, it is like a piece of dead hewn wood that gives no more fruit. Just as in the taste—that is, the spirit is the taste—so in corals, the color is the spirit, the rest is a Body. Thus all fruits are like their element in Body and **Spirit**. Not...
