# Of the Book METEORS
<note>original: "METEORORVM"</note>

Wind-stars are inclined toward rain, and yet they are not of the rain-stars, though they are of a similar nature. But
<margin>A</margin> they are particular wind-stars, not universal ones, such as the wind-stars of the <term>Peroledis</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for specific atmospheric or astral entities that govern certain weather patterns</note>. These same wind-stars are beautiful in color, pure, clear, and high-reaching, and the Ethereal Cellar <note>The upper atmosphere where Paracelsus believed alchemical transformations of weather occurred</note> cannot "resolve" or melt them. The reason for this is that they are as dry as seasoned wood, which can never become water; their nature is beautiful, light, airy, and joyful. They originate from a dry <term>Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury</term> <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary elements of alchemical theory</note> in which there is no moisture; therefore, they cannot be brought to a state of dampness. These winds are also mild, pleasant, agreeable, and healthy for mankind. For they are well-tempered and come from the good "Three Firsts" of the <term>Prima Materia</term> <note>The "First Matter" from which all things are created</note>; they gladden man and his blood. Whatever comes from them—that is, what comes from the stars—is well "digested" <note>matured or refined through alchemical heat</note> and clearly subtilized. But where the coarse species of the Three Firsts lie, such as in the rain-stars and the like, in those places there are also coarse clouds: black, dark, gloomy, and troublesome. This all depends on the First Matter. Furthermore, know that the wind-stars also have such a nature in them, but they bear no rain. They may have the "complexion" and quality of it, but they give no clouds, and therefore no rain. However, they can certainly provide promotion or hindrance to the weather, as has been sufficiently recounted. There is also an advantage in these beautiful stars: they keep their clouds beautiful. For the sun shines through in those places; it shines through them and subtilizes them even more. In the coarse rain-clouds, the sun can accomplish nothing. As the common proverb says: "A falcon cannot be made from a raven." Likewise, it is not possible for the sun to bleach something pure out of such coarse growth. Thus is the birth of beautiful clouds and wind: from the subtle, well-prepared Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury, with the help of <term>Vulcan</term> <note>The alchemical personification of transformative fire or heat</note>, who is the preparer of such things, entirely perfect and good.

<margin>B</margin> Now, moving further, as you have heard regarding the rain-weather: know also that there are still several signs that announce rain and such weather as has been described, namely in this form. It is said that "Morning-red" or "Evening-red" is a true sign. The reason is: when a rain-star is about to begin, and it contains within it a Sulfur that is too coarse, a Salt that is too coarse, and likewise a Mercury, such coarseness is merely a "foam." This foam is then cast up into the heights and becomes just like a cloud—yet it is not a cloud, but a foam and a vapor of many colors. The Red comes from the Sulfur and Mercury; the Blue, Brown, and Yellow from the Salt; and some of the Yellow also from the Mercury. These appear in the morning because they cannot endure the sun in the heights; rather, they vanish directly in the sun's heat, and their colors cannot be seen before the sun's brilliance—just as the moon and other stars, which have even better colors, also vanish. Now, when such stars begin, and their "foam" happens to evaporate in this way, the other preparations follow after: the clouds, the wind, and the rain, according to how that same star is natured. Sometimes it happens quickly that same day, but usually soon thereafter—unless there is a "concordance" or alignment of opposing planets, the moon, or wind-stars that destroy it. But they rarely show themselves without something coming of it, often long rains, for there is a multitude of stars involved. Thus you should now know that this Chapter has sufficiently explained the origin and essence of rain, along with the other Chapters and Paragraphs. And note that there is nothing else here but that the stars are "Trees" <note>original: "Arbores"</note> that give their fruit in the same form as those on Earth. Therefore, since they are on both sides of one mass, one First Matter, they join together and benefit one another. Just as man is of the Earth, he clings to the Earth and must take and receive his nourishment from it. Likewise, one should also note that often it does not rain for a long time; one should think nothing of this other than that those stars have poured themselves out and are now gathering more. And when the time comes, everything is fulfilled and restored at once; for nothing is neglected from above—what does not come at one time comes at another.

### CHAPTER VII.
## ON CONGELATION.
<note>original: "DE CONGELATIONE"</note>

Now you shall learn of the "Congelates"—that is, of frozen things, snow-water, and whatever is of the nature of snow; that is, of the things that make the Winter. And first, note in general that these are also merely "Trees"—that is, only Stars—from which they come, ordained thus by God. Therefore, it is necessary that these same Winter-stars be well understood in their essence and their species, for they are also from the First Matter of the Three Primes, just as I have written of the other species. So, know first regarding the beginning of such "generation" <note>creation or birth</note>: there are certain stars that are contrary to the Sun. And because they are contrary to the Sun, when the Sun moves from its "Exaltation" <note>The point in the zodiac where a planet or sun has its greatest power</note>, as in Winter, the Winter-stars then abound. There is one species among them whose nature is this: everything that the Sun "resolves" <note>melts or turns to vapor</note>, they "coagulate"—that is, they turn all the water into ice. Now their power is this: You see how God has separated from one another the Brightness and the Darkness—that is, Day and Night. You also see how God has separated the Heat into one place—that is, the Sun—and thereafter the Cold into another place—which is now the Winter Circle.
Thus, Heat has the power to resolve, and Cold has the power to coagulate. When they were together...

# Chapter Seven
<note>original: "Siebende Capittel"</note>

<margin>A</margin> [Heat and cold] were once joined, where it was neither hot nor cold. But Divine <term>Alchemy</term> <note>original: "Alchimiſterey"; here referring to the natural process of separation and refinement directed by God</note> separated them, and from that, their individual properties emerged. And just as heat is in the Sun and its stars, so cold is also enclosed within the stars. A free path was given to Heat for its reign according to the season, and to Cold its rule also according to the season, and a <term>boundary</term> <note>original: "Terminus"</note> was set for both. From this, it follows that each is powerful in its own strength to fulfill its office. And although at times the cold may not manifest—because it is too strongly overwhelmed by the warmth, perhaps due to the land or the <term>constellation</term> <note>the alignment of stars affecting earthly conditions</note>—its power is nevertheless not taken away. In the same way, the Sun cannot melt all snow. Therefore, it is necessary to note that resistance also happens to the cold in return.

So also know the further cause of Cold: Fire is a sufficient example by which the Sun’s heat may be recognized and what its effect is. <margin>B</margin> But for Cold, there is no public example like fire, except solely in the element of Water, in crystals, and other stones; thus is its form. Crystals grow out of water; now, their <term>matter</term> <note>original: "Materia"</note> is such that they have within themselves the <term>Spirit of Coagulation</term> <note>original: "Spiritus coagulationis"; the spiritual force that causes liquids to become solid</note>, and for that reason, they are coagulated—just as water is by the <term>Frigid and Icy stars</term> <note>original: "Frigoriſchen vn[d] Glacieſchen Sternen"</note>. Know then that in the same way as there is a Spirit of Coagulation in that place within the fruits of the water, so it is also in the Icy stars. And when that same Spirit enters the water, it turns it to ice and coagulates it. But the reason it does not last is that this same water is not a "Body" that is meant to be permanent in its coagulation, but is meant to be <term>resolved</term> <note>melted or dissolved</note>, and its <term>Tincture</term> <note>essential quality or color</note> is worth nothing in that place. But if the <term>matter of gems</term> <note>original: "materia Gemmarum"</note> were there and not yet coagulated, it would soon be coagulated in that same place with a firm and lasting coagulation. It is certainly true that if its <term>exaltation</term> <note>its peak state of power</note> were to remain in its <term>being</term> <note>original: "Eſſe"</note> forever, the ice would not be opened [melted], yet it would still not be lasting in the Tincture of the crystalline kind. These stars of the Icy kind rule the winter, whether in the water, in fruits, in the earth—wherever there is something that may be moist, it is subject to <term>congelation</term> <note>freezing</note>. The other stars, snow and others, are not to be counted as strictly as the winter in that place. For snow is the rain of winter, and at that time it is more convenient and useful than rain; therefore God created it in such a way. Now understand that the Icy stars, which make the true winter, have the Spirit of Coagulation in all <term>wave-like moistures</term> <note>original: "humiditatibus vndolis"</note>, and they are composed of <term>Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury</term> in such a way that nothing can be colder than they are. Thus, the hottest <term>First Matter</term> <note>original: "Prima materia"</note> went into the Sun, and the coldest into <term>Saturn</term>; for Saturn is the Son of Cold, along with the other wind-stars.

Now note, however, the <term>error</term> <note>irregular movement or "wandering"</note> of the stars, that it often happens that a <term>discordance</term> <note>original: "Diſconcordanz"</note> occurs among them, so that often the winter stars rise in the summer. That is, they become active in summer and not in winter; they miss the timing of their work, not in their circular path, but in their <term>course</term> <note>original: "Curſu"</note>. If then in summer the time is <term>Zephyric</term> <note>westerly/gentle</note> or <term>Boreal</term> <note>northerly/cold</note>, and the Moon agrees with that nature, and the stars become "fruitful" at that time, then they proceed and show their snow in summer. But if the time is not so—that is, if the Moon were not inclined toward them, and the winds were not helpful to it, and the region were too low, and the constellation too warm—then that same snow would become rain. For the warmth beneath the star in the air resolves it into water and it distills down in drops; that is, every snowflake becomes a drop. Similarly, it often happens that they begin high up, where they cannot be so quickly resolved because of the "Cold Cellar" <note>the freezing upper atmosphere</note>; but as they approach the earth in the lowlands, they resolve into water. Thus it also happens that summer stars—that is, summer rain-stars—become active in winter and break forth. <margin>C</margin> These do not let themselves out unless the winter stars are at their weakest; then they fall down and give summer rain. And even if the Icy stars intervene, they cannot coagulate anything while falling, only when freezing upon the earth. For it is not as people say, that the rain is turned into and formed as snow by the winter. The reason is: the snow-stars have their own particular "Tree" <note>source or lineage</note> from which they come; therefore, it [the rain] is nothing [to them]. Also, even if a frost were to occur there, nothing would come of it but a frozen water, which is not snow. Snow comes from its "Mother" <note>originating substance</note> and was never water. Thus you now understand the origin of the "error" in the growth of the stars on both sides, in summer and in winter. But where such errors do not occur, in those places the winters are at their coldest and the summers at their hottest. I shall leave this for now and entrust it to the <term>Astronomers</term>.

Now there is yet another kind of winter star which gives <term>hailstones</term> <note>original: "Grandines"</note> and <term>gems</term> <note>original: "Gemmas"</note>; these are not snow, but coagulated waters, and yet they were also never water in their First Matter as they were born. These same stars have a special circle to travel, and they are such stars that they give their hailstones and gems in summer and winter, in all four seasons of the year, regardless of the land's nature, constellation, moon, or wind-stars. At the times of snow in winter they do not come, nor in any common rain as mentioned in the preceding chapter; rather, they come only in summer and winter times when they have cold and wind from themselves, and when no other contrary force stands against them. For their generation cannot happen in mild, soft, or gentle weather, but only in rough weather, and at rough...

For they give off a cold from the earth so that they may be well recognized by such cold, although they are also born more slowly or more swiftly. Take this as an example: if a cold Sulphur that is wet, a cold Saltpeter that is fatty, and a Mercury that is mild are taken together into a mixture, and these three are to go together into one <term>Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> so that nothing remains but <term>Unity</term> <note>original: "Vnitas"</note>: they are in the beginning so <term>Contrary</term> that it takes a long time before they enter into one another, with hissing, bubbling, thundering, and similar <margin>B</margin> turbulence. So it is also in the heavens in such stars, that these same things are even more and higher in their nature than the earthly ones: therefore, their essence and manifestation are also more turbulent. When they now go toward <term>Perfection</term>, two natures separate from one another: the one into the <term>Solidified</term> <note>original: "Coagulatum"</note>, from which the Gems are made; the other into the <term>Dissolved</term> <note>original: "Resolutum"</note>, from which rain is made. And with both comes a specific wind, cold, and turbulence. Thus the star casts it out into the <term>Cellar of the Air</term> <note>the middle region of the atmosphere</note>; in this same place, one part dissolves and falls upon the earth as rain; the other part solidifies—for it has the <term>Vulcan of Solidification</term> <note>original: "Vulcanum coagulationis"</note> within it—and it makes that same body, which does not dissolve, into spheres, large and even larger, depending on how large the matter is; from this, Hail is now made.

Likewise, know about the "Tearing," that is, about <term>Hail</term> <note>original: "Grandinibus"</note>; they are also made thus: sometimes with rain, sometimes not. If it is with rain, it happens exactly as was said above. But if it becomes Hail, it is equal to the aforementioned Gems: only that such violent <term>force</term> is not present. For that same cold Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt are not so coarse or so highly graduated in their <term>impetus</term>. Although they produce wind and cold, it is not of the same nature as the Gems. Now, in such stars there are always two kinds: rain and small stones, as mentioned. That is to say, they have a "twin nature" within them: one of winter, the other of summer. That is: because of the rain they are summer stars, and because of the <term>Solidification</term> <note>original: "Coagulation"</note> they are winter stars. And they also have their own specific path, different from other stars, to manifest in winter or in summer. Those in winter are mild and sweet, like the snow; therefore, they have a <term>Spirit</term> and a <term>First Matter</term> of the summer nature, and one of the winter nature, working through their <term>Vulcan</term> on their affairs. They are like <term>Hermaphrodites</term> <note>original: "Hermaphroditæ"; entities possessing two contrary natures</note>, striking into both kinds—at one moment <margin>C</margin> they can be wintery, then summery. For that which is cold should have no thunder within it, nor any <term>Force</term>; but that which stands in the heat has it. Thus they are two <term>Contraries</term>, working together, bound in unity.

The birth of Snow is solely an ordained creation of God, who thus wills to be seen in his works in many and manifold ways. Just as the time must be right in the earthly <term>Vulcan</term> to give his fruits toward autumn, for all things are placed distinctly into an order. Therefore, as soon as they come out from before the star, they <term>Granulate</term> and <term>Drop</term> in sparks—that is, in snow-sparks—and fly upon the earth, for they have a mild and gentle nature. In this manner, it also happens that often a wind precedes them: for the reason that perhaps <term>hailstones</term> <note>original: "Grandinis"</note> were being formed, which are not entirely of a hail-like nature, but almost so because of their cause. Therefore, it is possible for no one to do a thing without those same tools which give and can give it; the heavens are something special there, and create a different nature than is possible in the other elements. Note therein that the description of why and how a snow, why and how a hail [forms], is not necessary to know, for as it is written: God has created it so that it should happen; it is not for man to know, except what man makes himself—that he may know, how and when.

# Eight Chapters.

A The more it is with a smoke: as then the <term>Arch</term> <note>original: "Arch" - likely referring to the primary essence or "archetype" of the matter</note> of these matters is. But when the perfection begins, so that at that place the <term>Massa</term> <note>the bulk or "mass" of the elemental matter</note> turns into a <term>Strall</term> <note>a beam or bolt of lightning</note>, in such a way that it perfects itself in its mass: then know that this same mass is nothing else but like a primordial force, well-fastened and enclosed, like a spirit that has neither body, blood, nor flesh. Now it follows that the other <term>Gewölcke</term> <note>clouds</note> that are alongside this one are born solely for <term>Regen</term> <note>rain</note>, the resolution of themselves into a <term>Wasser</term> <note>water</note>. And when now this <term>Resolution</term> <note>the process of dissolving or changing state</note> begins, so also begins the <term>Wind</term> and <term>Imperius</term> <note>commanding force or power</note> throughout the mass, and no clouds are born except for the <term>Tempestat</term> <note>storm/tempest</note> and to complete the discord. Now when the mass that lies in the shell feels the moisture from the clouds, so that the <term>Nässur</term> <note>wetness/moisture</note> comes to the mass, it is just as if one poured water into <term>Glockenspeise</term> <note>bell metal - a molten alloy of copper and tin</note> or the like. It happens now that the water touches the mass, then it breaks apart into all parts of the world, and gives a certain bang, a heavenly speed and agility: and from that moment, as many pieces as break, so many <term>Donner</term> <note>thunders</note> occur, every bang a thunder: in the same thunder there comes a thunder that goes from the bang, and because it strikes, the bang goes with the thunder.

When now such has happened, then this same mass strikes <term>Fewr</term> <note>fire</note> out toward its height, that is, toward the earth, as if at a target: as it first felt the opening, it goes there, forward and not backward, for it breaks open forward, not backward. Thereupon know now, when it comes out, it is recognized where it is: namely, a <term>Corpus</term> <note>body</note> that is nothing but a fire brought into a small mass, larger or smaller according to its nature: which body is compacted together, and thus <term>Spiritualisch</term> <note>spiritual</note>, <term>Aerisch</term> <note>aerial</note>, and <term>Etherisch</term> <note>ethereal</note>, so that from such a nature comes such a <term>Generation</term> <note>production/creation</note> that no one can contradict that it passes through everywhere like a spirit that has neither body, blood, nor flesh: no one can sufficiently describe or say its passage. Added to this is such a fast
B <term>Strich</term> <note>stroke/path</note> with such power that everything that is there must go to the ground and give way. And such a fire is so highly <term>Perhennisch</term> <note>perennial/ever-burning</note> that in a moment it brings all iron it touches into flux <note>melts it</note>: thereby is seen how high its operations are and how strong against the other elements, which are as nothing: with such strength and speed, no different than the nearest earthly thing: thereby shall be understood the coming of Christ, which is signified through it. For especially, and so wonderful an essence is in it, that it cannot be sufficiently contemplated nor known by a man. And Christ will also come in such a form and in such a way. He who considers this—that the lightning bolt shall be an example—he should never sin, nor deviate from the way. And their coming is more and more frequent, which cannot be without significance.

Then pay close attention to the strange nature of the lightning bolts. Some are
C <term>gewormen</term> <note>warmed/heated</note>, except only in that they lack <term>His</term> <note>heat/warmth</note>: in conclusion, they fall into <term>Coagulation</term> <note>solidification</note>, and their coagulation is <term>Fix</term> <note>stable/permanent</note>, and other <term>Emarum</term> <note>likely a corruption of 'humors' or 'vapors'</note> are not fixed; this one, however, is fixed and constant: and it receives this fixation from its own <term>Spiritu</term> <note>spirit</note>, which coagulates itself in the fluidity into a fixed body. Now know, however, that they often break and melt metals and do nothing to leather: that they often strike men dead and no one sees anything: that they often melt the lead in windows and do nothing to the glass: that they often burn the skulls and do nothing to the hair: that they burn <term>Bertzichen</term> <note>likely 'parchment' or 'garments'</note> and singe them away entirely, and nothing happens to the feathers. That they strike a horse dead through a saddle, and nothing happens to the saddle. That they often
D burn a coat and nothing happens to the body: that they often melt money in a locked chest and nothing happens to the wood. It is possible for no one to write of the wonders of the lightning bolt. I, for my part, can find such a natural cause in this: that it is an example to us that CHRIST will also come so wonderfully, that the broken reed he will not quench <note>a biblical reference to Matthew 12:20</note>, but that it is indeed that same thing. Or use <term>Ritust</term> <note>rites/rituals</note>: or the <term>Teufel</term> <note>Devil</note> must do such things. However, I remain with the first, and because Christ has placed himself in the example, thus to come here and to judge, who especially above all human reason performs special signs here, so wonderfully, that quickly and wonderfully his <term>Archeilauch</term> <note>divine rule/majesty</note> will come to pass.

Now, however, in the beginning of this <term>Meteorischen beschreibung</term> <note>meteorological description</note> I mention the <term>Pennates</term>, that is, the <term>Superos</term> <note>celestial beings/higher powers</note> in the <term>Firmament</term> <note>the heavens</note>: those same ones are now those who are masters in such work, to prepare them and be nimble, and are those who lead and point the lightning bolt; they are <term>Büchsenmeister</term> <note>master gunners/artillerymen</note> and aim the artillery, namely to where CHRIST wants: namely into that which is not in the way of God, namely into the enemies of God and not into the friends. For that is proven in the example, that CHRIST does no one wrong, only saying: Go away, you damned, into the eternal fire. Therefore such are <term>Praelagia</term> <note>omens/preludes</note>, not only the lightning bolt, but every weather that acts so violently—thunder, wind, hail, showers—everything is comprised here. Therefore look to those whom it hits; <term>Sodoma</term> and <term>Gomorrha</term> will also be hit, etc. They are grave omens.

### CHAPTER IX.
### ON EXTRANEOUS THINGS.

<margin>B</margin>Furthermore, it is also necessary to know regarding generation <note>the birth or production of things</note> that sometimes frogs, worms, or other living creatures are born from above and found falling down. Know then, as I mentioned at the beginning regarding the animals in the heavens, that there is no element that does not have within it a living creature—that is, of many kinds. Just as there are many kinds of worms in the earth, and many kinds in the water, and likewise in the air: so it is also in the firmament. For no one should marvel at this; Nature is a mother in the elements, among the upper ones and the others. From this it follows, when it is said that it has rained frogs, that such frogs are from the firmament, and in the firmament their like were born of such frogs. For certain reasons they have come to earth, just as the example shows that often moles <note>original: *Schermäuse*</note> come out of the earth and run about, though that is not their usual way; the nature of certain worms is similar. Thus, it is no less true that such are also found in the heavens, which come out of their region. Although it is not possible for something to fall down upon us from above—for it is "upwards" to them, just as if we were to fall up into heaven—it is indeed possible that they fall down, but to them it is "up," as is the nature of the heavens. Yet it cannot happen unless a storm causes such destruction in those places, and in that same impetus they fall down, thus coming into the rain or similar conditions. It is also the case that <term>Sperm</term> <note>meaning "seed" or "generative matter"</note> falls down in the time of May, from which tree-frogs are formed: for all tree-frogs are in the firmament, falling down in the manner of sperm, and growing below to their full maturity. And not only frogs, but more of such forms, which do not fall down physically; for that reason, a creature is often found in a place where its parents never went. This is solely the fault of the firmament in some cases; in others, the air is a cause, which has such forms within it just as well as the earth or water. Such is the birth of **Basilisks**, and many new, unheard-of animals whose origins are without earthly mothers, contrary to all other animals of the earth and water.

<margin>D</margin>It is also no less true that it often happens that people say it is raining blood: this is how it occurs. Those things which are of <term>Sulphur</term> <note>one of the three prime substances in Paracelsian alchemy</note> and the "Three Primes" often happen to turn into the dawn-redness <note>original: *Morgenröthi*</note>, as they are a foam of Sulphur; and the tenacity of the Three Primes is boiled down <note>original: *decoquiret*</note> and comes out in the manner of a foam: as was said of the dawn, that it is a light foam. Now, when that same foam enters into a mucilage or a bituminous nature, then that is the <term>Star</term> <note>original: *Astrum*</note>, and it sends that which becomes the real thing. For its color is red, and the thickness of blood, a little more or less. When it is thus prepared and transmuted, the heavens let it fall: for the heavens bear no tangible body—that is, everything must be separated from them. Thus it distills itself down, sometimes by itself, sometimes in a rain, as it happens. The frogs in the firmament are not substance, but they *become* substance, and so they fall down. Likewise, much happens with foams and similar exhalations, that they are incorporated into colors just as they are in their own colors, and thus the same color falls down: white, blue, black, etc. For the water that rains from heaven is not of one color, but has distinctions from one another. It often happens in certain mountains that it rains milk, in the same manner as the blood. That which falls upon the stones creates a white bituminous <unclear>vñream</unclear>, which in time coagulates and hardens, just like a stone that had grown upon another. And such heavenly <unclear>vñez</unclear> are of many kinds in all colors: red (that is, of blood), green, blue, black, yellow, etc. That which falls into the earth disappears in the water as well; also, much in the rain is broken up in its color, so that they cannot come to the earth as they are in themselves. It is no less true that the old <term>Naturalists</term> <note>original: *Naturales*</note> attempted much with such <unclear>vñneiß</unclear> in medicine and also in alchemy, wherever they could obtain them: and they called them **Heavenly Flowers** <note>original: *Flores Cœlestes*</note>. But what was accomplished with them is hidden from me—namely something, for their speculations were well-grounded. I mean the true Naturalists, not **Aristotle**.

# Chapter Eight

<margin>A</margin>
Furthermore, fire is sometimes seen to rain down, which occurs for the following reason. All rain that exists is nothing other than Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury <note>These are the 'Tria Prima' or three primary substances in Paracelsian alchemy, representing soul, body, and spirit.</note>. But the fire takes away [instantly] what **Nature** for itself cannot do in many years. But concerning the **iron** that falls back down, note such a nature: that same **ethereal magnet** draws the iron to itself as if grasped; then, because it is not fixed, it transmutes it into a rust for which that same magnet has prepared it. And everything that stands in **humidity**, and the like, and what on Earth can be [reduced] to a humidity and **putrefy**, that is all [drawn up], like rotten wood and other rotten things, until nothing more is there. [These are] not [common things], but **points** <note>specific occurrences</note> that happen **meteoric-wise**, to [reveal] them. Nature is wonderful in her works, and strange and great, ordained and gifted by **God**. And experience gives the visible proof: as does the **light of Nature**, which reveals itself and [leads] man in such [knowledge]. For nothing is so secret that it shall not be revealed, nothing so small that [it shall not be known]; that is, in man's understanding and recognition.

# Tenth Chapter
#### CHAPTER X.
### ON EXHALATIONS.

Now note further that the stars purify themselves; summer and winter stars do not do so with a single body—that is, they cast a body away from themselves, which is called "star-shot" <note>original: *Sterngeschoß*; likely referring to meteors or "star jelly," a gelatinous substance traditionally thought to be deposited on earth by falling stars</note>. Now its origin is thus: they have their nourishment in the firmament, by which they maintain themselves from that same element. And just as with food and drink, there is no intake without an excretion <note>original: *Excrementum*</note>. Now it follows that they are sustained by nothing but fire, just as man is by his blood and flesh. Whatever is not of the essence is cast off. So, when the stars have their usual time to cast their excrement from them: if it happens by day, no one sees it; if it happens by night, it is seen. It is a fiery star that falls down from the heaven of the stars, but one does not see how high it falls; rather, it only comes down into the lower heavens in the air, where it becomes visible and falls to the ground. Now it is no less true that many stars purify themselves in other ways, so that fire does not go forth in that manner, and yet it is fire, but invisible. Therefore, many cast their star-shot; much also goes away in the rain, much in the cloudburst, for these same weather patterns are the purgings of the stars, moving them toward an exit. But those that become fiery are just like one who drinks water, from whom water goes forth again: so they drink fire, and fire goes forth from them again. But as soon as it touches the earth, it is a jelly and a slime, like red-colored or yellow-colored frog spawn.

For just as the element of water has many sea-worms in it, and the air many strange worms, the air many strange beetles and gnats: so also does the heaven. These are the true Salamanders, born out of the fire of burning sulfur. And it is one of the four wonders in the four elements; they are cattle and animals of Olympus <note>original: *O'ympißind*; referring to the celestial realm</note> and are intelligent like the cattle in the water, endowed with a certain understanding. As soon as they settle there, they are not fiery to look at; but whenever they come, they are fiery again. And as soon as they become fiery again, they also shine. They also have a sleep and rest, in which sleep they do not shine: only in the motion when they fly.

# ON METEORS

Thus, not only in the Sun and Moon, but also in other suitable stars, they make another star, a new one, or the like; they also create many such strange types in the heavens, all of which is their work.

<margin>A</margin>

And so it often happens that two appear, which are *Gemini* <note>The Twins</note>, signifying a rain twice as long as a single one signifies by itself. These are provided and ordained by Divine Providence in such a manner. For there is nothing that does not produce a blossom: The lightning is a blossom of the weather and of many more fruits, and there are many blossoms that we cannot see and have no knowledge of, because they consume themselves in the air and pass away. ## BOOK ONE.

### Concerning the Rainbow.

<note>The following section begins with a large decorative initial J or I featuring an ornate border and a mask.</note>

The birth and origin of the rainbow is exactly like the birth of women. For in the same way that women must have their time for their fruit, so too must a rainbow. Likewise, just as it happens that sometimes one rainbow appears, sometimes two, and sometimes even three: that is for the same reason as when a woman brings forth more than one child. Both are understood by the same principles.

<margin>B</margin>
Know also of its path, that there are some that run exactly with the "water-stars" <note>Stars associated with the element of water</note>—that is, alongside them; some outside of them; some in the length of the Zodiacal Circle, and the like. Furthermore, know that they come at unequal times: some are situated in winter, some in summer time. Just as a woman may give birth at any hour, so it is to be known here also; for they have no fixed autumn or harvest, but only when their conjunctions <note>The alignment of celestial bodies</note> arrange themselves, then comes the time of their birthing.

Although it happens that a hundred of them are not seen, the reason is this: they require a tempered environment in which to be born. That is, not too dry, nor too wet; not too cold, nor too warm; but in the middle. For this reason, whatever rainbows exist in winter times are frozen by the cold and broken in their birth. Likewise, those in summer times, when the sun is clear and dry, are parched and burnt up. Therefore, such are not seen, otherwise there would be a rainbow every day. But in the mornings, and in the evenings, and during stormy times, when a "temperature" <note>A balanced state of the elements</note> exists, then they have their joy and time for birthing.

Although rainbows have their name solely because they are meant to signify rain, the reason is that they choose to exist at such a time, and at other times they are dried up or frozen. They tend toward rain, but in the manner stated above. Therefore, just as the births of women are, so are these; and as those signify nothing <note>Likely meaning they are natural occurrences rather than omens of doom</note>, so do these.

The rainbows take their colors from the Salt of the Fire; for they are from the element of fire—colors, and no weather. And as you see a fire cast [light] differently—green, yellow, blue, brown, etc., red, etc.—not mixed among one another, but appearing freely, distinct next to each other: so the rainbow divides its colors, which it possesses by the power of the Salt-spirit <note>The crystalline or formative principle in alchemy</note> dwelling in the element of fire. For such is its nature and innate property.

<page-num>97</page-num>
<header>BOOK ONE.</header>

Regarding its form and shape, know this: as you see that all things are directed into a form, such as Man, cattle, herbs, trees, stones, etc. It is not possible for the Philosophers to discover why they are made so. Although we may understand the confusion regarding Man—for which reason many have eyes and tongues—we understand even less about other created things, except solely that they have pleased God in such a manner.

Thus, consider how He has given form to the roses and the lilies <note>original: "Gilgen"</note>: in which forms nothing useful happens except for the wonder before one's eyes. Man's form is required by necessity; these, however, are not. So it would also be that their form proceeded from their Property <term>Eygenschafft: the inherent occult quality or "signature" of a thing</term>, so that it were a single thing: that which cannot lose its form and remain itself, nor can the form break while the Property remains. Thus, just as the star goes into the form of the seed, and so with time into its fruit: so the rainbow grows into its form, invisible in the lower firmament, until it fulfills the forty weeks. Then, when the hour of its birth is at hand, a tempered weather is present, and it reveals itself and becomes perfect in its form and colors, as the nature of the fire has made it.

Now, its stay is not long: for as all things have their time of life, so it is here also. A very quick adversity breaks it: nevertheless, it exists for a time, though some stand longer and some shorter. This is because a time may take a breaking. Just as a child and a year-old man <note>likely meaning a man of years/age</note>, when they die, how far apart do they stand? Also compared to a forty-year-old? Now the nature is such that every rainbow stands with its feet on the earth, just as it is lowered into the air or urged upon a flower that grows upward with its leaves: so all upper Impressions <term>Impressiones: celestial influences or atmospheric phenomena</term> are directed downward. That which is "down" to them is "up" to us; for when the roots are above, the growth must stand downward—that is, from their soil, and not into their soil.

### Concerning the Figures that appear strangely in the Heaven.

<margin>B</margin>
Oftentimes strange forms and figures present themselves in the heaven: now in the likeness of a man, now an animal, now this way, then that, in a strange and unheard-of manner. Such a procreation is natural in the firmament: for from the stars they take their body and matter <note>original: "Corpus vnnd Materiam"</note>, and from the same they also take their form. But as you see that among men deformities <note>original: "Mißgewächs," literally "mis-growths"</note> grow into strange shapes and beings which cannot be described except for their total deformity: so in this way the figures in the heaven are deformities—some from the rainbow, some from dry clouds, some from the mixing of such forms together. Just as when three or various kinds of seed <note>original: "Sperma"</note> are poured together, a monster <note>original: "Monstrum"</note> is produced: so also there are mixings of the stellar seeds. When the bodies then come together, a single mixture results in its form: with that, they break, each one the other: thus forms are produced from it which no one can indicate or predict, from the aforementioned mixing. Therefore, such forms should not be taken as strange or as something miraculous <note>original: "Miraculs"</note>, nor as a prophecy: for many such errors of nature occur.

Therefore, every rainbow that fails in itself becomes a cloud with its colors, in a strange way—red, green, yellow, etc.—and with a strange form among other clouds in the heaven. Where such clouds are seen, it is solely a deformity of the rainbow, whether by day or night.

### Concerning Lances.

<margin>A</margin>
It also happens that sometimes "games" <note>likely referring to "Chasmata" or "Sky Games," optical phenomena like the Aurora or mock suns</note> occur, and such forms: when rainbow colors run into them, it is solely a deformity of a rainbow—that is, it goes into the ground seldom; it goes into the length, sometimes separates from one another, and makes more than one piece out of it: sometimes spheres and the like, as it is the nature of every thing to break. For who will or can describe the broken thing individually? How strange, or in what shape its pieces become? Sometimes they loom like castles, sometimes like churches, sometimes like plates, and other such things, as it happens in the breaking. Therefore, man should not look too deeply into such failed things: for they happen on the earth as well, in all things where deformities are encountered. So the figures just mentioned are solely broken rainbows, and that same body, color, and essence: as it then separates from one another and breaks, not only in form but also in color. They also have a different age—that is, they may live as long as the nature of the rainbow allows.

There also occur sometimes bright figures and forms in the heaven, as sometimes a new moon, or a likeness of a monster, or some other form, as seen above, like fires. This takes its origin from the stars "shooting" in that way. As you see that the stars purify themselves and throw a fiery streak down upon the earth: these are natural, for it is their bloom, like a tree that pushes out its flowers. And just as the stars have a small glow, so also does their "blood" <note>original: "Geblüte"</note> as long as it lives. That is, as you see that the glowing worms <note>glow-worms</note> have their starlight by night, but not by day. Those that are always living have them: so this star-creature also; it shines as long as it lives: that is, as soon as it comes to the earth, it is extinguished, and...

## Concerning Night-Harm, or the Night-Wind.

Know also that by night the heavens purify themselves more than by day. From this it follows that "Night-Harm" <note>German: *Nachtschaden*; a term for illnesses or blights believed to be caused by harmful night air or spirits</note> and similar things occur by night, which do not exist by day. Just as you see that thunder, hail, showers, etc., come from the heavens: when such a raging occurs, it is a poisonous purification falling down from the stars, poisoning wherever it lands. From this it follows that the SALAMITA <note>A Paracelsian term for a specific type of elemental spirit or force associated with the air and fire</note> of such poisonous air—wherever he may seize it—mixes himself into it. He leads it according to his nature: before houses, into stables to the cattle, and even before windows if something is sticking out. Therefore, this does not happen every time; it only happens when he can have such poisonous air, which he then carries about. From this it follows that in those people whom he has afflicted, "Blood-Erysipelas" <note>German: *Blutterysen*; likely referring to Erysipelas or "St. Anthony's Fire," a skin infection</note> grows, along with many similar strange diseases which are called Night-Harm; thus they are naturally born from the heavens and led by the Salamita to the places where he may do damage. If he always had such matter, he would also do it at the highest point in the firmamental course with knowledge.

## Concerning Comets.

The origin of comets is a special growth that comes from no mother, nor from any seed, but is a composite of the stars. The reason is: they <note>the stars/heavens</note> know the future course of our luck, misfortune, death, or dying; war or famine. From this it follows that when they wish to reveal such things, for reasons lying within them, they form a star which they take from the heavens and make from it a figure and a shape that is strange and wondrous to behold. They lead it through the air, high or low, as they then signify the future to the people, according to the content of that thing, whatever news it may be. Regarding this, know that the arrival of comets is indicated by the movements of those same stars, as if they had it from Nature. For such a manner is in the spirits <note>German: *Gehyst*, likely *Geist*</note> to signify through prefiguration. These are the pieces that do not concern the regular course of the heavens: that is, what will happen will be recognized as if it were from Nature. Therefore, such soothsayers are of two kinds: those who indicate the future of the stars, which then concerns the elements; and others who work against the course—that is, they undertake it without knowledge of the course—such as death, birth, etc. This happens by the nature of comets and not from the regular course of the heavens.

->CONCERNING FROGS.<-

Furthermore, know that it often rains frogs, worms, and the like from the sky: the origin of these is as follows. When the *spermata* <note>The "seeds" or formative essence of living things</note> of worms, snakes, adders, toads, etc., lie in the earth, and a rain or a frost, rime, etc., falls into them—as such an accident may happen from above—this *spermata* is hindered from proceeding into its generation and is thus broken. Subsequently, this *spermata* enters into decay; that is, every thing that is broken must decay. Then, when the frost passes away, or whatever accident befell it, it begins to rot. From this decay grow "misgrowths" <note>deformities</note>, partly resembling those animals, but they are perverted monsters. These are the ones said to have "rained down," for people do not know their origin, and for such reasons they are regarded as having been rained.
Although *spermata* also come from the stars in heaven and fall upon the earth, from which similar things are seen to grow as if they had fallen from heaven: this happens in this way. All the leaves, or wood, or grasses in which pests grow and eat the leaves, likewise the seeds from which caterpillars or other wood-worms or tree-worms emerge. Wherever such seeds and *spermata* lie, visible or invisible, and astral rains fall upon them, some of those seeds grow into monsters while the rain is still wet. For through these rains it is revealed where such genera of frogs and other things are.
Thus, in these things you shall know nothing else but that where such animals grow, none of the *spermata* of the worms have crawled down and through the decaying refreshment...

# ON METEORS <note>original: "DE METEORIS"</note>

Rain, when transmuted, becomes a worm or another animal, according to how the monster <note>In this context, "monster" refers to a marvelous or unnatural biological omen</note> may form. Sometimes it begins from one rain to another, or to a third, and so on, until finally it breaks out all at once and comes forth, just as if they had only arrived at that hour with the same rain that was previously mentioned as the beginning.

### ON BLOOD. <note>original: "DE SANGVINE"</note>
It also often happens that "blood-water"—that is, rain almost like blood—falls. This is quite rare, yet it occurs because the "star-shoots" <note>likely referring to meteorites or gelatinous "star jelly" believed to fall from the sky</note> mix themselves into the rain and fall down with it. When these star-drops fall upon the earth or cold stones, they color themselves red or liver-colored, yet in themselves they are as clear as water; but in the mixing with the earth, they take on their colors.

They also often come from rainbows, so that they are resolved into water. Since rainbows contain all colors, they then send those same colors to the earth with the rain. Such colored rain is seen specifically where rainbows stand in the rain and are large and strong. When they begin to dissolve, they vanish away with the rain. In those places, if one catches the rain with fine white cloths, the colors will be found upon them, provided that not too much rain falls and washes it away again. Although not all rainbows turn to water, for they are of the air <note>original: "luptisch," likely a variant of "luftisch" (airy)</note>; however, the large ones standing in the rain have a watery nature in them, which is why they dissolve.

### ON CROSSES & FIGURES IM-
pressed upon Tunics and Skins. <note>original: "DE CRVCIBVS & FIGVRIS impressis super Tunicis & Cutibus"</note>
Know also that from such colors as described above, the drops—if they catch upon fine cloths and are not overwhelmed by too much rain—make little crosses in the cloths. This is caused by the way the drops fall according to the thread of the fabric and the like. Thus, people are frightened, and also because it is the nature of water to float and fall from a beautiful sky without becoming rain; or rather, individual drops fall, and wherever they land, they make spots or stains, originating from the stars as stated above. Although they come rarely, it happens commonly every day, but they are consumed or washed away by the rain so that they are not noticed.

From such colors, the *Salamica* <note>A Paracelsian elemental spirit or force associated with the atmosphere; likely a variant of "Salamander" or a specific meteorological spirit</note> takes its power and paints crosses on people's clothes, or pillars, whips, buffaloes, and the like, just as was said above regarding the lightning-bolt and the dragon. Now, if such a drop should fall, whatever color it may be, it creates a "painting" <note>original: "Gemeide"</note> upon it, so that one is troubled or wonders at it—each one different from the other—and looks only for spiritual things, which is to say, looking for significant causes.

No one should wonder at such falling colors, for they are manifold, as you see them in the rainbow, in the wilderness, and in the stars. Also, if a color should fall that is not of their firmament, know that decay gives colors; that is, when such a thing becomes rotten—like wood that is white, but when it rots, it becomes green and yellow, etc. Such generation also exists in these things, which the *Salamita* <note>variant of Salamica</note> heeds and carries hither and thither.

### ON LITTLE STONES. <note>original: "DE LAPILLIS"</note>
Likewise, stones are often formed from rain; that is, as you see, all stones are made hard and coagulated by salt. Similarly, all wood and whatever else is there is made compact and corporeal by salt, and without it, nothing can become hard. From this it follows that when the salts dissolve in the heavens and fall down, if they catch onto something they can penetrate or permeate, they then harden in that thing and turn it into stones or the like according to its nature. As you see, if you place pure salt in water and put peas, lentils, or beans into it. Similarly, it often happens that beans, peas, and lentils harden and become misshapen, not as they should be; this happens for the reason mentioned. Also, all rot that grows in fruit comes from the rain, which has such transmuting properties within it.

It also happens sometimes that the seed—that is, when peas or lentils are sown in the earth—also turns to stone. This happens because in that same field or soil there is a "salt-bloom" <note>efflorescence of salt</note> running through the field. When sowing occurs there and rain comes which dissolves the salt-bloom, then whatever was sown is turned into stone—that is, made equal to the salt. And when salt-blooms are dissolved by rain, whatever lies therein or whatever they can catch—wood or otherwise—they turn into the nature of stone. There are also certain wells that have such a nature, which also take their power from such salt-blooms.

# BOOK TWO
### CONCERNING THE STONE FROM HEAVEN.

<margin>A</margin> In the heights of the firmament <note>The sphere of the stars and upper atmosphere</note>, where the first three <note>Likely referring to the Tria Prima: Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt</note> lie—as indicated in the beginning of the Theory—they grow and originate. These same first three are so high that we cannot see their form, yet they possess form, as stated in the Theory; we [perceive] only their colors. Thus, it follows that in the element of Fire <note>The region above the air</note> these also exist, and whatever stones are generated there, those same stones fall down. And [this is] unheard of and happens rarely, yet it occurs more on the sea than on [land]. Such stone generations are in the way. As you know, the thunder grows, and it is a star, as is evident. Now, if the beginnings of such thunder are there, and it is possible and natural, then the bolt <note>original: "Straal" - referring to a lightning bolt or "thunderstone"</note> of such generations comes: that is, as often as there is a bang, so often is there a particular star. Now, if many reasons <note>or "principles"</note> went together into one generation, they all become one star, also in its form and nature, as it is then recognized there. Thus, it cannot go toward a great storm. For the reason is, this generation happens too quickly and falls out of the air as soon as it is coagulated—to be understood as when water freezes; it is at first soft, and when [it hardens]. Thus the matter is at first only an airy work, and like water beginning to coagulate: and as soon as it is hardened, it is no longer airy, but earthy <note>original: "Terrisch"</note>: and then it must fall.

<margin>B</margin> Upon this, it is possible that such matters come together without any use, and join themselves together above all courses in heaven, and by their nature come together and create another hardness. Like lead that is melted, as soon as [it cools] it is hard in an instant. Such matters are in the firmament of Fire; [while they] have their like, they remain airy: but as soon as a contrary or foreign [element] falls into them, it becomes something else and is no longer airy. As you know regarding rain, while it is a cloud it does not [fall], it is only in the heights: but as soon as it takes the foreign conjunction and allows itself to dissolve, then it becomes water and rains, and can no longer remain in its height, but must fall. Thus are the matters in heaven, of a thundering nature, that is, upon the bolt. There are others like them, which, when a contrary element enters, also become stone.

---

### CONCERNING METALS.

<margin>C</margin> Likewise, such a nature of metals floats in the element of Fire in heaven, just as the metals [on earth]: and yet it is a metal such as no one can recognize. Know that the fiery bolts with the heat-lightning are solely metals, harder than iron or steel, and fluid like copper, and of other colors, and shaped like a bolt. Such a thing is in heaven just as well as on the earth. But [just as] nothing falls up from the things below, so nothing falls down from the upper things, except [what is] explored in the elements, and through a miracle or strange joining together, from which a body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is formed. Strange things also fall down, if it were possible for us to join them in the upper vault. Know then, if the saltpeter-star and the sulfur-star were joined together with equal arrangement, many such impressions <note>A term for atmospheric phenomena like meteors or lightning</note> would fall upon us. But they are not arranged in that way; you should know that stones fall and contain metals, which have their birth like the bolts.

The great stone at Ensisheim <note>A famous meteorite that fell in 1492 in Alsace</note> in the Sundgau, weighing one hundred weight <note>original: "j.C. Schwer"</note>, was formed from the matter of the stone-bolts, so that over a hundred conjunctions of the bolts came together there, and [it was like] poured-out molten silver: so quickly did this material body fall, as its [shape] indicates with its humps and forms, that it stood in all its heat and puffed out, and cooled in the same; and what is there was all boiling hot. If something from that region comes into the cold, it is purely [solid] and hardens and falls. But while it is in the [upper] fire, it [remains fluid]. But once it comes out of it and then coagulates, it must fall.

# BOOK THREE.
### CONCERNING THE WINDS.

<margin>S</margin> Know of the winds that they also have their roots and origin in the stars. For in the same way as there are certain stars that give snow, others rain, as is described in the whole of Meteorology <note>The study of atmospheric phenomena</note>. So also there are wind-stars, which give their natural wind and otherwise neither snow, rain, nor anything else. But if such snow or rain occurs [with it], that happens without the cause of the wind, unless the wind has carried it from one foreign land to another.

...through its strong blowing. Furthermore, know also that certain rains begin with wind; these will be indicated in their own chapter.

<margin>A</margin>
Regarding these winds, however—as nature alone reveals—know that they have no fixed number, as if one were to say there were only four <note>The author is refuting the classical Aristotelian view of four cardinal winds</note>. For this reason: the heavens are full of "wind-stars," positioned below and above the earth. Many a wind comes from the East into France that originated in Hungary, and many a wind comes into Thrace. Yet, such a wind is neither the West Wind <note>original: "Zephyrus"</note> nor the East Wind <note>original: "Eurus"</note>. Likewise, many a wind starts in the Alps and goes into Lombardy, or starts in the Alps and goes into Swabia. It is neither the South Wind <note>original: "Auster"</note> nor the East Wind; it is an Alpine wind.

Similarly, many a wind begins on one half of the sphere, such as in the southern parts <note>original: "Austri"</note>, and travels under the sphere into the northern parts <note>original: "Boreä"</note>, and over the sphere in that same region, being both South and North. Thus also the East Wind sometimes goes under the sphere through the path of the West Wind. But it is not the West Wind, but the East Wind. Conversely, many things happen with the others in our sky—that is, as far as we can see—where a wind rises for us and moves to one side. Its nature and name are therefore not to be understood according to the four winds. Naturally, however, one might categorize them such that all winds blowing toward him were "East," those at his back "West," and others at the sides "South" and "North," creating sub-categories according to his will. But just because he does so does not mean that is the reality.

<margin>B</margin>
Now it may happen that a wind comes upon us directly: for example, Switzerland or Swabia might have a wind coming from the South <note>original: "Mittag," literally midday</note>, while those in Lombardy or by the sea neither see nor hear of it. From whence comes this wind? It stands in the place where it begins. Although some believe a wind is like rain, which sometimes travels a hundred miles before it falls, the reason is this: the wind is not a cloud; it is born as soon as it comes out of its "hole." Thus it is certain in this way. Likewise, a wind may blow for 30 miles—a gust from a star—and go no further, and then dissipate. No wind can travel such a great distance unless it be the East Wind from the Orient—that is, coming across the sea to us in the Occident—or if "mid-stars" are present which drive them along so that everything is moved by winds. And there are not 4, nor 12. There are a thousand origins, and...

<margin>C</margin>
Now, concerning the strong winds that continue for a long time without change, they often bring rain through the North or the South. The wind is a "growth" of that region. Often from the South or the East—that is, in those same regions—judgment should be made as to whether it is a "pure-born" rain-wind, as described in such places. It may cause the land to become fruitful, or sour, or meager, or wormy, etc. For local rains are the natural rains of that land. But if such a rain is driven—timely or untimely—into a land that does not belong to that region, it causes damage to the fruits, growths, and whatever is therein. For every land has its ordained weather, rain, and air. Where this is disrupted, an incursion into those growths follows, and a corruption within them. This is the cause of difficult years, of bad fruit, and of everything that should not be and is against the nature of the land.

<margin>D</margin>
As stated above regarding the origin of winds, know that in them there are both helpful and adverse qualities. For there are many strange types of herbs upon which such differences can be observed. From these winds come particular diseases, rot, and the like. Now, all these winds should be understood according to their properties or their origin. Just as you see a tree blossom for 4 days, 6 days, or 3 days, more or less, so too is the duration of the winds; they must run their course in such time. One blows for 3 days, another for 1 day, 2 hours, 1 hour, etc., or for weeks or months. Just as all plants have their time for their "exaltations" <note>A term from alchemy/astrology meaning a state of peak power</note>, so these stars run with their winds—into this land or that, wherever each is directed—and each is different from the other in its distance, strength, and weakness. It is the same within the star from which the wind issues.

<margin>E</margin>
Thus the origin of the wind is this: in the star from which it comes, the wind is a "growth," just as a tree grows from the earth or as something grows overnight. Thus the wind is a growth upon the stars, though it differs in that it more closely resembles fire. You see that when wood lies together, it is ready for fire; then, when the fire is applied, it lasts as long as the wood remains. It follows that in the "wind-stars" it is just like fire. Therefore, know that in these stars lies the *materia* <term>materia: the physical substance or "fuel"</term> of the wind, just as if it were wood, and it is ignited upon the firmament; as long as it is there, the wind lasts. This *materia* is a firmamental **Sulphur**, **Mercury**, and **Saltpeter** <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary substances of Paracelsian alchemy</note>, yet not with rain or that kind of matter, but solely windy, in every way like the power of fire. All these things are a living, stirring growth that moves and can be perceived by the senses.

# BOOK FOUR

When the winds are thus ordained to grow and blow, they blow according to their directions. One toward the East, one toward the West, one toward the South, and the other toward the North, as it is. Sometimes a <term>wind-star</term> <note>original: "Windstern"; a celestial body believed to govern specific winds</note> stands over <term>Slavonia</term> <note>the Balkans/South Slavic region</note> and surpasses that land, and first settles down in <term>Austria</term>, and thereafter follows its path, just as they choose to go out. Some stand over <term>Swabia</term>, and shear away, and fall down into <term>Italy</term>. Some stand in <term>Poland</term>. Some over <term>Portugal</term>, and turn toward the sea. Some over <term>England</term>, and turn toward <term>Turkey</term>, and turn toward <term>Apulia</term> <note>Southern Italy</note>. Thus it is with all winds, that each has its line and its designated breadth. For as they come out of the stars, so they spread out. Like the branches on a tree, which spreads out above the earth much larger than it is within the earth.

Regarding this, know also that they are also warm and cold in form, according to their nature. For there are some cold ones that stand in the South, and some warm ones that stand in the East and West. Although the cold stars are more [frequent in the North] and the warm ones more in the South. Nevertheless, they should not be generally held as cold or warm for that reason: for they are mixed together. Although it is true that the hot stars in the North receive cold from their cold region, and those from the South receive heat from the sun: just as when snow melts and loses its coldness, or [water] freezes from the cold. Thus they lose their nature from external influences. But such is not always the case, but only by accident. According to this, however, no wind should be judged as cold or hot [only by its direction], but according to its innate nature and kind. For it is to be known that just as there are hot and cold herbs upon the earth, so also these wind-stars are to be understood in the same way.

<margin>B</margin>
Regarding winds, sometimes a great impetuous wind occurs, which is like a cloudburst in its path. As you see the fast [stars], so a star is often overtaken and falls out all at once, which otherwise [would take] a long time. So there are some stars that rarely produce wind; but when they do blow, a storm arises that tears houses and trees out by the roots. These arise [suddenly] upon the earth. Then, when it comes to the earth, it sweeps along it as long as it lasts and consumes itself. There are also many winds that always remain high in the heavens and do not come down. These are directed by their <term>emunctories</term> <note>original: "Emanctorien"; anatomical term for excretory organs, here used metaphorically for celestial vents</note> which are bound to the heights. And there is wind with one another, against one another, upon one another, each with its own punishment <note>or "force/drive"</note>, and according to its strength they sometimes mix together or repel one another, each driving the other away from itself, and thus [wandering] back and forth like one traveling across the land. But what comes to the earth is not contrary, seldom alone, but for the most part [multiple winds] move the earth or the sea with their tempests. So there are also some <term>summer-stars</term>, some <term>winter-stars</term>; this is to be reckoned the same as the <term>spring-stars</term> <note>original: "Kreutzern"; referring to the spring quarter</note>, and <term>autumn</term>, and <term>harvest</term>. Each has its time in which it especially brings something forth: so also the time has its stars, those in autumn, those in spring, etc., which become ripe. All are some cold, some warm, etc., as all things are made in their order.

### THE FOURTH BOOK
### CONCERNING THUNDER
### Of Lightning.

<margin>6</margin>
<image-desc>Large decorated initial 'V' at the beginning of the paragraph.</image-desc>
And as there is an origin among other <term>impressions</term> <note>original: "Impressionibus"; a Renaissance term for atmospheric phenomena</note> of the heavens, so know here also of <term>lightning</term> <note>original: "Himmlißen"; an archaic term for celestial flashing or lightning</note>, and that in this way. There are some stars that alone give off a smoke of <term>sulfur</term>, that is, a <term>vapor</term>. When this comes outside of its star and is driven by the wind in the middle-heaven, then [the lightning occurs]. But it vanishes in an instant, like a <term>spirit of wine of sulfur</term> <note>original: "Spiritus Vini Sulphuris"; an alchemical preparation of sulfur and alcohol</note>, or something else. The sun ignites it, and then it burns. But it vanishes in an instant, like a spirit of wine or another thing. Now when it burns up in this way, the lightning is also finished. Regarding this, know also that such lightning does not come from one star alone, but from many that have their course together and thus enter into one another. Moreover, often thirty lightnings come out of one star, in this manner: as often as a vapor goes out, there is a burning, because the vapor is often plentiful, and thus there is much burning. Know now here concerning this lightning, that it is the nature of the sun to ignite it in the heights and not at the bottom, that is, the lowest part. For often at the bottom there are rain-clouds, cold, etc., so that one might not see it. But when the vapor goes out of the star, it blows it down to the bottom: just as when one blows with the mouth against a wall. Now when this blowing has happened, and it is a sulfurous vapor, the sun is at the top of it and ignites it. Then, as large as the vapor is or goes, it burns, whether it be in water or in the clouds, wherever it is: just like a vapor of wine, which burns as far as it goes, no matter what it enters.
So also many such vapors occur at night; these are of another genus and kind, and in this way. As you see that the air [ignites] the spirit of sulfur and <term>salt</term> <note>original: "Salis"</note>, so here also in this place. Stars are of such a kind that when their vapor goes out, it has in the air...

As you see, when you mix the *Spirit of Salt* <note>hydrochloric acid</note> and *Sulphur* <note>sulfuric acid</note> etc. together in such a way, as soon as you pour it into the air, everything that has been poured out burns. From this it follows that the night, through its cold, moist air, ignites this sulphur and salt-spirit, and also produces "heaven-light" <note>lightning; original: "Himmlizen"</note> just like those during the day. And so it is a cycle, that these stars provide the summer, and it is from them here. And where these stars are not present, the sun can nevermore create a full, complete summer. Therefore, if many of these stars are in motion, and are strong and powerful, the summer will accordingly be hot or cold. ## Concerning Thunder in a Clear Sky.

<margin>B</margin>
Regarding this, know concerning thunder that it is also a star of such a kind that it creates a sound out of itself, and in this way: You see that nothing contrary can persist in its action. From this it follows that this star has within it a *Sulphur* and a *Saltpeter*; these two create the bubbling and thundering, thus. This "thunder-star," as stated above, has such a heat within it that it casts out all its *egestion* <note>waste or discharge</note> boiling: that is, as you see that in a pot there may be boiled *fixed Sulphur* and *fixed Salt*, and as soon as it comes into the air or into moisture, it begins to thunder and to rise up until it cools completely. So also here, when this *mucilage of Sulphur and Salt* <note>original: "Mucillago Sulphuris"</note> falls from the star and comes into the air, the saltpeter cannot remain with the sulphur: for its nature is such that when it senses moist air, it must thunder; likewise the sulphur when it is with it. Now when such a thing falls from the star and comes into the air, until it cools in the air, it trembles like an *earth-tremor* <note>earthquake; original: "Erdbidmen"</note> in the air and thunders. This thunder goes toward the earth and gives its resonance in the middle of the sky, where we hear it. But it is much higher than we can perceive. Thus this thunder lasts until it cools, then it becomes air—that is, it is turned to dust and carried by the wind. It is also its own nature that it drives itself, like a thing that flees its contrary as long as it lasts.

## Concerning the Storm.

Likewise with the storm <note>original: "Wetter"</note>: when such a star comes that provides the storm, know that the same is initially also from Sulphur and Salt. When it wishes to go out, and its harvest is ready, and its time to *purge itself* <note>original: "Emungiren"</note> has come, it first gives off its vapor like a boiling thing; thereafter this vapor gives off its lightning, be it day or night. For the sun does not ignite it, only the air: therefore it can be ignited by day or night. From this it follows that as the star thus discharges, the boiling must give off a vapor; the same, as far as it blows out, it flames and gives a lightning flash. Upon this, the star pours a "boil-off" out into the air; this discharge begins to thunder, just as when one throws molten silver into water, it thunders as long as it is in a state of boiling or heat. Thus it happens from such a star that a great number of such vapors may occur, and much "boil-off" be cast out, so that thunder and lightning go together or follow one another, as such arrangements may happen, catching up with each other. It is also the nature of such stars that they provide a rain with it: for the reason that all steam that comes from the *salt-spirit* becomes a rain, and that which comes from the *sulphur* becomes a flash of lightning. From this it follows that according to the contents of the star, lightning and rain occur, much or little, according to how that same star has its being and the quantity of its *egestion*. <margin>C</margin> Thus it lightens, rains, and thunders together until it is all spent. Know that there is no other cause than the boiling of the *materia* <note>matter</note>, followed by the moisture and heat, as is the nature of rain and the like.

## Concerning Hail.

There are also other stars which start in the same manner as those mentioned before with lightning, thunder, and rain, but further with stones—that is, with crystals. And they come about because this storm is such a cold thing in itself, and yet such a hot thing is with it: so that from the hot parts come the lightning, thunder, and rain, as stated above; but following this, there is also such a cold nature there that the same water is of such a cold nature that as soon as it resolves into drops, every drop freezes and becomes a "snow-stone" <note>hailstone</note>, and thus falls down with the same *impetus* <note>force</note> as the other, lightning or rain. Now know herein that this nature is from the *Salt of Crystal*, so strong that it is resolved in the star by great force: for it is a separation, just as if snow and boiling water were mixed into one, and then brought apart again into their own beings without the damage of their *corruption* <note>decay or alteration</note>. For no thing is so hot that it does not have a coldness in it, and likewise with the cold, it has a heat. Thus there is a separation in this star, from which separation two kinds fall down: that is, the Warm and the Cold—the Warm in its rain, the Cold in its frozen nature, for such is the property. Know also that herein the *Salamita* <note>likely a reference to a spiritual or elemental force, possibly related to the Salamander/Fire element</note> places hair and other things into these water drops before they freeze—that is, *congeal*—and then sends or leads the same to a place where it pleases him. Also, he can make hail out of such stars when the *materia* is there which would otherwise perish, etc.; he can promote it and carry it across the land.
