# ON METEORS.

<margin>A</margin> Sometimes drops fall upon people or animals, beneath which holes form. If these fall upon the fruit, they poison it; and if the cattle or humans then eat of it, widespread pestilence and many similar things result. Sometimes they fall and create masses, or burn holes into stone, or rot wood—so that while one place remains healthy, another in its prime and in good soil is ruined. Such cases include many crosses falling upon a person, revealed in many colors, appearing like something else yet not being that same likeness; it is divided into a figure according to the threads, just as if it <note>The text here is slightly fragmented</note> were upon wood; it can be wiped off, and the same from bodies, and there are many such forms.

The origin of them all is this: that some arsenic and orpiment <term>Auripigment: a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment</term> <insert>from the body of the</insert> stones is distilled down, and whatever it hits, it clings to. But that good things fall to the good, or that it falls with more advantage upon one than another, or similar things: this is because the spirits of the air rule according to their pleasure, as is mentioned regarding those *Spirits* <note>original: "Spiritibus"</note>. Although such things are attributed to sorcerers, it is in itself no sorcery, but rather a *premonition* <note>original: "Prælagium"</note> of something else. So <insert>it is with the</insert> *premonition* from spirits, like a *prophecy* <note>original: "Vaticinium"</note>; yet their origin <insert>is not from the</insert> Devil, but from God, who works through them so that it is known it does not come through the sorcerers, or that one path is taken rather than another. But this is how the world believes, and how it is mentioned in his books.

<margin>B</margin> Now we must treat the *external premonition of the Spirit* <note>original: "Prælagio Spiritus externo"</note>; first, to understand what a *premonition* is. It is a sign that a thing will happen: just as Christ was a *premonition* that the Jews would pass away, and he served as a sign to the Jews. Now, conversely, if they go against natural reason and liken themselves to things that have no permanence, they will perish. But we shall let that be and move from the previous speeches to the *external* <note>original: "externis"</note> signs, which will fill a small book for us, as follows hereafter.

As we have indicated regarding the internal spirits, so shall follow hereafter regarding the external spirits. The external spirits know everything that will happen to man, and they may reveal it and make it known to men through heavenly signs. Thus, something appears in the heavens that was never there before, appearing strange, signifying something strange in the world through the heavens. And wherever such signs are encountered, it is to be understood that they cannot be warded off: for such signs signify a future event or something new that must and will happen and cannot be turned away.

A comet that appears has no natural origin, but is a light fixed by the spirits to signify something, or a change through a national calamity, or something not yet considered in the land. Its path and its motion are from the spirits and carry a meaning; they come from the highest spirits and signify significant changes, and those of long duration, with many strange occurrences. The same is to be noted of other stars when they arise and have never existed before, in the manner of a comet.

<margin>C</margin> Thus, through the power of the spirits in heaven, other figures are opened which are even stranger, sometimes over particular cities or lands and not in others. This signifies to those where it appears a future evil that will encounter the land. But they are not to be understood as to exactly what will happen or what will be, yet they do not go unfulfilled; something follows afterward that has not happened before. And the stranger such figures appear, the stranger the dealings that follow. Thus, signs are given in a spiritual manner, and some in a worldly manner. They are things that never were before, and thereafter they are recognized as a *premonition*.

Sometimes animals, or their limbs, are seen in the heaven: this is a significance of a future harm to one who is designated or recognized by such an animal. Also, when the natural stars in heaven appear twofold, contrary to natural course and behavior: as the moon among the heads signifies a confusion. Just as the moon is above other stars, so it is there over the people; and with the sun, which is the highest among the stars, it signifies an evil under the highest head. Likewise, if something falls from heaven that is against the course and custom of the stars, it signifies to that land a future [event] made by the spirits to give man to understand his error and his evil which is coming to him, which they do not understand; and it is the power of the spirits, as it stands in *concerning the powers of the spirits* <note>original: "deporentijs Spirituum"</note>.

The crosses that fall from heaven upon the people, and other figures besides, are only *premonitions*, signifying the frivolity of the people and an evil life. The crosses signify a superstition through which the people [are led]; the nails signify the same. The other figures of the saints, such as the gridiron of Saint Lawrence and the like, signify a superstition regarding the saints; they also signify to the land a future evil and a punishment, or various things, in the same way that it happened to the saints; and whatever signs are found there, the same...

# FROM THE ELEMENT OF FIRE.

From this same element, various signs shall break forth: If a red rust <note>original: "Roost"; likely referring to atmospheric phenomena or blood-colored precipitation</note> falls, it signifies that fire shall come upon the executioner and upon the people, and likewise with other signs. Such figures do not occur by chance; let yourselves be better instructed: they fall from the spirits and are an ancient <term>Vitonulla</term> <note>A Paracelsian term likely derived from "nulla vita" or "void of life," referring here to a spiritual force or a specific type of omen that cannot be suppressed</note> that might wish to remain quiet, but it cannot be, for it is right. The falling of such crosses and similar signs signifies a future plague and a great punishment upon those who nourish themselves by the cross and who uphold the cross <note>This likely refers to the clergy or those profiting from religious institutions</note>; they signify a general war or punishment, which, along with the error of the cross <note>original: "Creus Irſal"; referring to heresy or confusion regarding religious doctrine</note>, is a cause of suffering brought upon the people.

The falling of crosses is the highest <term>Prælagium</term> <note>original Latin: "praelagium," meaning a foreboding or omen</note>, and the most powerful above all others: likewise, the other punishments of the plague indicate the life, the essence, and the deserving of the people in their faith. It signifies that the ancient histories, the martyrdoms, and the crucifixions shall return again, and all things shall be brought back to their former state.

# METEOROLOGICAL FRAGMENTS.

### Sequences
#### Various other Meteorological Fragments.
### Concerning Frost.

The origin of frost is as follows: When the summer air of the firmament begins to be affected by cold, dry winds—so fresh and cold, and moreover possessing and attached to congealing powers—it freezes the dew (which falls as dew) according to its congealing nature and properties. Although cold usually does not freeze water <note>The author likely means that moderate cold does not easily freeze large bodies of water</note> due to the weakness of its nature, dew is thin and subtle <term>subtle|refined, delicate, or vaporous</term>, and the air easily penetrates it and freezes it into ice. Thus, every frost is merely a frozen dew, and has no other beginning or matter within it than that of the dew. 

However, such a frost is formed in its own nature, and every frozen dew coagulates <note>original: "coaguliret"</note> according to whether it is strong in its course or its movement. And as they rise into the heights, the wind then blows over the earth because of that altitude, and does not touch the earth itself. <margin>The frost clings to the leaves</margin> The leaves cling to it so that it takes hold; otherwise, it would fall to the earth and remain below. It also moves with moisture, and while in the state of dew, it clings to itself and heaps itself upon the branches <note>original: "Rest," likely meaning "Reis" or twigs/branches</note> before it is separated into actual drops. It is the most subtle form of frost, for dew is the purest and the sharpest substance, as it originates from the biting salt <term>biting salt|a reference to the Paracelsian "Sal," one of the three primary chemical principles believed to govern material properties</term>.

### On Lightning and Thunder.

<margin>A</margin>
<insert>Y</insert>ou should understand lightning in this way: as was indicated in the first beginning concerning the three firsts <note>The "three firsts" (Tria Prima) are Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt, the foundational elements in Paracelsian alchemy</note>, that lightning and everything born in the *media interstia* <note>original: "Medijsinterstijs"; the middle spaces or intervals of the atmosphere</note> originates there. Note that lightning is a dead fire that does not burn, nor ignite, nor flame. It comes in two forms: on beautiful nights, and during the day when heavy rain is beginning and increasing. Note two types of onset: the heavenly ones that come at night with the sulfur that has been separated and is drawn from all the fruits of the three firsts in that form. The *digest* <note>The "digest" refers to the process of maturation or "cooking" within the elements</note> of the three firsts casts off from itself a vapor, like a wind or a smoke—yet not moist like smoke, but perceptible in form like a wind. This same wind comes out of the digest of the three firsts because it does not match their maturation; therefore, it is cast out. And when it is separated from the digest, specifically from its part, then an ignition arises from that which goes against it or which it encounters. For when the outer winds, Eurus <note>The East Wind</note> and Auster <note>The South Wind</note> (for this happens only between these two winds), encounter this cast-off, separated wind, they ignite it. For only the Heavenly must ignite it and no other. In this way, such ignitions of contraries also occur in the winds to the destruction of others, creating a flame like the appearance of a light. But because it is a wind, it flames up quickly, and one follows another out of it, more or less according to the nature, strength, and abundance of the digest. These indicate no moisture, only fair weather and sweltering heat. For the heat of the
<margin>B</margin>
digest causes such a thing, as is shown in the digest.

But the lightning in the day and night that accompanies violent weather has another cause: a wind goes out from the house of the maturation of the three firsts in the same way. But in that same place is a moist digest, and this same moisture moves through itself like a boiling thing. This same thing, driven into a moist condition, is ignited by the zealous air, like the fair night-wind. Then follows the thunder; when the saltpeter, mercury, and sulfur boil through one another, they do not remain still but boil. They do not harmonize into one because of their contrariety, which cannot be reconciled. Thus they strike through one another and bubble up a wind from themselves, which is ignited as far as it has gone and goes. And as soon as it burns, that same lightning ignites the sulfur of the digest, so that it becomes burning from the dead fire, according to the nature of its property. Thereupon the sulfur ignites the saltpeter, and as soon as it burns, it strikes away from itself all the water-clouds that the digest prepared and fixed. Therefore, it follows that from the lightning a thunderclap comes: because the mercury and sulfur ignite, and that ignition reaches the saltpeter, which strikes when it feels the water-clouds around it while burning. Similarly, there are many voices that give thunder beforehand—early thunders—because that same digest-wind is not so large that it reaches the earth or makes itself visible, but it is still above our sight. For only the Heavenly must ignite it and no other. In this way, many heavenly lights also occur that make no thunder: because they fade away before they return to the digest, or are violently expelled by the water-clouds that fall between them, so that the flame of the lightning does not come back behind itself due to the falling rain of the waters that surround them.

## ON THE RAINBOW. Another way.

The origin of the rainbow is that it comes from a star, like any other fruit from its seed. Therefore, just as you live on earth, where often a horse is green, brown, red, yellow, etc. <note>This likely refers to the variety of colors in nature or specific astrological "signatures"</note>, so also is the *Arona* <note>likely a term for the celestial atmosphere or a specific plant-like celestial growth</note>, and thus the growth of the earth.

Thus the rainbow is also a herb of the heavens: when its star rises, it pours it out, first as a cloud, then onto the earth. Thus its form is such that its colors are there: just like a tree that grows, there is its branch, there its roundness, there [its fruit]. For what concerns the form, that same thing proceeds from God, and is not for man to know.

The rainbow's way of growing is thus: initially there are 8 or 9, they have their star at an unnamed time, just as when one makes a child, and [in] winter: so also the rainbows. Although in winter it freezes, so that it may not reach the ground, or [it stays] in the warmth.

<margin>* It is made from the * Conjunction <note>original: "Coniunction"</note> which is in the star itself; that is, it is its own egg, which is hatched by the time.</margin>
Now the rainbow is produced from its own star, like a herb from its seed: and

<margin>Corruption <note>original: "Corruptio"</note></margin>
as it now grows, it begins and grows into its form and colors, like a herb, but all invisibly. When its time comes, it fixes itself upon the floor of the earth. Then, when the earthly moisture enters into them, it first gives the colors and becomes visible. And just as a woman who makes two children: so the rainbow makes two, also etc. three or the like, and it is for the very same reason. Now many such rainbows occur in the year, summer and winter: but because it is a subtle growth, the cold takes it away, that is, it freezes before it becomes ripe. Likewise the winds consume it, the sun burns it, so that nothing comes of it. Likewise the winds blow them away while they are still young and not strengthened. They succeed best of all when the weather is moist, half warm and half cold; then their greenness is at its best, and their time: therefore they come at rainy times. Not that they signify rain, but the better the rainy weather is, the better their condition—unless it were a cloudburst that would resolve it in the heaven.

They come in the morning, at night, etc., just like the birth of a woman, which also comes at such hours. Although at [night] not many are seen because of the light: for the moonlight gives so much brightness (not) that one may see; likewise neither does the darkness, etc. And know this, that such rainbows are as far as the heaven goes. But in some lands more than in others, that is, according to the heat of the sun, etc., the cold of the weather, or the wind, where they may not be so much seen <note>original: "erfchen"</note>.

### ON COMETS.

If we now wish to know the origin of Comets, know then that they are a gathering of men, a harbinger to them. From this it follows that a comet can never exist outside of Nature. For Nature is no <term>Phyronilla</term> <note>Likely a reference to a fickle or deceptive character/spirit; Paracelsus often used idiosyncratic names for elemental forces.</note>. Just as the blossom on the tree is a harbinger of its fruit, yet it is not the fruit itself: so is the comet a work made by the spirits of the air, just as when a <term>Magus</term> <note>A practitioner of high natural magic.</note> creates a likeness of his heir.

Note, however, that because our affairs, governance, etc., come from the brain, so must it be born from the brain, just as the body is born from the earth. Thus the origin of the body's globe changes, as does the <term>Testa</term> <note>Latin: "shell" or "tile." Here used metaphorically for the "shell of reason" or the cranium/intellectual vessel.</note> of Reason. And just as the body is created clumsy and coarse by the world, so is the <term>Ingenium</term> <note>Natural talent or mental capacity.</note> created by the <term>Testa</term>. Thus there are two mothers: one in the Earth, and the other in the Heaven.

From this it follows, as you see, that the body is transmuted by the Earth—that is, out of the body, for it is the Earth. This is also understood regarding Reason: that it is changed by the <term>Testa</term>. For here is the cause of what belongs to the body and what pertains to Reason: and thus they are two <term>Corpora</term> <note>Bodies.</note>. Now, the body is not a body of the Earth—that is, it is the Earth's; Reason is of the <term>Testa</term>. But on both sides, the form is carved for the body, and Reason for the <term>Testa</term>.
<sig>B</sig>

Since there are thus two bodies in one person, there are also two kinds of <term>Presages</term> <note>original: "Praelagia." Omens or forewarnings.</note>. One for the body from the Earth, the other from the <term>Testa</term> of Reason. Just as a great fruitfulness is a great future—a happy year, etc.—and worse follows after. So it is also with the indications of Reason.

But note herein: there is a tree that has grown in its professions, in foliage, etc. So are they also in the four elements. Out of this, a Comet is like a worm that falls in crosswise and causes his tree to wither: so it is with the Comet, etc.
->Salanita the witch-lover, the near-murderer.<- <note>original: "Salanita der Herenbulet, der Na hemörder." These appear to be obscure names or epithets for specific types of destructive comets or spirits.</note>

### Rain.

If we are to know further of the natural waters of the <unclear>Rewrs</unclear>, know then that waters also spring from the Heaven; these are the rains, snow, etc.

For such is the nature of the entire sphere: that all things run against one another. That is, the water of the globe runs upward, that of the valley runs downward; thus they run from both sides toward each other.

<margin>6</margin> Now, rainwater is a water that generates nothing from itself, but in many ways, through <term>Conjunction</term> <note>The meeting of celestial bodies or elements.</note> and otherwise by itself.

Therefore know that they are divided into as many parts as there are parts of the Earth and species of generated virtues that come out of the Earth. But not that this is a fruit of the Earth—that is, that each follows its natural course—rather, it is its own pride, as the water with its mineral and the earth with its fruits: each for itself. Therefore we write here of its water, according to our purpose.

Regarding the distinction of waters, we give you this to understand: that there are as many seeds in Heaven as there are from the Earth or in the water. These same seeds produce the rains, but it is not for us to know what kind of seed each one is. Just as we cannot recognize herbs by their colors alone—for they are all green—and if the form were never before us, we would have no knowledge of them.

So now the water is without form, so that we can take nothing from the form to know what is <term>Marjoram</term>, what is <term>Lavender</term>, etc. Although one rain is clearer than another, as with the shades of green, such degrees give us no understanding.

### PHILIP THEOPHRASTUS,
->ON<-
### MINERALS
->BOOK<-
<sig>B</sig>
Since I have undertaken to write for you concerning Ore, and everything that pertains to Ore, and how it comes into its birth and nature: it is therefore necessary first to point out that several before me have written of the birthing of Ore. Having read them, I have found them not to be righteous, but rather in error. For as they write, it is certain that they have not understood the *ultimate Matter* <term>Materia ultima: the final, completed form of a substance</term>. Where such *ultimate Matter* is not understood, how much less can the Beginning be understood? For anyone who wishes to describe a Beginning must know the End best of all. What use is a Theologian who does not know his End? What use is an Astronomer who speaks much but does not know the Radiance? Therefore, as a Jurist <note>Paracelsus likely uses "Jurist" here metaphorically for one who judges or has authority</note>, I have more power to write than the others before me. I will first present the discovered Matter, so that you may see the beginning which I shall lead you through by that same indication, and may well recognize what the beginning is. For a Physician must first recognize the disease; thereafter he knows how to treat it. To recognize the disease at the start is where the Art lies, not in the entrance; the entrance is blind, the exit is visible—therein lies the knowledge. Therefore, I now show such a Foundation, so that every thing may be well recognized in its First state, because it is also well-created. For man should take the works of God unto himself, so that they are not hidden from him, and that they stand well-known to him in their Foundation; for otherwise he will misuse them. For what use is an Ore in the hand of one who does not know it? He should have it who can use it. For everything that God has created is for him who knows how it should be used. Man should know this and increase it, and avoid those things which have arisen from the Devil.

As I now intend to write of the origin of all Ores—and this not from myself, but from experience through Him from whom I have it—I say, as in the first paragraph, that the Last should be understood before the First, and from the Last, the First. Of this I give an example: that CHRIST was never understood until He sent the Holy Spirit, who enlightened all things; through Him we understand CHRIST, and He came after CHRIST. Likewise, through the Holy Spirit, we understand the Father and the Son.

So I say of this Philosophy of Ore, that the *ultimate Matter* are the things that should be sought in the Beginnings. Now, in other paragraphs of Philosophy, I have maintained that three things—namely, Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury—are in the Beginning, and spring from the four "Ventilators" <note>original: "Wüttern"; referring to the winds or directions</note>, that is, from the four Elements. Now to present here at the start: Iron, Steel, Lead, Emerald, Sapphire—these are nothing other than Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury. For every thing that is born of Nature is breakable, and the Art <term>Alchemy/Chemistry</term> shows what Nature has made it from. Thus Nature gives us to know that in the Beginning are the three...

<header>FIRST TREATISE.</header>

### FIRST TREATISE.

<margin>a</margin> These three things—just as well as in wood and in other things—are namely Fire, Balsam, and Mercury. For if you break down Steel, Gold, Pearls, or Corals through the Art <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy or early chemistry.</note>, you will find **Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury**: and as soon as you have these through the Art, there is nothing left of the original ore, but everything is broken down. Since a thing is thus broken down and gives up its substance—namely Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury—and if you ask, "What is it?" then know that there are three things from which all material things come: Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury. These three things are the *Corpus* <note>Body</note>, and it is universal in these three things. I have laid out the beginning here for you so that you should know that three things are in the *ultima Materia* <note>ultimate matter; the final form or the fundamental components</note>, and from these all ores become. How God further created Nature follows hereafter: on this foundation, nothing can fail.

<margin>b</margin> Now, upon this, God created an Element of Water, and from the same, He poured forth continually into the birthing process the minerals, so that they might grow daily and be useful to man for his use. And He thus created the Water so that it should be a mother of the first things: Fire, Salt, and Mercury; and ordered it in such a way that metals, gems, stones, and ores should become one with the water. And the mother is useful: thus God created everything, each in its own kind—the bird in the air is one thing, the fish in the water another. As far apart as these are from one another, so too is the nature of other things different. All these things are of the Lord, who has thus accomplished His will. Now know first that the Element of Water is the mother of all minerals, and yet it is not like them at all: for just as the earth is wood and yet is not wood, so also are stone, iron, etc., from the water. The water becomes that which it is not itself; the earth also becomes that which it is not itself: so also must man become that which he is not. Whatever shall go into its *last Materiam* <note>final matter</note> must become different, for the beginning should be nothing to anyone. Now in the Element of Water is a *prima Materia* <note>first matter; the raw material of creation</note>: a Fire, a Salt, a Mercury, and they have in them several kinds, of which more will follow. Thus, they have stones, they have metals, they have *Gemmas* <note>gems</note>, they have stones, they have *Kiß* <note>pyrites or gravelly ore</note>; and the metal is one thing, the stone another, the pyrite another. So also in the heavens: the lightning bolt is one thing, the rainbow another, the sky another. So also in the earth: wood is one thing, the herb another, the flower another, the fungus another. Thus a Craftsman has let Himself be seen—a Master over all, whom no one may defy: He is alone, all in all, He is the *prima Materia*, He is the *Rerum ultima Materia* <note>the ultimate matter of things</note>, He is the one who is everything. Therefore, it is now proper to write of the minerals, and first of all of the property of the Mother—that is, of the Element of Water—as follows hereafter. Although the ancients have written of these things which I have taken under my pen, saying that they come from the earth; they meant well, but tested it poorly, despite various trials and what is necessary for testing.

<margin>c</margin> Now, the first thing with God was the Beginning—that is, the *ultima Materia*; that same *ultima Materia* He made into *primam Materiam*. Just as a fruit that is to give another fruit has a seed: the seed is the *prima Materia*. Thus now the *ultima Materia* of minerals is in a *prima Materia*, in a seed, and the seed is *Elementum Aqua* <note>the Element of Water</note>, and He resolved it so that it is a water. Now, for this purpose, He created Nature so that she should make the *ultimam Materiam*, which is itself in water, and she takes what is in the water under her power and preparation. What belongs to metals, she separates into metals, and each metal for itself; what belongs to precious stones, likewise into its kind; what belongs to stones, the same; and so with the *marcasites* <note>a term then used for various metallic sulfides</note> and other species. Then God ordained the seasons, so that there is an "earth" in the grain <note>a time of ripening</note> and an autumn in the fruit: so He also ordained that the Element of Water should have its harvest and autumn. Thus the water is an element and a mother, and a purse <note>a storehouse or vessel</note> of all minerals: and the *Archeus* <note>the internal "alchemist" or vital force of nature</note> within her joins and orders things in Nature, so that each comes into its *ultimam Materiam* of Nature. From Nature, man takes it into his *ultimam Materiam*: that is, where Nature stops, there man begins; and her *ultima Materia* is man's *prima Materia*, and the breaking down of Nature is man's *ultima Materia*. Thus God has created so wonderfully that the *prima Materia* is a water and is soft, a drink: therefore its birth—that is, a fruit—is hard, like the metals and stone, than which nothing can be harder; and thus the hardest comes from the softest, a fire from the water, beyond understanding. But since the Element of Water is a mother of minerals, it is not beyond the understanding of Nature: for God has created wonderful children from the mother. Namely, look at men: from one mother, each has a particular body and property—not according to the body, but according to the kind. Thus all metals are, according to the body, water: but the properties are metals, stones, marcasites: for otherwise they have no meaning except to be different in the substance of the *Corpus*.

<margin>d</margin> Thus God has now created the Element of Water so that it should be an element of all metals and stones, and has separated it from the other three elements in a special *Corpus*, so that it is not in the air, nor in the earth, nor in the heavens, but is a free, independent *Corpus*. And He creates the same upon the earth, and it has its *Concavitet* <note>cavity or basin</note> in the earth, wherein it lies:

It lies there: and is so miraculously created that it must carry, along with the Earth, mankind, so that he may wander upon it and make use of it. Furthermore, it is to be known that it is so miraculously created that it goes in a circle around the globe and does not fall from its place: so that the part which is beneath us stands upright just as well as we do, and yet is distinct. And it is so miraculously created that the pits of the true element—that is, where it is in its exaltation <note>A state of highest power or refinement in alchemy</note> and center—are entirely without a floor, so that it has no support from the Earth upon which it stands, but stands freely like an egg within itself, and nothing falls upon the shell. Thus the element of Water <note>original: "Aqua"</note> also has such a miraculous shell, and it is a great wonder-work of God. And in this generation, and in the generating of all metals and stones, they manifest and show themselves in many miraculous ways.

In addition, you should also know, as you see, that all fruits of the Earth grow in the Air, and nothing remains in the Earth, but everything comes over the Earth and immediately separates itself from the Earth. In the same way, the growth of Water—metals, salts, gems, stones, talc, marcasites, sulphurs, etc.—all goes from the mother of the element into another mother, which is the Earth. And when its "work-tree" is fully within the Earth, then its fruit grows upon it, according to the nature and property of that same tree.

Likewise, a metal of this or that kind grows there; here a genus of salt, there a genus of sulphur, there a genus of gem, etc. And just as one finds many cherries on one tree and pears on another tree: so are such <term>growths of the element water</term> <note>original: "kruckus Aquæ Elementi"</note> to be found in the extremities and <term>compartments</term> <note>original: "Loculus"</note> of the trees of the element water. And as some trees bear much fruit and some little: so there is also such a property, nature, and condition here. Therefore, such trees should be sought first, and thereafter the fruit: for thus the <term>rural miner</term> <note>original: "Rusticus," literally a peasant or rustic, here implying one who labors in the element</note> who builds in the element of Water is taught, just as the plowman on the Earth is taught by the Earth how he should cultivate it and where to find the fruits.

Therefore, know also that it might well be said of the plants of the Earth that they grow in the Air because they are in the Air; yet that cannot be, nor is it so: rather, their roots are found in the Earth, and they take their origin from the Earth and <term>perfect themselves</term> <note>original: "persicieren auff ihr Perfection"</note> in the Air. Just as in the Air, so that which comes from the Water completes its perfection in the Earth and is generated in its place. Thus the growths of minerals prove that they are all water and exist because of water, and that in the water of those same <term>predefined limits of minerals</term> <note>original: "prima Mineralium Prædefinierten Termino"</note>, harvest and autumn reveal themselves and generate that which is within them.

And when a root begins, it is first of all that this same root rises into a tree—that is, a <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>—out of which that same mineral shall now become metal or something else in the Earth. For in the same way that a nut or a cherry does not grow directly upon the Earth, but first becomes a tree, and after the tree comes the generation and the fruit: so Nature provides a tree, which is a watery body, and that same tree grows into the Earth and fills the pores of the Earth just as the Earth fills the Air. And when such a tree is in the Earth, then its fruit grows upon it, according to the nature and property of that same tree.

Likewise, a metal of this or that kind grows there; here a genus of salt, there a genus of sulphur, there a genus of gem, etc. And just as one finds many cherries on one tree and pears on another tree: so are such growths of the element water to be found in the extremities and compartments of the trees of the element water. And as some trees bear much fruit and some little: so there is also such a property, nature, and condition here. Therefore, such trees should be sought first, and thereafter the fruit: for thus the rural miner who builds in the element of Water is taught, just as the plowman on the Earth is taught by the Earth how he should cultivate it and where to find the fruits.

So there should also be such an observation regarding this generation, that an example should always be taken from the Earth, and in this way: there are some trees that give their fruit, but like a nut and its kind, it has a rough shell on the outside, then another, then a thin skin over the kernel. So also are metals and genera of minerals. Like iron ore, silver ore, and other ores; therefore one must separate them, and then one finds the fruit within. There is also sometimes a kind that gives its fruit freely: like cherries, plums, grapes, which cast nothing away from themselves, but everything is good. Thus one also finds in the water-springs free gold, silver, coral, <unclear>Carade</unclear>, and the like. All this is ordained in Nature, that the shell in which the mineral lies is different and varied: which is solely according to the kind of Water, that same climate, region, and division. And also regarding the bark, what is within it, like the fruit itself. So as you see a body from the kernel: so know that there is also in the element itself a body and a spirit, and the spirit is in the body.

# FIRST TREATISE.

Noble and good. For just as a human being is two bodies—one coarse, which is not as it should be, and then within that same one, a good body—so are all plants <note>original: "Gewächs," referring to anything that grows, including minerals in this context</note> to be understood. For all things that God has created, He has brought forth in a similar process of corporeality. But He made man differently, because he is made after His image, so that there is also within him the Eternal, which is not in the other creatures. Thus it is also understood regarding the death of the elements: that water is also another thing, and that water is its own death; it eats and strangles and consumes its own growth. As the earth provides an example: what grows from her returns into her and is lost, so that nothing more is found of it. Just as with yesterday: it is gone and is worth nothing more; there is no one who may see it any further. So also the past night. Thus all things that are of the earth go back into the earth, and the earth consumes them, in such a form that it is not a form of a liquid <note>original: "Liquors"</note>; which is not a water, no oil, no bitumen, no mucilage <note>original: "Mucilago," a thick, gluey substance</note>, etc. Just <margin>or Trunk.</margin> like a wood out of the earth, which the earth is not, nor is the * seed <note>original: "Saam"</note>, and yet it is a wood from the earth, and the branches are like it. Thus now the tree of the mineral is formed into such a body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, and is henceforth set out in its expanse: so that often one is from the other 20, 40, or 60 miles apart. So that one branch goes into the German High Mountains <note>likely the Alps</note>, as into the lungs, another branch into Joachimsthal <note>St. Joachimsthal, a famous silver mining town in Bohemia</note>, and likewise another branch into Transylvania <note>original: "Siebenbürgen"</note>. For such is the distribution into the whole world of the earth. For a tree is a new growth there.

But concerning the tree of the Water Element <note>original: "Aquae Elementi"</note>, note this: When nature wants to give a growth into the world, whether it be of gold, silver, iron, copper, etc., or of precious stones, emerald, sapphire, garnet, etc., or of salts, be it alum, vitriol, plumolum <note>likely a lead-based mineral or "feather alum"</note>, etc., or of springs, sour, sweet, cold, warm, etc., or of corals, marcasites, etc.; then she raises the tree up out of the element of water into the earth, so that it stands with its roots in its center * of the sea. Then it also gives <margin>of the Womb <note>original: "Matricis"</note>.</margin> itself out of the earth and distributes its branches. Thus know now that its trunk is like a form of a liquid: which is not a water, no oil, no bitumen, no mucilage, etc. Just like a wood out of the earth, which the earth is not, nor is the * seed, and yet it is a special body from the earth. This liquid is the trunk, and its branches are like the wood of the tree, and the branches are also like it. Thus now the tree of the mineral is formed into such a body, and is henceforth set out in its expanse: so that often one is from the other 20, 40, or 60 miles apart. So that one branch goes into the German High Mountains, as into the lungs, another branch into Joachimsthal, and likewise another branch into Transylvania. For such is the distribution into the whole world of the earth. Then the trees become weak through one another as far as the earth goes. Now when a tree has grown, each one into the plains <note>original: "Planicies"</note>, that is, to the daylight; sometimes they remain, sometimes in the earth, according to whether the kind is long or small. Upon this it follows now, that in the extremities <note>original: "Extremitatibus"</note> of the branches, the nature of the water element pours out its fruit through those same extremities into the earth. And as soon as they come into the earth, from that hour the coagulation <note>the process of becoming solid</note> happens, and that becomes of it from that same tree—much or little—that which it is intended to be. When the fruit is entirely pushed out, then that same tree withers and dies within itself, consumed like all things, and leaves its fruit lying; and it goes into the consummation <note>original: "Conſummation," the final end or destruction</note> in which all creatures conclude and take their end; and according to nature, a new growth is there again.

Therefore, know in all things that the first matter <note>original: "Prima Materia"</note> of all kinds of mineral fruit lies in the element of water, and that this same first matter is solely Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary substances of Paracelsian alchemy</note>. And these three things, as they are named, have within them all metals, all salts <note>original: "Salia"</note>, all gems, etc. And if they wish to be generated, then the first time of their fruit must not pass them by, as each kind disposes itself into its genus and species. As if one had in a sack, mixed together, all the seeds that are now in the world. And if he now sows them in the garden, nature is there and gives to each seed its own fruit at the end, so that each seed comes into its essence and perfection, without harm to the others.

As it should be understood here not alone, but also in the element of water, as if it were a sack in which all seeds were and wished to be sown: so each genus and species grows into its kind and property. Thus God has ordained the wonder-works of His creatures into the four elements: and these are the elements from which the fruits go, which man then uses...

...should do: And created by God, every species in its own property and essence. Thus are the **wonders of God** recognized and experienced. Therefore, Philosophy should proceed, which alone allows the works of God to be known—which every human is obligated to recognize, regarding what his Creator has provided for him. Now, however, just as there are many kinds of fruit, so too are there many kinds of **Sulphur**, **Salt**, and as many kinds of **Mercury**. There is one kind of Sulphur in Gold, another in Iron, another in Lead, Tin, etc. Likewise, there is another in Sapphire, and in Ruby, Chrysolite, Amethyst, Magnet, etc. Also another in Springs <note>original: "Fontibus"</note>, etc. And not only are there so many kinds of Sulphur, but also just as many different Salts: such as one in metals, another in gems <note>original: "Gemmis"</note>, another in stones, another in Vitriol, another in Alum. The same applies now to the Mercuries: another in gems, and as often as there is a species, there is another Mercury. One essence is Sulphur, one essence is Salt, one essence is Mercury. We must divide them further, so that there is not only one kind of Gold, but many kinds of Gold:

<margin>B</margin>
Of the same, but many kinds: Therefore also so many kinds of **Sulphurs of Gold**, and thus of all metals and stones; as many kinds of Sulphur, high and low, so many kinds of Sapphire-like Salt, so many kinds of Mercury, and also with the Turquoise and all their like. So that you may know that Nature has grasped all these together in one fist, and from that she gives out each one according to its best and strongest: She thus distinguishes the metals into a particular kind, and moreover each species specifically that is within a metal. You should understand that as many species are created as there are things that grow, and each has its own Sulphur, its own Salt, and its own Mercury. Just as when a painter has a color, he makes from it many figures and forms, none like the other. So it is there also: Nature is the painter. In this, however, Nature and the painter differ from one another: the painter makes dead things, Nature makes **essential things**; the painter makes shadows, but Nature makes bodies.

Furthermore, know that it is the same with colors: namely, that all colors come from **Salt**, for Salt gives the color and the **Coagulation** <note>The process of becoming solid or firm</note>; Sulphur gives the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, the substance, and the structure; Mercury gives the virtues, powers, and secrets <note>original: "Virtutes, Vires, Arcana"</note>. Thus these three must be together, and none can be without the other; and God gives them life, so that they become what He intends for them to be, according to His pleasure. Now Nature takes the species that belongs to a thing and draws it out of the Salt: just as she takes the body from the Sulphur, so she also takes from the Mercury that which belongs to each.

<margin>C</margin>
Therefore, he who wishes to know the bodies of all things <note>original: "Corpora Rerum omnium"</note>, let him study Sulphur; thereafter, he who wishes to know the colors, let him take the foundation of Salt; and he who wishes to know the virtues, let him fathom the secrets of Mercury. This is the foundation for finding the **Mysteries** in every growth, as it has been brought forth. Therefore know that Nature possesses such bodies, colors, and virtues, and can bring them apart again, forming, coloring, and endowing them as is appropriate and given by God. For see how wonderfully in a small seed a tree grows, with such beautiful green colors in the leaves, with such various colors in the blossoms, etc. Thus in Nature the Mystery is so great that one must marvel. For God is wonderful in His works, which shall not be left neglected, but shall be watched and daily experienced by those who walk in the way of God.

Now it is also necessary that I instruct you on the order of minerals. For I am prompted to do so by the manifold orders used by others. First, it will be concerning the metals, which are not of one kind, but each metal in its essence and for that which man requires: of which there are many kinds, each according to what man needs. Thus some are also suited not in the form of metallic nature, but in the form of being worn, or for dwelling, for the preservation of the inner body, such as Sapphire, Ruby, and Carnelian <note>original: "Carniol"</note>. These are created in another form, so that man may well have them with him, to ordain a shelter and such a vessel for himself. There is another kind of stones which man does not need like a metal, or a salt, not of one category, which cannot be metals, but are for man to handle for his necessity in other ways...

## First TRACTATE

Furthermore, metals, gems, and stones are neither intended for nor suitable for this. Therefore, concerning springs, we shall proceed in princely order: namely, that they should take the form of a water-well. Some are for the internal body, some external; some are cold, others warm, others sour, others sweet. There are so many varieties of these that no one can fully categorize them. Furthermore, there are more, such as the marcasites <note>A historical term for various sulfide minerals, often iron pyrite or "fool's gold."</note>, of which two are found: namely, gold-colored and silver-colored. Their species are many, in which God has retained a particular abundance. These He has given into the hand of man, so that he may seek in them what he desires, and take out what God has given there, and learn how to extract it. And furthermore, there is another kind, of which there are four types: namely, Red, White, Yellow, and Black. Each is a genus <note>A "genus" or "kind" in the Aristotelian sense of classification.</note> unto itself—not metals, not gems, not stones, not salts, not *sorres* <note>original: "Sorres," likely referring to sory, a vitriolic mineral or copper byproduct.</note>, not marcasites, but a distinct kind for itself. He has also provided sand in abundance, of which no more need be written than that it belongs to construction; it is a different kind for the mason, not at all like those mentioned, such as the corals. Of these there are many kinds; Red and White are well known, but other colors and forms are also found, and all corals will be clearly identified in their own paragraphs. Yet further is a kind that is quite human-like and a supernatural genus, which by nature makes itself into instruments in many strange ways and properties, such as eagle-stones <note>Aetites; hollow stones believed to assist in childbirth.</note>, shells, *randlen* <note>likely small round stones or pebbles</note>, *schüßlen* <note>dish-shaped stones or fossils</note>, etc. Thus, note in the following paragraph the origin of these mentioned things from
**B** the element of Water. And as just intended, so many are the kinds of fruits from the element of Water. And although it is true that I describe only those known to me, I know well—and more than well—that the entire globe, the lower and upper spheres, is provided for in no other way than at all ends, as I write, above, beside, and on all sides. Therefore, I am well permitted to write of it. It is indeed true that much still lies in the earth that I do not know; others also have no knowledge of it. For I know well that God will yet bring many strange things to light that have not yet existed or been revealed. Therefore, after me shall come more of the *Magnal* <note>original: "Magnal," likely referring to the "Magnalia Dei" or the great works/mysteries of God.</note> that does not yet live and is not yet open.

Now you should know that there are three parts in the Art from which the completion of minerals comes, and these artistic parts are innate in the nature of the element, in the first three. For just as a man has his gift in the arts for which he is suited, so also the Art has its place in the first three. And you should know that it is not possible for any man to complete a thing or work solely by himself, without helpers. Thus, no one is above the other, except for those alone who can join them together—that is, those things which belong together. For example, there lies iron ore. Now, what can it do alone? Nothing, without the smelter and the refiner. Secondly, it is nothing without the buyer, or the finished product without the one who can buy it, and the buyer for the one who uses it. Thus, it is not a single thing alone. So it is also in Nature: it is not one thing alone that makes a mineral or stone, but rather several things are layered together that belong to it: the smelter, buyer, seller, consumer. If Nature does not need it, she provides it to man, as the first matter
**C** which belongs to him. But she requires a *dispensatoris* <note>original: "Dispensatoris," a distributor or steward.</note> who orders the things, so that what is meant to become of it, does become of it. This same one is ordained by God: Nature. Furthermore, this one must have the workmen who join such things together, and that is the *Archeus* of Nature <note>The "Archeus" is the internal "alchemist" or vital force that directs natural processes.</note>. Furthermore, this one must work the materials and bring them into that for which they are ordained. From this it follows that three must be taken together to bring every mineral to its end: namely, Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury. These three are to be one body, and that in which one works is the Sulphur; then there must be the Mercury; then there must be the compaction, congelation, and that which it is to become. Now, not every Sulphur is a body for gold, nor every Mercury for its kind, nor every Salt for the *coadunation* <note>The joining or uniting of parts into one.</note>. But just as there are many kinds of blacksmiths, one for this and one for that, etc., so it is here also. Therefore, God has ordained that the Archeus brings together what belongs together: like a baker who bakes a bread, brings together what belongs together; like a vine-dresser who gathers for the vineyard and belongs to the vineyard. Each is predestined to his office, and each finds what belongs to his office. Thus, when the Archeus has his *glans* <note>likely "glance" or "intent"</note> and is to produce a tree in gold, in iron, in hyacinths, in ivory-stone, in *dusselstein*, in marble, in sand, in *tachiniten*, etc., he takes together the *Simplicia* <note>Simple, unmixed substances.</note>—Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury—which are of that kind and suitable for the undertaking. Afterward, he takes them together into their *Athanar* <note>A furnace used by alchemists for slow, consistent heat.</note>, wherein they decoct <note>To cook or process with heat.</note> themselves like a seed in the earth. Furthermore, it is not only sufficient in the earth, but they decoct among one another in such a way that the Sulphur gives up its body in which they work, and they prepare it in their opportunity for what it is to become. Afterward, of the other two, the Mercury decocts itself into its property, so that it shall be what it is. After such decoctions have occurred, there follows the conservation—that is, from the Salt—which coagulates all things together. That is at the first...

Which instruction on minerals is necessary so that it may be sufficiently understood, and that no one takes for themselves the interpretation of the ancient writers or their followers. Although they are held in high regard, it is only by those of their own kind, who are like-minded and of lesser understanding; otherwise, they do not cease and do not apply the effort to collect and retain it with such diligence.

## II.

And further, concerning the birth of metals, know that there is a good number of them: For that is a metal which the fire may master, and which may be brought into an instrument by man: namely Gold, Silver, Iron, Copper, Lead, Tin; these are recognized as metals in the light of day. Furthermore, there are now also several metals which are only [found] in the writings of the ancient philosophers or in alchemy <note>original: "alchimi"</note> as metals: Such as Zinc, Cobalt <note>original: "Kobolet"</note>, which allow themselves to be hammered and forged by fire: Also certain garnets, which are called garnets, of which there are many forms, and which are also metals. Now, it is no less true that there are many more of them which are also unknown to me. For there are Marcasites, in Bismuth <note>original: "Wismat"</note>, in other *Cachimae* <note>A term used by Paracelsus for the "dross" or immature forms of metals</note> which yield metals: No one can know them all, one only knows the most prominent ones, which are most convenient and intended for use: Such as Gold, Silver, Iron, Copper, Tin, Lead; those who let themselves wonder at them pass them by and do not strive for their properties. For the [metal] caster does not, the brazier does not, the goldsmith does not; yet it is a [metal] that is not yet born: for no one teaches further, except in a [certain way].

<margin>* not philosophical</margin> Regarding *Argentum Vivum* <note>Latin: "Living Silver," i.e., Quicksilver or Mercury</note>, that it be a metal, that is not found [to be true]; among other minerals it is a mineral, not a metal, not a stone, not a marcasite, but a special growth of nature, like others for itself, with a body like other minerals. Thus, nothing is to be held of the idea that there are seven planets, and so also seven metals. Therefore, if they do not [fit] further into metals, they compare them together: so Gold shall be the Sun, Silver the Moon, Copper Venus, Saturn shall be Lead, Jupiter shall be Tin. Now [take] Venus and Copper together, as it rhymes in one kind, bring them together; Lead and Saturn, see what it is: bring together [the others] and see what fruits come from it. Such things and philosophers are namely a [hollow] mantle: for there is no ground nor philosophy, nor any right <insert>political dealings</insert> <note>original: "Polische Händel," likely referring to deceptive or complex affairs</note>. Now it follows from this, that *Argentum Vivum*, its complex, nature, operation, quality, and property together, and [how] it rhymes and fits together—it is all nothing: It is not in such a manner as the other. Although the philosophy of plants also brought in seven herbs, but did not prove them. According to their sense, *Mercurialis* <note>Mercury herb</note> should be Mercury, *Solsequium* <note>Sunflower/Marigold</note> should be the Sun; according to their modest understanding, *Lunaria* <note>Moonwort</note> should be the Moon. You want to look into heaven, at what is in heaven, and the earth, and the [stars], and want to be astronomers and philosophers, and want to be all that: And you do not see [what is before you]. They want first to see in heaven what is in heaven. This distribution, let it remain with those who do not act according to [truth], but according to their long robes. Thus sounds the chapter on metals, that they are a number of six from the common sort, which are known, which I mentioned above: And yet four more, which are also known to me, whose number and form will follow hereafter. [There] may be a great number, for it happens in the testing of metals that [many] are found, and if one tests them in the metallic way, that is, according to the nature of the six metals, they cannot [be identified], for their test is not such; I consider them to be an innumerable amount: Although [the creator] may well recognize and cover that, as He is in His examination.

Now, concerning the birth of Gold, know that there is a Sulphur, highly sublimated and purified of all its dregs and ingredients, diaphanous and whitened <note>original: "Candirt"</note>, so that there may be nothing among all metals [purer]. And it is the *Sulphur Auri* <note>Sulphur of Gold</note>, the first matter <note>original: "prima materia"</note>. If the [alchemists] could find this Sulphur, as it is to be found in the Gold-tree, they might well rejoice: for that is the *Sulphur Philosophorum* <note>Sulphur of the Philosophers</note>, not the other from which Iron or Copper comes, etc. That is the scruple of their [universal medicine]. Also at the highest, separated in a metallic way from all earthliness, the *Mercuriale Corpus* <note>Mercurial Body</note> is transmuted to all perspicuity. Therefore, the [Salt] of Gold <note>original: "Aurorum"</note> which is generated is the other piece of the first matter. Accordingly, the first matter of Gold, and of the tree upon which Gold shall grow, [is like] roses: and is at the highest crystallized, and so highly sequestered and depurated from all [harsh], acetic, aluminous, and vitriolic [elements], etc., so that no attachment [remains]. In itself it is at the highest elucidated, in the highest perillic <note>likely "berylline" or crystal-clear</note> diaphanous thing...

<header>The First TRACTATE.</header>

## The First TRACTATE.

<margin>A</margin> All things together are Gold <note>original: "Aurum"</note>, which is cooked in measure, as was previously indicated in the beginning. Now it is no less true that it is not just one kind of Gold, but many kinds: (not just one degree, but Nature herself gives 22 degrees to the highest Gold. At best, 24 are found through Art <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy/Chemistry as practiced by man</note>, to make the same permanent in the light of day. For this is the reason: that Gold is the same in its tree <note>The "Tree of Metals" or "Arbor Philosophica"</note> as an Epicurus in his kitchen. As soon as one of these comes upon it, joy departs and it diminishes. So it is with Gold; as soon as it is the first matter of man <note>original: "prima Materia hominis"</note>, it is in its kitchen and loses eight of the 22 degrees. Now there are others, namely better and worse, into which it comes; there it is also to be counted in degrees from the highest 26 up to 30: the lesser degrees are also there. So it is also the nature of Gold to be milder or coarser. This is the cause: the sediment <note>original: "diment"</note> from the stars and other elements that help in the cooking. In the same way that one man is larger or more subtle than another, so also are the types, so that it does not always bring the same degree. This is the reason that it often happens that there is too much Body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, or too much Salt <note>original: "Sal"</note>, or too much Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"</note>, whereby it receives an uneven degree. For instance, too much Salt gives much pale yellow; too much Sulfur <note>original: "Sulphur"</note> gives too much redness: this occurs in the silver-ores when they collapse. For in Nature there is youth just as among men, and the degree is unequal: it also gives a needle <note>A "touch-needle" used for testing purity</note> from 12 up to 24. But if the impurities (which are possible to remove through Art) are taken away—which then happens through antimony <note>original: "Spielglaß"</note>, through quartation <note>original: "Quartier"</note>, and through the Royal Cement <note>original: "Teinett Regal"</note>—then the false weight comes away, and the 24 degrees remain there. Therefore, the Alchemist should not presume to graduate the Gold which is already thus, and not otherwise, for the false weight is lost so that it is a <margin>B</margin> bringing of the right balance <note>original: "Libra"</note>. For what is not of the good there, that cannot be graduated, even though the Gold has left itself in the "kitchen" at the same time. Its recognition is that the Body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is not lost in the Royal Cement, the *Anamomo*, and the Quart; it retains at all times what belongs to a Gold.

For thus there is also white Gold in form, which becomes so from the Sulfur, as stated above: and yet the other two, Mercury and Salt, are white and of a golden nature; these same ones tinge the Sulfurous Body. Thus, when it loses a redness, it becomes white: for the Sulfur receives a tincture <note>original: "Tincuram"</note> into another color, whether it be quite red, or white, or yellow, so they transcolor into the tincture which the Mercury and Salt provide. Therefore, if there are a hundred parts of the Sulfurous Body, then the Alchemical tincture may transcolor much; but if the other tincture—the Alchemical tincture—should tinge the Mercury and Salt from white into red, then that same Gold comes into the colors that Gold should then have. For we should know that there are also complexions in Gold, and in every metal, just as well as in man.

<margin>C</margin> Now regarding this, one should also know that where there is a white complexion <note>original: "Complexio alba"</note>, it is transmuted through a bodily transmutation <note>original: "Transmutationem Corporalem"</note>. Thus the red also; the two colors hang separated in the raw state—the yellow in the white—and are subject to the primary colors. This transmutation in Alchemy also happens so that it is made according to the complexions, and previously tested on man: that a melancholic becomes a sanguine, and also that a black soot becomes a white one, and from the tincture. For Nature in her mineral operation acts similarly to man in his birth: so also should man act similarly in the birth of Nature; he who can prevail over her in such things is he whom Nature has gifted with such mysteries <note>original: "Mysterii"</note> from the "Star of the Arts"—that is the concern of the Astronomers.

<margin>D</margin> Now look also at this: that in such things where Nature is concerned, she is thus created. In Sulfur there is nothing but the Body alone; in Salt also nothing; only in Mercury [is the essence]. What the Sulfur is and what the Salt is, they are there so that one may be a body in the Gold and the other the confirmation. Now what Nature is—that is, what the power, virtue, property, essence, and kind is—all comes from the Mercury <note>original: "ex Mercurio"</note>. Now there is something in Sulfur of a property that belongs to a physical body: yet it is only as a body in that place where the Mercury is not: so it is in the Salt. Now know, however, that the Salt is a balsam and preserves the Mercury, so that its virtues and properties <note>original: "Virtues, vnnd Proprietares"</note> do not rot or become useless. Therefore, that same power is embodied in the Gold, so that after the coagulation in the Salt, when it is separated, it cannot be found through Art; likewise the property of the Sulfur is not found. But all are in the Mercury; they are there. Therefore, when Art separates, it leaves the Body behind and does not regard it as medicine <note>original: "Medicin"</note>; it also leaves the Salt and does not regard it as medicine. Even though a Body has something as a body, and a Salt as a salt: yet these medicines should not be sought in them, but alone in the Mercury; there it all is. For such is the creation: that in all growths of Nature from the four elements, they are not alone, nor do they happen by themselves as understood until now: but they have in them a magnet which, in the decoction and preparation, draws to itself the essences of the three primes <note>original: "trium primarum Effentias"</note>, that is the "Quantum Esse" <note>The essential quantity or being</note>, as the fourth of the elements, the Salt's "Quartum Esse." For the mineral consists in three things: and yet a Mercury is found, and yet the Mercury also loses much of its weight in the final separation.

So now that Nature is thus prepared, and comes to such growth: first, the Gold becomes...

# ON MINERALS

<margin>otherwise: On Sulphurs</margin>

A tree, according to its nature, first puts forth shoots, and after that the branches are formed; then finally comes the fruit. The blossom reveals itself upon the earth in the same manner as it first appears upon a tree. And just as the blossom is the outermost part, while the kernel is still unsettled within the tree, so it is also in the "memory" <note>The "memory" or "matrix" refers to the formative blueprint or internal structure of the mineral vein.</note> of gold and all minerals. When the blossom passes away, then the fruit also comes into being—though not always exactly where the blossom stood. For the "Gold-Tree" is of such a nature that it may extend several hundred fathoms <note>A fathom (Klaffter) is a historical unit of length, roughly six feet.</note> deep within the earth, sometimes appearing at the surface, and sometimes in the middle. 

Thus, there is a distinction between gold and silver in their form: gold is the "male" element, and as such, it possesses greater stability <term>fixation: the alchemical property of a substance to remain unchanged by fire</term> than the other. In contrast, the matter of silver is, in its primary state, like a "female." Although gold and silver share the same primary matter <note>original: "Materia prima"</note>, they are separated by as much as the difference between man and woman.

It is also important to know that gold, in its growth, is so burdened with external influences <note>original: "mit zufall vberladen," referring to impurities or accidental qualities that affect its development</note> that nothing can truly develop except through the "year of Mercury" <note>original: "gerer ano Mercuri" (likely a corruption of "gyrus anni Mercurii"). This refers to the alchemical cycle or "year" required for the transformation and maturation of the metal.</note>.

<header>FIRST TREATISE.</header>
<note>original: "TRACTATUS PRIMUS"</note>
Like iron and steel. Thus shall it also be separated, each into its own kind; so two metals are made from it, distinct in essence, form, and property.

### N O T E.
Thus the metals are revealed, as I have said: namely Gold, Silver, Tin, Lead, Iron, Steel, and Copper-Female and Copper-Male. Thus there are eight of them. But if they are counted as one metal—with Copper-Female and Copper-Male together—then there are six: that is Gold, Silver, Tin, Lead, Iron, Steel, and Copper to be counted as one metal, because the Male is forged within the Female and is not separated, though they ought to be separated from one another.

### ON MIXED METALS.
<note>original: "DE COMMIXTIS METALLIS"</note>
Therefore note now, that a Male is not always alone without its Female, but often they are together, such as Gold and Silver, or Iron and Steel, so that they grow together in one operation, and from the same each retains its own nature. And yet they are within one another, so that neither hinders the other, and they do not come apart by themselves; likewise often Tin and Lead. But where such are together, there is not much to be accomplished, for they do not fit into one body <term>Corpus; the physical substance of a metal</term>, but into several bodies, each needing to be separated specifically.

### ON ADULTERATED METALS.
<note>original: "DE ADULTERINIS METALLIS"</note>
It also happens that metals adulterate themselves: namely, only Gold and Silver mix themselves into the other metals, for the reason that they are the most subtle. And where such First Matter <term>Prima Materia; the primordial "mother" substance from which all things grow</term> is present, so many grow into one another, each for itself. For it may well be that on one tree six or seven fruits are grafted; so also is there a wondrous planting in Nature.

### On Zinc.
<note>original: "Vom Zincken"</note>
There is also a metal, such as Zinc, which is generally unknown. It is a metal of a special kind and of a different seed, yet many metals are adulterated within it. This metal is fluid in itself, for it is made of three fluid kinds, but it has no malleability <note>it cannot be hammered into shape</note>, but only a fusion <note>it can be melted</note>. And its colors are distinct from other colors, so that it is not at all like the other metals as they grow. And it is such a metal that its ultimate matter <term>ultima Materia; the final, perfected state of a substance</term> is not yet known to me. For it is almost as strange in its properties as Quicksilver <note>original: "Argentum vivum"</note>: it accepts no mixing, nor does it endure the fabrication of other metals, but stands for itself.

### On Cobalts.
<note>original: "Von Kobolten"</note>
And again, a metal is produced from Cobalts; this metal can be cast and flows like Zinc, has a particular black color exceeding Lead and Iron, with no glint or metallic shine at all. It can be struck and hammered, yet not so much that it might be used for anything. And its ultimate matter has not yet been found, nor any preparation. For there is no Male or Female, like Iron and Steel, which thus cannot be worked, but must remain as they are until Art <note>meaning the "Art of Alchemy"</note> may find their separation.

### O N  G R A N A T E S.
<note>original: "DE GRANATIS" - likely referring here to garnet-rich ores or granular metallic deposits rather than just gemstones</note>
There is also a special metal found in streams and likewise in moss, in small grains like beans, more or less, which can be cast and hammered by themselves, though not willingly into instruments. Not much can be used of them except for the sake of their properties, whatever may be in them. And it is a fact that if Alchemy finds nothing there, then it will not come to light what it actually is. And they have much "adultery" <note>impurities or mixtures</note> with them, Silver and Gold, which then flows into them as into a Copper or Lead, etc. They are [formed] from a yellow Sulfur, etc.

### Note ON GEMS.
<note>original: "DE GEMMIS"</note>
And there are Garnets of another kind which are transparent, etc., in crystalline form, in which there is Silver and Gold.

### O N  Q U I C K S I L V E R.
<note>original: "DE ARGENTO VIVO"</note>
There is also a metallic kind which can neither be hammered nor cast, and it is the mineral water of the metals. Just as there is water among other things, so is this among the metals. And therefore it must be a metal, because through Alchemy it is brought into malleability and fabrication. Although for the common man it is not stable, sometimes it is stable. Of this, there is much to know: it is the First Matter of the Alchemists <note>original: "prima Materia Alchimistarum"</note>, who from it may make Silver, Gold, Copper, etc., which then tests and proves itself; perhaps Tin, Lead, and Iron also. For its wondrous nature is manifold and cannot be fully fathomed with little effort. But this much it shows: that it is the First Matter of the Alchemists in the generating of metals, and moreover, a great medicine.

# TREATISE ON CACHYMIA, THAT IS, ON
## The Three Imperfect Bodies.
<note>original: "TRACTATUS DE CACHYMIIS, ID EST, De tribus Corporibus imperfectis"</note>

<insert>A</insert> Thus you should also understand regarding these things, that there is a genus of minerals whose nature is metallic, yet they are not metals; nor are they other categories such as Salts. Rather, they are a special kind, of which I indicate several: namely Marcasite <note>Iron pyrites</note>, of which there are many types in red and white; also Bismuth <note>original: "Riβ"</note>, of which there are also many types, red and like Marcasites. After that are the types of Antimony <note>original: "Spießglaß"</note>, of which there are also many types, perfect and imperfect. After that the Arsenicals, of which there are many types. Likewise there are Talcs, Orpiment <note>Arsenic trisulfide; original: "Auripigment"</note>, and many such <term>Cachymia</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for mineral ores or "half-metals" that contain metallic spirit but lack the body of a true metal</note>, namely in many lands of special kind and property; likewise many types of Cobalt.

Now, concerning such things, it is also important to know that they have a certain metallic *prime matter* most closely within them, and come from the metallic *three primes*. The metals—such as gold, silver, copper, lead, etc.—flee to them and incorporate themselves into them. But because they have with them the metallic enemy (of which there are many who are against them), nothing can be extracted. For they are robbers in such a way, just as if a companion were to follow another and take what is his, keeping him imprisoned within himself; and when he should let him go, he kills him and consumes him entirely. Now, from whence these same are born follows hereafter in order.

### The Names of the Cachymia.
<insert>M</insert> Marcasites, Bismuth, Antimony, Cobalt, Talc, Orpiment, Sulfurs, Arsenicals—as many as are known to me.

### On the Origin: A General Introduction.
<insert>A</insert> As the chapter and text are called "On the Three Imperfect Bodies," this refers to a growth of metal, like a foam from a soup or meat. Some are in the *Body of Mercury*, such as Antimony, Arsenicals, and Orpiment. Some are in the *Salt*, such as Talc.

### The Third, Fourth, and Fifth Books of
### Natural Waters.
<note>Decorative initial 'E'</note> Which of these might be the First and Second belonging to these is not yet known at this time: Should they be found in the future, they shall not be withheld from the common benefit. ## On Natural Waters: The Third
### Book, by Theophrastus of Ho-
->henheim.<-
### The First Treatise, on Corporeal Waters.
->I.<-
<note>Decorative initial 'W'</note> Since God has created all things, divided into two uses: one for the preservation of the body, the other for its medicine. As you see, what food, drink, wood, and art He has given, through which we alone adorn and maintain the body. So also has He created for the sicknesses of the body its medicine, so that the body may also turn away its ailments. For when a death comes out of Nature into the people, so that the same Nature is taken away again: that is to say, the sickness does not depart unless Nature drives it away, either in the body or in the medicine. For if such did not happen, then the evil would remain forever among the people. For death comes out of the external Nature, therefore the external health must intervene and proceed toward such healing: that is, the healthy star must take away the unhealthy one. Note therein two kinds of medicine: One that man does not see, which gives healthy years and times; and one that man prepares and governs himself. For God governs one, and it is not in our power; the other we may apply. Therefore, as God is powerful over His own, so should man be in his heaven, that is, in the kingdom of the earth. And just as God does not use His course without foundation and truth under heaven, so should it be maintained by men, by those whom God has ordained, and be completed and used without pride: as the teaching comes from God, and not out of high-mindedness.

->II.<-
So, on the other hand, note also that there are two kinds of causes for sicknesses: One is that which we see and feel; and the other is that which we do not see. And it is to be understood just as if the body became sick, which we see physically, and our shadow on the wall also became sick, and a disturbance arose in it, and the body also had to bear and suffer that same thing. For as unspeakable and invisible as that is, so is it to be fathomed from the external causes that precede our body in its sicknesses, and the body is forced to follow. From this it follows: who has seen the star of the Plague <note>original: "Pestis"</note>, who the star of the One-Day Fever <note>original: "Ephemeræ"</note>, who the wind of death? No one. But that which is poisoned, and that which dies—who has not seen that? For it is greater and more secret than the poison from...
