# ON LUNATICS
<note>Latin: De Lunaticis. In this context, the author explores how "madness" or animalistic behavior stems from man's physical nature.</note>

<margin>A</margin> What makes a man into a beast, that is the same path I lead; if he acts so, he is a beast and no man.

->Matthew 7<-

### You shall not give that which is holy to the dogs,
->nor cast pearls before swine.<-

<margin>B</margin> <insert>I</insert>n this it is understood that dogs—those that are dogs in form and shape—are not the only ones meant. Nor are the swine kept by the miller the only ones meant. Rather, those are meant and presented who look like men but are not. To those same ones, one should give nothing of the holy things, nor give anything of the pearls of the Gospel; let them be. Now know concerning the dogs and swine, since the Scripture points them out, that they are to be understood here as being within the man. For man is indeed twofold: if he were not fundamentally a pig or a dog, then it would be a great lie and blasphemy to scold a man who had God’s image in such a way. <note>The author argues that calling someone a "dog" is only truthful because the person has adopted a literal animal nature, not just as a metaphor.</note> This lies within the man, not in the cattle, yet the man conducts himself like a beast. From this it follows that he may be a pig or a dog: for the animal nature of all beasts is within man, as John says: "You brood of vipers" <note>Matthew 3:7; original: "Ottergezucht"</note>—that is to say, those people possessed that very species, and those others are of the dog species or the swine species. For every man who does not act humanely is equal to the beast he resembles, and he rightly bears its name. And for this reason, even if he is not a dog with hands and feet, the form does not make the pig or the dog; the essence and the dog-nature are what matter, while the form proceeds on its own. For the Scripture calls him a man, yet he is a natural beast in body and essence; both the dog and the man on two feet have the same stomach, the same life, the same flesh, and the same dog-like essence and property. Therefore the Scripture speaks truly, and it is to be understood that man is the animal naturally—not through a parable, but physically, coming from the *Limbo* <term>Limbo: In Paracelsian thought, the "Limbus" is the primordial material or "dust of the earth" from which the physical body was made, containing the seeds of all creatures.</term>. From there he inherits the pig and the dog, given to the spirit from Adam’s life, which is the man. Upon this they tread with their feet: the human feet become swine feet, the mouths become ravenous maws, just as dogs and swine tear at things when they find something to eat. Thus the man, when he is in his beastly nature, also goes about in a dog-like and swine-like manner.

->Matthew 7<-

### In sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

<margin>C</margin> <insert>C</insert>hrist allows a man to be a beast and says himself that he is so inwardly—that is, in his nature. It is as much as if he said: "You look at them outwardly as men, and they resemble men, and they were also created to be men. But now they are not." For the Man in Heaven <note>Referring to Christ or the Divine Image</note> created man out of the *Limbo*; therefore he has the beastly nature, and has placed it alongside the human in his soul; and thus the soul is the beast of the man. They are not men as they appear to be, but inwardly they cannot hide what they are from the *Limbo*: namely, wolves, and ravening wolves. Know then, this is another genus of men, and it is a wolf-genus; just as those mentioned above were dog-genera and swine-genera, so is this species a wolf-genus. A natural wolf, and not a likeness of a wolf, but the wolf itself, in a form that is twofold; he lets the "man" go and uses the wolf’s way, which he could not use if he were not a wolf by birth. If man were not made out of the *Limbo*, he could well excuse himself: for then he would not rot or die, but would be as in the Resurrection: pure and chaste.

->From Matthew 10<-

### I send you as sheep in the midst of etc.

<margin>D</margin> <insert>C</insert>hrist speaks in a parable thus: "I send you as the sheep"—that is, *like* a sheep, but not "You *are* sheep." That is, He does not say, "You sheep, go among the wolves," but "I send you *as* the sheep." But those in the midst of them are the wolves. That is not a parable; they *are* sheep [in nature], and the lovely nature, and the wolves. From this follows: "And be wise as serpents." That is spoken in a parable: for the Apostles were not beasts nor animals, but pure men in the image of God as they should be. Now, because they were not animals, they learned to conduct themselves so that they would be wise, to protect themselves like a serpent. As if he would say: "Look at a serpent, how it protects itself; do the same yourselves, but not with beastly wisdom, but with that which I teach you and will give you in the hour when you have need of it."

# ON LUNATICS <note>original: "DE LVNATICIS"</note>

**A** Furthermore, one should know that the stars have a course which was given to them from the first hour of Heaven and Earth. This same course is of such a nature that no one truly knows its essence. We know well enough that it moves up and down, through one another, in circles, this way or that; but with what conditions and properties <note>original: "Conditionib. Proprietatib."</note> it functions, that is not for us to know. For example: we know that a summer comes, then a winter, then a winter again, and so on until the end of the world. But as for us being able to know exactly *how* the summer can be, that we cannot know, nor is it within our knowledge; for an entire year may be spoiled, yet the specific hour of that change is hidden from us. Even if we already know a little from daily experience, it is still as nothing compared to the primary cause.

**B** Now, the Heavens run their course in such a way, and to our benefit we know, that this course possesses within itself a Reason <note>or "Intelligence"</note> which accords <note>original: "concordiert"</note> with our own human reason; in the same manner as the herbs...

...with the animal understanding <note>original: "viehischen Verstande"</note> so that those who harbor such thoughts are filled with wonder. Now, the things of God are without presumption; for once experienced, it is known that they do not proceed from the animal but from the Divine Spirit. Therefore, faith, which is so high, cannot be fathomed by the beast. For this reason, it surpasses the stars and breaks or shatters the head and the brain. Whatever they undertake must be so: that is, they are marked by it and give so much gain until they fall into derangement. And as soon as they are shattered, they allow themselves to be burned, killed, rubbed away, or driven off, and they consider it all well-done within their animal understanding. Now, note these things well and precisely, for they have a wide reach. He who rages, runs, races, and strikes is full of presumption; yet he who runs in without presumption but possesses human reason is just as much a maniac <note>original: "Maniacus," referring to one suffering from mania or religious delusion</note>.

So that you may digest this better and more easily, note a distinction that Christ gives, saying: "All those who come in my name" (that is, all who come uprightly and not through delusion <note>original: "Ansinning," likely meaning obsessive or delusional</note>) "will perform signs." This means that while many delusional people are born of the beast to lead people astray, you must pay attention to their fruit and signs, etc. If they perform them rightly, then they are my apostles, my martyrs, etc. The animal understanding in humans is greater than in all other animals, for in man is the nature of every beast: the grieving, the daring, and that which is in the wound. His tongue—the ability to speak that is within him—is something other animals do not have, as is the skill to use what is animalistic within him with cunning and likeness. Now, if someone steps forward with such a nature and ponders it, it takes place, and such reason and wisdom come to him that the common people would not recognize the signs of Christ in it. Who would not see him as an angel? <insert>B</insert> And as the Scripture says, even if an angel comes down from heaven, if he does not [speak truth]—this is spoken regarding cunning. Thus, when such a "believer" seeks to fathom things through animal understanding, it is beyond his animal capacity; and what he lacks in reason is supplied by that same star which once ascended in faith. Now it surpasses him in reason, just as if one wanted to take the sun to help him see, and by living with the sun itself, he is blinded. So also these fleshy animal-spirits now go mad and rage within themselves, straying like cattle that have been struck on the head; they run to and fro, and wherever they run out, they become so enraged that they run into fire or water. Thus these believers rely on this animal understanding, for they have nothing else with them except that they live and walk like beasts.

So that you may better know the madness <note>original: "Touby," likely related to 'Toberei' or 'Tobsucht'</note>, the delusion, and the true Mary <note>original: "Mariam," possibly a reference to the contemplative vs. active life or a specific theological figure</note>: One who is meant to be in the same spirit with which Christ speaks and whom Christ teaches, [must leave] all animal desire. Namely, in food, drink, and what belongs to the cellar, along with women—that is, running from their own—for such destroyers run to those things: to food, to drink, to the filling of the belly, to women in marriage or otherwise. Know then that they are animalistic, even though they use the Spirit of Christ (but only in the letter). For the Word of God suffers no "applier" <note>original: "Anleger," one who merely puts on the word externally</note> except one who has the Spirit of God and does not truly rage within himself in a delusion; they believe themselves, and upon that they harden. Secondly, they use animal reason so highly that the stars must help them, and they persuade and shatter human understanding, for among the beasts these things are unfathomable. Therefore, one must borrow wisdom, and it surpasses man as the sun surpasses the eyes. For when they study the Scripture, they find stars that lend to them (unto destruction). If one wants to wage war, he finds strife and fighting; there are stars that help him and lend to him: for all these things are animalistic.

<header>CONCERNING LUNATICS</header>

# ## ###

**A** Why is adultery forbidden? Because it is a beastly labor, not one permitted to the children [of God]; and permission is what makes marriage holy: whatever is not permitted is beastly. Pay close attention to these things, for every wise man knows it is the same with Heaven as it is with Earth; so too with the Soul, the Body, the Spirit, and the Beast. The beastly elements are always companions in all things. But the Spirit looks toward God; it does not fall into "choice"—that is, there is no choice like "I will do this or that" so that the Spirit shall help you; that happens [naturally]. Rather, the Spirit alone, without any intermediary, shows us the way out: thus we must be alone in fellowship and brotherhood, and not divided into two or three, etc. In this beastly nature, every sect huddles together, whereas in Christ there is no sect. Sects spring from the beast; they remain beastly and persist therein, and rage against anyone who does not act from the [true] Foundation from which that thing should proceed. 

Just as when danger is sought by a master who stabs himself and becomes frantic <note>original: "Pſinnig" - likely "sinnig" or "unsinnig," meaning mad or frantic</note>, because he must lean upon the stars. And so also as a physician, whose Foundation comes from the stars, if he speculates a Foundation for himself, he cannot arrive at the Truth. Thereupon, they must follow the "Beast-Stars" in heaven; these turn him about until they persuade him through sharp speculation, which is beyond common beastly understanding. Now, he follows what he is persuaded of. This persuasion is the beginning of insanity <note>original: "Vnsinnigkeit"</note>. Thus they fall into it so completely madly that they care for no one anymore, following their own straight line <note>original: "Fadenrecht"</note> to the highest degree. He who thus resists or allows himself to be led astray is just as insane. Therefore, physicians are insane when they are not properly guided; so are artists and alchemists when not guided—they exalt themselves when they are not given their way, and they talk [nonsense]. There are more such insane people; if one lets them go in peace, they resemble those physicians, alchemists, and artists who follow their own stubborn way; and more, who because they are insane, must not be guided.

**B** Thereupon, let all know how to recognize Heaven in relation to Man, for Heaven and Man have a concordance <note>term: Concordans - a harmonious correspondence between the macrocosm (universe) and microcosm (human)</note>: just as a marriage is between Man and Woman. There, the woman should follow the man; but if the man follows what the woman wants, he is insane, for he is no longer himself and borrows his reason. And anyone who does not use his own reason is a *Lunaticus* <note>term: Lunaticus - a "moon-struck" person or lunatic</note>, doing what the Moon <note>original: "Luna"</note> wants—that is, what his "Barbarian" <note>note: likely referring to the lower, unrefined nature</note> wants. Thus Heaven is also a woman, adorned with all the cunning and cleverness with which Eve outwitted Adam and brought him into beastly reason. Thus, know that we have born within us as our property the beastly understanding: to lie, to deceive, to hold onto good and evil as part of our own nature. Now, if we do not protect ourselves from this, beastliness proceeds, not the human spirit. Then the Ascendant <note>term: Ascendens - the astrological sign rising on the eastern horizon, thought to influence personality</note> governs and imprints itself; in short, just as if your wife imagines something for you and says "do this," and the man does it, and in the end he goes astray and knows not the way out. If one finds a "warrior" in heaven, he wants to be a soldier—that is his Ascendant. If he wants to be truthful, he finds his Ascendant. If he wants to be a lover, or a thief, or a warrior, etc., it is the same.

**C** Know that we bring no Ascendant with us from birth; we only take one when we wish to. Therein lies the falsehood of Astronomy and Astrology, and all those who practice Prognostication and the like, and whatever involves the Ascendants. According to how they are used, so they are—one almost or more insane than the other. For as all know, any merchant who conducts a business, if he gives [false measure] and strikes back, and does not love his neighbor but craves his goods, he finds the stars to show him the way, for they know it. Is he not insane? Yes. For the cause is: he who leaves his Creator must be a raging man, a mad man, and a possessed man. And through Trines and Quartiles <note>term: Trinis and Quartis - astrological aspects (120 and 90 degrees) used to predict fate</note> they become entirely insane—more insane than those chained to the wall. They have no more reason; though they have the appearance of reason like a man, they blind themselves and are against God, like the madmen put in chains; they abandon the [true] way. If they could, they would strangle it.

That there is much more to write here about the Ascendants upon which the [stars] depend is not necessary to relate here. For my purpose is only to write concerning Lunatics. But before this volume is finished, that same Foundation will also be taken up. Thus, know further how to recognize the insane: they do not act from the Spirit as a man should, but from the [beastly] spirit as mentioned. Therefore, their stars rise and fall like the Wheel of Fortune is painted, which only takes its origin from the beastly nature. For if they were in the Spirit and walked therein as a man should, they would not fall or rise, as David says: *Blessed are those who walk in the way of the Lord.* <note>original: "Selig sind die da wandlen im Weg deß Herren"</note> But if we do not, it must go for us as it does for the "Buseligen" <note>note: likely "busselig" or "pusselig," meaning confused or giddy</note>—that is, like the beasts. Now understand...

# BOOK OF PHILOSOPHY
<page-num>172</page-num>

<margin>A</margin> and depart, as the astronomers say in their practices <note>original: "Practicken" – refers to astrological calendars or prognostications</note>: this year the merchants will have a good year in one month, and in another month bad luck, etc. Likewise for soldiers, likewise for artists, etc. If these things were not disorderly, and people kept themselves in the way of the Lord, they could well understand the prophets in the manner in which they are recognized; and for that reason, they sway the spirit, and the "Augurs of the Heavens" <note>original: "Augures Coeli" – sky-diviners</note> do not indicate these things. By this, one recognizes the insane nature of those who thus wander up and down, back and forth, in such constellations, all of which is not Christian. Therefore, know the sum of this treatise: that my intention is solely directed toward recognizing the human being—in what way he walks, so shall it go for him according to that same way. If he walks as a Christian, it goes for him thus; if he walks as a beast, it goes for him thus. So that if he walks in Christ, he goes as Christ leads him; if he walks as a beast, it goes for him as the stars and the "calvish intellect" <note>original: "Kälberiſch Verſtand" – a derogatory term for foolish, animalistic reasoning</note> lead him. With this, I wish to have concluded the third treatise and begin the fourth, concerning the healing of lunatics.

### TREATISE IV.
->ON THE CURE.<-

<sig>B</sig> It is further intended to undertake the signs in the face of the heavens, that is, the stars, so that we may recognize them at their best. Thus, we should first know the onset <note>original: "Anſinnige" – the beginning of a mental affliction or "insanity"</note> and the first [moment] in which planet, zodiac, etc., he has fallen, and according to that, begin the healing. For instance, if he were seen in the speculation of the spirit, then Saturn would have seen his wife <note>original: "Weib" – here used in an alchemical or astrological sense of a "mate" or complementary force</note>. For every star is a woman. Now the cure must stand against Saturn. If he had brought Venus upon himself in an ascendant, one must conduct the cure against Venus; and likewise with Mars, with the Moon, with the Sun, with Mercury, with Jupiter. And do not think only that there are seven alone; there are many thousands of them, all of which are to be considered.

<margin>B</margin> First, know that the preventatives <note>original: "Präſeruatiſſ" – prophylactic measures</note> should come first, and after them the cure according to the indicated rules <note>original: "Canonem"</note>. Here is a short rule: that you break the beastly intellect. For example, if one wishes to steal, stumble, and exalt himself in faith, then measure the signs of which Christ spoke: "Do it, let him be, and say nothing to him." But if not, take heed whether the fur belongs to the fox, whether he be a wolf, or a dog, or a sow—that is, where he intends to fall, into what star: toward spirit, toward war, toward lying, toward the "hourly" <note>original: "Horär" – likely referring to horary astrology or temporal whims</note>, toward violence, etc. Likewise, from the investigation where you notice how he wishes to suffer, if there is no preventative said beforehand and alongside this—because he does not do what Christ said and commanded, that God be there as an apostle or prophet—then turn him away from his beastly intellect, explain to him, instruct him. If he accepts it, it is good. If not, tell it to the neighbor. Let him be warned; if not, tell it to the church. If it will not help, treat him like the heathens <note>original: "Etnſchen" – ethnikoi/gentiles</note>, cast him into the outer darkness, so that he does not seduce the whole city, his house, or the land with the power of his poetic spirits <note>original: "Dichgeiſtern" – spirits of delusion or false imagination</note>. For where such "beast-prophets" arise, there is the devil's hen-coop; he waits for it, promotes it, drives it forward, and begins it in the community. Since he is like that among the heathens, he is better off among the Christians than in the church.

For who can root out these things otherwise, if serious words will not help, but an authority <note>original: "Oberkeite"</note>? That is the preventative; that is why it is there. But where they overlook this and forget the honor of Christ, and say things otherwise than Christ says, then it goes ill for the land. For the King and the authorities are children—that is, they do not discern these things. It is better that the insanity be taken in the preventative respectably, so that they are completely deafened, than at the end; for at the last they persist and remain, and it is easy to fear the persistence and the intrusion of the evil spirit. Since Christ says so much about false prophets, false Christians, and false apostles, such people are to be highly measured—more than it behooves me to write here as a natural philosopher.

Likewise, know also if one rages and wishes to wage war: prevent him also as stated above. If he will not, it is better that he be placed among the heathens than that he should strangle one who desired nothing from him, and do to other people what he would not want them to do to him. So that such vice and "un-peaceability" <note>original: "anverſterblichkeit" – likely a variant of "unverträglichkeit"</note> be avoided, no one should be exempt from the punishment of the heathens.

Likewise, if the insanity goes into gambling, raving, whoring, and the like in such labor, do as above: if not, cast it into the power of the heathens. It is better that they lie in that state than that one should expect such evil and eat such poison that grows from them in the future, and give no excuse nor permission for it.

Likewise with the usurers <note>original: "Buchern" – likely "Wucherer"</note> and merchants, do also thus: remind them of the Ten Commandments, the commandment of Christ, of the dear neighbor. Do it for yourself first, then with your neighbor, then with the church. If he will not desist, it is better he be cast among the heathens. For one should consider the malice that comes from the merchants, which shall appear and stand before our eyes. For the things that grow upon them are unfathomable to explain. For the devil throws himself into such things where he otherwise could not mix in.

Similarly, if one rages in the arts, do to him also thus: present his error to him, what he cannot do or what he can do. If he will not believe you, and your companion, and the church: it is better that he have a millstone around his neck and be cast into the sea than that his art, as he held it before him, should have a progress into the work, through which falsehood, deceit, murder, stealing, etc., spring forth.

# ON LUNATICS
<margin>A</margin>
Thus it is understood by everyone that the **preventatives** <note>original: "Præseruatiuen"</note> alone rest in the hands of the **authorities** <note>the ruling civil or religious powers</note>, when nothing else will help.

But further, if the preventatives have not been used, and it has come to the point that they have been overcome and no longer know themselves: then truly I can give no other counsel than to proceed cautiously by two processes. The first: if they still have a path of **reason** running alongside their **insanity**, to take hold of that. Secondly: where that is not found within them, to use the medicine that **Christ** teaches regarding the **possessed**: with **fasting** and **prayer**, through the observance of the commandment, "love your neighbor as yourself."

Regarding the first: if a wise man were in a city, sitting in council, giving reports, and held in honor—for such things no one may be insane, but must be wise—yet alongside this he carries on a trade as a **shopkeeper** or **merchant**, and in that specific area he is maddened, yet he considers his way right, persists in it, and honors it as just: then take for yourself the rational path in which he still walks. That is, with that same reason, split his "horn" <note>an idiom for breaking someone's pride or stubborn delusion</note> and recount to him what you have to say, even as he looks upon you as the insane one. If it helps, it is good; and take two or three others with you. Likewise the **Church**: if he will not listen, make a **pagan** <note>original: "Ethnicum"</note> out of him. For he is so insane that he cannot follow, because he is in the wrong. Therefore, one must fear that the **devils** are also there; thus it is not unjustly advised to turn to prayer and fasting. 

Likewise, if one is a **whore-monger**, a **gambler**, a **robber**, a **thief**, etc., he always has a side-path of **certainty** <note>or conscience/conviction</note> within him; lead him by that same way as before. Where that will not follow, there is no other way; for as long as certainty can be sensed in such a deaf person, he should be well-sought and exhorted. For it is a hard thing for a **rich man** to enter this Church; it were easier for a **camel** <note>original: "Rämelthier"</note> to go through a **needle's eye** than for a rich man to enter the **Kingdom of Heaven**. Therefore it is hard and difficult for them to <sig>B</sig> leave [their ways]; therefore you and the Church must speak with them about leaving it. This is why the preventatives should be undertaken while they are not yet rich or established, for then they are easier to turn and to govern. But once they have grown up and risen, they learn [their vices], and it is hard to take away what they have undertaken, especially if they do not follow Christ. For once it has come to that, it is more than hard to lift them out.

But if reason does not teach and the **conscience** cannot be felt, but rather there is only a complete, mad insanity—**wild**, **thievish**, stubborn, and having nothing of soul or body to live for, neither for themselves nor others—then we should, out of the commandment to love our neighbor, lead them into fasting and prayer, and we along with them should think thus: "In the misery in which you are, in that same misery we wish to preserve you and ourselves, taking your yoke and burden upon our backs, and thereby worship God our Redeemer to release you." For truly, such people are to be recognized as not far from the possessed and the afflicted. And in the end, they will be brought into no other order except through fasting and prayer.

For who can tame **Mars**, and **Saturn**, and the other **stars**? Who can make known their manifold wickedness in such a form? Since they do nothing else but obsess the human **spirit**, though they have nothing to do or trade with the human being, and they take away his correct understanding so that he casts out the true man, forgets his **God**, and clings to **errors**, worships **images**, holds to the stars, and speaks whatever they teach him.
<sig>C</sig> Therefore, no medicine is to be found here, except entirely as was said of the possessed.

And although it is true that **Nature** has many medicines for the insane: know that I do not place them here, and this is the reason: Nature speaks of **Mania**, and for that there is a cure; but this is **Lunaticus** <note>moon-influenced madness</note>, and not Mania, therefore natural counsel helps nothing. No natural medicine helps against the **spirits of the stars** when they possess a human being. Just as a blind man who is blinded by the **weather**, the **heavens**, the **sun**, etc., nothing helps him anymore; he remains so, as far as he is ruined. But that which comes from Nature, Nature heals again.

What further wickedness is in the stars, and what **extravagance** <note>original: "Vppigkeit"</note> we should guard ourselves against, I will strike out <note>or elaborate</note> in other books. What I have written here in this book about **Lunatics** happened for the reason that you might recognize the human being, in what way he walks and acts, so that **brutish reason** is not mistaken for the **light** of man. For the **Apostles** were pure men; therefore Christ called them the **Lights of the World** and the **Salt of the Earth**.

->But those who are not so, they walk in **darkness**; they are not lights, but darkness. This is the reason for this writing, to instruct you in this.<-

# ON THE GENERATION
## OF FOOLS
### BY THEOPHRASTUS <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541).</note>
#### TREATISE I.

### Prologue.

<image-desc>Large ornate initial capital 'I' at the beginning of the paragraph.</image-desc>
It is a matter of great wonder that, since God has redeemed man so highly and dearly with His death and the shedding of His blood, He allows that same man to be born as an unwise person. Such a person can neither recognize nor understand His name, His death, His honor, His signs, His works, or His kindness shown toward humanity; he is robbed of all the reason and wisdom that belongs thereto. Furthermore, since man is an image of God, he must thus be afflicted with and appear as a fool, a simpleton, or an ignorant person. Yet, since man is the noblest creature of all, he must stand as if shameful before all other creatures, even though all other creatures are free <note>original: "gefreyet," meaning free from the burden of sin or the specific mental "imprisonment" of folly</note> and man alone is not. Now, the reasons for this are many, not all to be recounted here in this preface. But this is a great thing: that God does not look upon the person, yet died for many—namely, He redeemed them all. However, beyond that, there are fools and simpletons among men, and it is difficult to find the cause. As far as nature is concerned, the cause is easy to find, for man may well be the master of nature in fathoming such things. Furthermore, that a thing is born is a heavy matter, for what birth gives, who can name it or take it away? It is all the more difficult that fools are born and it is not a sickness; they are uneven, and have no vision nor herbs whereby they might become wise. Additionally, although Christ healed many sick, possessed, and lepers, and all kinds of misery, nothing has been found for this. It is not possible for Nature. There must also be a great *Arcanum* <term>Arcanum: a secret, powerful remedy or "deep mystery" in Paracelsian medicine</term> that could turn the things that fools have within them, but nothing is there. Therefore, it must be a great *Mysterium* <term>Mysterium: a divine or natural mystery beyond ordinary understanding</term> that is hidden in Nature to be fathomed: specifically, why man alone becomes a fool, though he is the noblest creature who should be entirely without blemish or lack. But these things are all to be set aside; since it has been ordained, one must philosophize about things as they have happened. There is nothing to say regarding medicine, therefore this book of the treatise will lack that, and in the other treatises only their origin, source, and customs are to be seen. Not to make them known, but to inform everyone who takes these things upon himself, so that he may know what man is and upon what he stands. And that he may consider that his wisdom is nothing before God, but that we are all equal to fools in our wisdom. And as much as we marvel and devise in our animal reason, all that is equal to these fools, and Christ alone must be our helper, otherwise we are all fools. Therefore, the fools, our brothers, stand before us just as we are friends and one in blood. Thus we are [the same], though one might be a fool and the other quite wise; yet one blood is there, and thus also one reason; one is as noble as the other. So also, one is as wise in animal reason before God as the other. And He who redeemed the wise has also redeemed the fool, just as He did the wise.

### BOOK ONE
#### TREATISE I.

<image-desc>Large ornate initial capital 'J' at the beginning of the paragraph.</image-desc>
Now, since God intended to create man, and to create him according to His image, and also to set him in Hebron <note>A traditional site associated with the creation or burial of Adam</note>, man had to be created pure. Although all creatures are free, man was made from the *Limbus* <term>Limbus: in Paracelsus's theory, the "great chaos" or primordial matter from which all things were extracted</term>, and this same *Limbus* contained the nature and properties of all creatures; therefore, man shall also be called the *Microcosmus* <term>Microcosm: the "little world," reflecting the entire universe (macrocosm) within the human body</term>. For such reasons, God kept man so pure that the properties born of the *Limbus* did not bleed through or break forth, but remained entirely clear. Thus He placed and brought a pure man into Paradise: although he was potentially stained with all things, it was unknowingly. For if one does not know that which is within him, he cannot do it, and does not do it. Now, this man is clean and pure, even though that [potential] is within him. Just as a maiden, while she is pure, does not know what it is to be a woman, even though she is one [potentially]; so it was with Adam and Eve, in whom the nature of all creatures existed, but they did not know it. Therefore, no impurity or vanity could or did happen there. But because man was of the world, and led from the world into Paradise, and the secrets were given to him there, the Leviathan <note>The serpent or devil</note> took him...

<summary>Paracelsus introduces a philosophical and theological study of "fools," arguing that while their condition is a natural mystery, all human wisdom is foolishness before God. He begins the first book by describing man's creation as a "Microcosm" from the primordial Limbus, originally pure in Paradise until the intervention of the Leviathan.</summary>

<header>THE GENERATION OF FOOLS.</header>

# THE GENERATION OF FOOLS.
<note>original: "GENERATIO STVLTORVM"</note>

...a cause to show him what he was. Now, if he had not seen him out of the Limbo <note>The "Limbo" here likely refers to a state of primordial chaos or potentiality before physical manifestation</note>, he would not have tempted him to join him; nor would it have appeared to Adam and Eve in such a way that they could have done what the Leviathan <note>The author uses "Leviathan" here as a name for the Tempter or the devilish force</note> desired. But because they [possessed both Good] and Evil, only they did not recognize or know it: it happened to them just like [a young girl] who does not know who she is, but she sees a young boy before her; she loves him, yet knows not for what purpose or why, and yet desires him. And then the boy [comes] and offers her food to eat; and she, out of ignorance of the bite, tastes it: [and so she learns of Good] and Evil. Thus the Leviathan, because in Eve and Adam a wonderful nature [existed], he [tempted] them and caused them to fall in their virginity; for which reason they were then driven out [of the Garden] of Hebron <note>The author associates the earthly site of Hebron with the original site of Paradise or the creation of Adam's body</note>, and returned to the place from which they were made (where [they], not knowing and unable to be advised, were to be used and tended). As [man] was originally ordained for Paradise and created therein Pure and Chaste, entirely guided and placed in the Image of God, until the Leviathan brought him to his Fall: then he lost [his] Freedom and his true Nature, and became therefrom a Worldly Man, burdened with [earthly] things in the world until the very last human being.

B Following this, when they came out of Paradise, they were no longer [perfect], but rather fragile, mortal, miserable humans, and subject to all misery. [Then] they perceived what the world was; there they felt the Moon, Mars, [Saturn, Jupiter], Mercury, and the harsh signs of the Zodiac, and every star in [the heavens]. [Then they felt] the misery of the world and the wretchedness of mankind, thus: they saw what [they] were, and saw that there was a breaking of beauty, of fairness, [and that all] things were fragile; they saw the many sicknesses of children, the many [evils], the many disagreements, discord, and all misery. Therefore know that [Man] was created Righteous in the Image of God, and Chaste, Pure, Healthy, [and] led [into] Paradise, and given a land there above all lands, where neither Death [could reach him], nor Sickness nor Impurity, neither the Uncreated nor Enemies. [But when they] came out into the world, there was nothing but weeping and gnashing [of teeth], and what [was perfect in his] creation was taken from him, and he was deprived of the perfect Image. [From this] arose the origin of murderers, warriors, and thieves: for they [lost] Piety, Integrity, Chastity, Discipline, and Nobility. Then there were whoremongers, then there were gamblers, then [deformed] children, then the blind, then the deaf, then the mute, then the lame, then [the sickly], then monstrosities and the like, which thus continue on and on until the end of the world without ceasing. For the world's way, property, and essence begets these things every day, one after another and in heaps. And so certain are these breakings [of the body and soul], and so firmly and constantly preserved, that no one can nor may turn them away: [as the world turns] out, one child must be born blind, another lame, another crooked, another thus: one a fool, another [a simpleton]. [Such is] the world's property; thus the children of the world become. [Therefore], because we have come into such misery and are subject to fragility, [we must] write and include the Philosophers' [views] on whence fools [get their nature] and origin. To recount the same is right to put forward, seen [in light of man] with his perfection: and thereafter from the expulsion of [Paradise], so that man must fall hard into the nature of his [earthly] kind, and [be] broken [in] health, in truth, in fairness, in beauty; [and how] greed and all [manner of] breaking occurred and grew.

C It is to be pitied, and more than lamented, that God allowed His Image to be so [diminished], deprived of the properties of Hebron and all Divine Imagery, and allowed [man] to become crooked, lame, blind, deaf, and mute: even though God Himself [is perfect] in [His] Image, and man has lost it. And although he still boasts of it and recognizes it: Oh, but when he looks at himself, how far [he is] from the Divine Image! How could [he boast]? Like a peacock who is beautiful, but when he sees his feet, he sees his [ugliness]. [How can we] say that we stand in the Divine Image? Nevermore: we may [say] that we once stood therein: but in Hebron, not in the world. In the world [we are] from the [fallen] man; from the [other] we are displaced. We may well say we are [made] according to the Divine [Image], but we do not say we are still fashioned as it is. He who [is] according to the Divine Image [and remains so] must not die, he must not walk upon the [mortal] world, he must be Immortal [and free] of [suffering]: if not, then the creation, as it should be, is broken. [Man is] surrounded by misery: for how can the blind man say he has the Divine Image? [How can] the fool say it? Whether it be internal or external: had we been in [the Image], had we stood according to the Divine Image, it would have been Eternal, without death, without poverty, and without all tribulation. But now we are far removed from that, and [are] merciful <note>The author likely means "pitiable" or "in need of mercy" here</note> humans, and subject to all elements, and everything that [is] in [them].

# BOOK OF PHILOSOPHY CONCERNING

<margin>A</margin>
the spirit, the pygmies <note>original: "Pigmeen"; Paracelsian elemental beings of the earth</note>, the nymphs, fate <note>original: "Fatum"</note>, the augurs, and Satan; and furthermore, there is no star in heaven that lets us plead, no herb we dare take without worry, no drink of wine without concern. We are cast into the midst of such wolves and against life itself. This is why we are never certain of our children—what will be born: here a <term>M. la.</term> <note>likely an abbreviation for "Mola," a "false conception" or uterine growth</note>, there a monster <note>original: "Monstrum"</note>, there fools, there thieves, there murderers, there robbers, etc. But it is not necessary to recount all these miseries, but rather to speak further of the birth of the "Mark" <note>likely referring to the essence or character</note>: in what way and form a wise man begets a fool, and in what way a rogue begets. Along with this, how a fool or a jester begets a wise man; these are the properties of the world. But let each take up his cross and follow after to the place where we are invited.

However, so that you may know how fools are made: they are created solely by heavenly teachers and un-masterful masters, and in this manner. You know that a master who does his work carves well; a stonemason likewise works upon the stone and produces work. For no complete master ruins his work. It is the apprentice <note>original: "Jungen"</note> who keeps practicing until he finally hits the mark; but until then, it is worth nothing, it is ruined, and it is a work one must laugh at when seen. Now know this: man sows man, but he does not *make* him. Since he sows, he must have a Maker. The farmer sows the seed, but man sows man, and <term>Vulcanus</term> <note>The archetypal smith or "inner alchemist" who forges form</note> makes him. And yet Vulcan alone does not do it; rather, Vulcan is like one who makes an image, but not alone, for he has the wood and himself. It is to be understood thus: the trunk of the wood becomes much when man adds to it in his sowing. Now, once the wood has grown (as with a woodcarver), the carver begins; as the wood is, so he makes an image from it. Thus it lies with the wood, and it lies with the master; they both make the image. Furthermore, know that man provides the wood, and Vulcan carves him. Now, however, in this carving of fools,

<margin>B</margin>
it is not Vulcan himself there, but apprentices who ruin it. Thus there is a [ruined work] if they are poorly formed and poorly proportioned. Now, however, know concerning Vulcan: What is there that does not grow up young again? And what is there that does not increase and decrease? All things that exist renew themselves and pass out of the Moon <note>original: "Mond"</note>, which alone is visible to every farmer; it grows old, it wanes, and then near the Sun it becomes a young moon. In its youth, up to its [fullness], its potency, impression, quality, and nature are far apart from one another. So it is also with Vulcan: he becomes young, he carves, he grows old, and he becomes ever [weaker]. Thus it is ordained, and man is not master of himself such that he might do more than provide the wood. Furthermore, it has come into his hand as the master builds. Thus these regions have their Vulcans, the houses <note>original: "Edes"</note> have their Vulcans, the times of the year have their Vulcans; he who hits the mark is the saddest. Of these, the firmament describes itself: for these Vulcans are many [kinds of] fools. And the apprentices ruin the carving so violently and are so sluggish that one rarely escapes without a fool being made.

The masters do not grow old while they are at their best and most capable; they are forever young masters, which is what makes so many fools. For it goes as it does with the moon. Now, there is not just one Vulcan, but many. Each has his own hammer and carver, and carves for himself a particular image. Then men are distinguished and separated from one another; that is, their [nature] follows from this. They are also not given the same senses: for that which is not [made the same] cannot have the same senses. Therefore, many kinds of [forms] are made, and thus also many kinds of senses. Now know this: the nature of fools cannot be [easily] explained, nor their "naturities" <note>original: "Naturiteten"; the specific natural characteristics</note>. Therefore, he is a poor astronomer who cannot describe fools and read their "naturities"; such a person can even less describe or recognize things in the future with his *tricks.

How then should one [know], since one was not sitting by the marriage bed and watching? He who knows nothing of the stone-hut <note>the mason's lodge or workshop</note> lets them work without explanation. That reflects poorly on the (recognized art), as they say.

Now, to prevent these things further is not possible. But he is drunk and drumming: now, in that drumming, the inner body is so powerful that it speaks out from within him what the inner body wants to have, and that same thing remains clumsy and mixed with animal reason. For the fool is so fashioned that he can mock us just like the wise man who possesses such reason, or he speaks what is dear to him, whether it comes out rightly or wrongly. Therefore, the fool is more to be regarded in his speaking than the wise man, because he does not resist the true human being with the animal body.

<margin>*</margin> And it is, however, in the same way a thing for us to understand through deprivation: since fools are of such a kind and speak the truth—which does not come from the poetic spirit <note>original: "Dichgeist," referring to the inventive or fabricating mind</note>—that <gloss>(they)</gloss> the wise man himself considers it, and looks upon it, and contemplates that his body, which is no fool, should make him into a fool, and thus also come forth without resistance. For look at the prophets, whom God especially chose; He made the animal body of them all "mad" <note>original: "doll," meaning crazed or senseless in a worldly way</note>, and now out of such making mad and making drunk, the true spirit stood there, and nothing resisted him, and nothing was forgotten by him. Therefore they were looked upon as simple folk and thus despised in such simplicity. And those are closest to God who walk in simplicity, for they have no conflict with the true [spirit]. Their sayings and teachings also came forth as if drunken, and were not set in order as the animal body is accustomed to do, which is easily led. And so the fools are held to be such, and through the simple ones great prophecies have occurred. For the spirits are within the human being, and [the body] is subject to them in animal reason—that is, that same reason does not resist. Thus that same body speaks out what a spirit knows, which spirit is then innate to the human being and possessed by nature, with which God also [endowed] the human being. They are fools because they are not masters of their reason. And that is the best thing in a person: one who does not let the "fool's reason" <note>here meaning worldly, calculating logic</note> rule over him. We despise fools because they are not "animalistic" <note>meaning worldly-wise or cunning</note> as we would be if we were born fools. Therefore, let everyone consider that he [kills] the animal understanding within him, so as to teach the true human being to come forth, and to teach arts, and to seek wisdom. No one [needs to bring it from outside], for everyone carries it within himself, of which we then have manifest knowledge; that teaches more than the letter. Not the "poetic body" <note>the fabricating self</note>, let that be an instrument and nothing more, and let it be good and useful to the human being. And do not teach him that he alone is the spirit—alas—which was given to the human being. Thus did Lucifer; he esteemed himself to be that which he was not, he who came from Heaven.

But when [fools] are brought to words or set in the market, they should be despised by no one. For many prognostications are presented thus from the foundation, and the most truthful is the spirit of the human being: as soon as it falls into the mind, out with it! For where that does not happen, then [fabrication] falls into it and wants to give it a shape, which "giving of shape" is a lie and a falsification of the truth. Therefore, let reflecting and contemplating occur out of the "poetic spirit" and not out of the true human being, whether it turns out well or ill. Thus it is, and especially with fools, who are not driven about by men. For with that same driving-about one breaks them, and cunningly sets them in "fools' places," and they enter into the fantasy with which they are driven, and thus the true spirit is struck back. But it well becomes a Prince not to let the fools or simple people at his court be led astray: let them proceed in their jests as nature gives it to them, and notice all things, and weigh them well.

<margin>6</margin> Now it is also the case that the stars are in the fools, and they lead and drive them. This is an indication that we are all subject to the Heavens, and that everyone who casts the true human being away from himself is driven by the Heavens, like the fools and other such simpletons. Therefore we recognize that while the Heavens play in the fools, so [they also play] in all of us humans. That is: our wisdom is toward God as the fools' wisdom is toward the Heavens. And as we drive the fools about and laugh at them, so is our wisdom which God has given us. This is not to be understood as if God were playing with us <unclear>...</unclear>

And Death separates the two bodies in their life from one another: first the animal understanding, then the human understanding. It takes that long for him to kill the animal and lead the human beneath the Cross of Christ, to dwell there until the Day of Resurrection. Then we shall come together and see that our mockery, which we held against them, will turn back upon ourselves in repentance, and our contempt is a judgment upon ourselves; and we shall remember that we should not call our brothers "fools." For we do not know what we are; God alone is the judge and knower of these things. Even if Nature has failed, there is nothing failed in the soul and the spirit; they [are no less] than one who was born crooked, lame, or without feet, so that he must [watch] another who can run well. When the two come together in that world, which of them will be lame? Neither. Therefore, no one should be esteemed or called a fool or a simpleton, since it is only Nature that has failed, into which we have fallen: for Adam and Eve shall neither harm nor benefit us against one another here in this world.

## Prologue.

<image-desc>Decorated initial capital 'W'</image-desc>Although the creation of all natural things is known and in good knowledge to us, and everything that God has created—each land recognizes its own that is within it and grows there; each human has his own knowledge of himself; likewise, every craft and trade carries knowledge within its subjects—through such things, all the creatures that God created are recognized, and nothing is hidden that is not or shall not be known to man. Not that everything is in one person—that is, that one man knows it all—but each knows his own. When they all come together, [it is seen] that not just one land has all knowledge, but only its own. When they all come together, then everything is known. And every city, village, house, etc., carries its own knowledge of all natural things. Furthermore, in the crafts and trades in which all creatures are used, some in this and some in that: and thus everything is used and experienced for what purpose it was created. And so it concludes at last in this: that everything serves man and is subject to him. Now, however, beyond that which the natural light <note>term: "Naturlich liecht" — the Light of Nature, a Paracelsian concept meaning the innate intelligence within the physical world</note> grasps and recognizes, there is something that reaches and is elevated even further, solely against the light of nature—that is, in the light of the nature of man, which is above the light of nature, there it is fathomed. Through this, she [Nature] may be recognized by her own shine. But in the [higher light], outside the light that is born in Nature: that is the light [through which one] experiences, learns, and fathoms [divine] things. Those who seek this light of nature, seek the light of the human, who speaks about Nature. For man [is more than] Nature; he is also a spirit, he is also an angel: of all three [he has a part]. [When he is] in Nature, he serves Nature; if he walks in the spirit, he serves the spirit [as] an angel. The first is given to your body, the others are given to the soul. [Know] now that man has a soul, and the two [spirit and angel] alongside it. Therefore he triumphs over Nature, to fathom...

<margin>A</margin>Also, that which is not in Nature is to be experienced and fathomed: Hell, the Devil, and his kingdom. Likewise, man fathoms Heaven and its essence, namely God and His kingdom. For he who must go to a place should first know the essence of that place, as far as he desires to wander there. Man must also recognize the knowledge of Nature as it exists, and what wonders God has given and created. For it is the office of man that he should experience things and not be blind therein; for he was created for this purpose: to speak of and present the wonders of God. Every essence and property is possible for man to fathom. For nothing is created that is not to be fathomed by man; and it was created so that man should not go about idle, but walk in the way of God—that is, in His works. Not in vice, not in fornication, not in gambling, not in carousing, not in gaining wealth, nor in gathering treasures for the worms; but his spirit, his light, and his dealings should be to contemplate divine things. It is more blessed to write of the Nymphs <note>water spirits</note> than to write of the religious orders; it is more blessed to write of the origin of Giants than to write of courtly etiquette; it is more blessed to write of Melusina <note>a legendary female spirit of fresh water</note> than to write of chivalry; and of the Earth-men <note>original: "Archelle," likely referring to earth spirits or gnomes</note> and the miners, than to write of fencing and serving ladies. For in these things are Divine works; in the other things the spirit is used to serve the malice of the world and its pleasure in pride and impurity. He who experiences and hears much on earth shall also be learned in the resurrection; he who knows nothing shall see nothing. We are all learned, but not equally; all wise, but not equally; all skillful, but not equally. He who fathoms deeply is the greatest. For fathoming God shuns the vices of the world, flees the service of the world, courtly discipline, estates, fine gestures, and lying curses. But the wonders of God are taught by the 
<margin>B</margin>light of man, and he does not ask the tongues <note>human speech/authorities</note> about it. Discipline toward God—that is man’s constitution. What is man but a shadow, which is nothing? Man pays for no discipline, rewards nothing in it, dies away, and in death it is like smoke. Why then does man make a show of discipline, and leave true discipline aside, and the love of his neighbor? Now the good tree puts forth its bloom and its fruit. How great is he who, in foreign lands, meditates upon his Creator; he finds pearls that shall not be given to the swine. But he who meditates only on man, he seeks pearls like a sow that turns everything over and finds nothing useful to him. Thus, know further how to understand the beginning of this book: not that I write of lovely things and eloquence, but of supernatural things which do not need eloquence, but rather let the chatter be and remain what it is.

<margin>C</margin>First, in what I present to you, it is proper to explain the matter about which I shall subsequently write, and what it is. Know then that the content of this book is to write of the four races of spirit-people: namely, the Water-people, the Mountain-people <note>gnomes/pygmies</note>, the Fire-people <note>salamanders</note>, and the Wind-people <note>sylphs</note>. Among these four races will be treated the Giants, the Melusinas, the Venusberg <note>the legendary subterranean realm of Venus</note>, and similar histories. Fifth, the birth and origin of Giants, and how children are born of them—though not of the same race as our race. How these things relate to us is to be named. First, their creation and what they are; second, their land and habitation where they are, and what their government is; third, how they come to us and allow themselves to be managed, and mingle and dwell with us; fourth, how they perform certain special wonders, such as Melusinas, the Venusberg, and similar histories; fifth, the birth and origin of Giants, and likewise their destruction and return. Now, it is less likely that a philosopher should be built upon the Scriptures and take his foundation from them [in this matter], as there is nothing specifically written in them regarding their nature or for research, except for the Giants, of whom some things are handled elsewhere in the Scriptures. Yet the cause lies in the foundation that the works appear and are true. Likewise, as magic spreads and appearances occur, and their origin is presumed, so these things are also fathomed. For the writers of the Bible and the New Testament treated those things which the soul has to do with God, and God with the soul, which these philosophers cannot push back. For knowledge and understanding of the Devil and spirits comes to us. Thus, this is also something to be fathomed for what it is. So we have the power to walk in all the works of God, of the kind found in the light of Nature.

For just as a sick person needs a physician, and a Christian needs his Redeemer, so too is such a creature necessary; they represent their purpose and are not created in vain. For Samson was a man: yet he had a strength that was neither natural nor believable, and he carried it in his hair: that was considered a necessary appearance by the ancients. ### CHAPTER II.
WHAT THE SPIRIT AND SOUL ARE: ALSO
*Their Spirit is Flesh, and their flesh is Spirit: An Example*
*of the Resurrection.*

The flesh must be understood in this way: that there are two kinds of flesh, the flesh from Adam, and that which is not from Adam. The flesh from Adam is a coarse flesh, for it is earthly, and is nothing other than a flesh that can be bound and held. The other flesh, which is not from Adam, is a subtle flesh, and can neither be bound nor grasped, for it is not made of the earth. Now, the flesh from Adam is the man from Adam, who is coarse like the earth; the same is compact, so that man cannot pass through a wall or a partition; he must make a hole for himself through which he passes, for nothing gives way to him. But the flesh that is not from Adam is that to which the wall gives way: that is, these same fleshes need no door, no hole, but go through entire walls and partitions and break nothing. Now they are both flesh, blood, bone, and the like, which belong to a human being, and in all nature like a human: but it happens that there are two origins, that is, two fathers. In the same way as a spirit and a human: the spirit goes through all walls and nothing blocks him; the man does not. This is to be weighed: thus people should recognize those of whom I write here. With the distinction, however, from spirits, it happens that they have blood and flesh and bones. Thereby they bear children and fruits, speak and eat, drink and walk, which things the spirits do not do. Therefore they are equal to spirits in speed, but to humans in procreation, form, and eating: and so they are people, or have a spirit-like nature in them, yet also a human nature, and are one thing.
<margin>B</margin>
Although they are both things, spirit and human, they are yet neither: for they cannot be humans, as they are spirit-like in their conduct; they cannot be spirits, for they eat and drink, and have blood and flesh. Therefore it is a special creature, outside of those two: and yet placed into these two kinds, a mixture made of both: like a composite of two pieces that does not appear as such; or two colors poured into one another, of one form, and yet both. But it is further to be understood in this also, that although they are spirit and human, they are yet neither. Man has a soul, but the spirit does not: the spirit has no soul, but man has one. This creature, however, is both, and yet has no soul, and is still not equal to the spirit, for the spirit does not die, but the creature dies. So it is not equal to man, for it has no soul: it is a beast <note>original: "Viech," referring to a soulless animal</note>, and yet above the beast, for it looks like the beast, and the animal body also has no soul, like the man, therefore it is a beast. And yet they speak and laugh like humans, therefore they are more like humans than the beast, and are neither man nor beast. Like an ape that resembles man in procreation and works, so are they toward man. And as a sow has the anatomy of a man, so that she is inside like a man, and yet is a sow, not a human: so also these creatures are to be compared to humans as apes and sows, and yet are better than those: for they are in every way like humans, only without a soul, and better than humans, for they are like the spirits whom no one can capture. Therefore Christ was born and died for those who have souls, that is, those who are from Adam: not for those who are not from Adam, for they are humans and yet have no soul. This much the Scripture allows of them, that they must be permitted to be humans: but as for the soul, there is no knowledge that they have it.
<margin>C</margin>
No one should wonder at this, that such a creature should exist: for God is wonderful in His works, which He often lets appear wonderfully. For these things are not daily before our eyes, but quite rare: and we see them only so that we carry a knowledge of these things, that they exist, and yet we count it as a dream. The great wisdom of God is not to be fathomed, nor

# ON PYGMIES AND SALAMANDERS.

<margin>A</margin> It is also necessary to investigate these great wonders—just as we are required to investigate in order to rightly recognize our Creator—in the miraculous things that have happened to us: namely, that they <note>The elemental beings</note> are not descended from Adam. They do not enjoy the same earth from which Adam was made, as was presented in the first treatise. They have children, and their children are like them, not unlike; yet Man is the image of God, that is, he is made according to His image. Now, Man is not God, even though he is made like Him; however, they <note>elementals</note> are not Men simply because they are made after His image, but they remain in their creation, the same creature that they are, and remain as God created them. Thus He wills every creature to be that for which it was created. And just as Man cannot boast that he is the Creator of God, but rather was made thus by God—and God wills it to be so—they cannot boast that they have a soul, even though they appear similar to him. Just as Man does not boast that he is God, even though he was made after Him, so Man [boasts] that he is not God. That the wild folk <note>original: "Wilden Leuth"</note> lack a soul, yet they are Men. Thus one belongs to God, the other to the soul: Man is a man alone.

<margin>B</margin> Thus they are humans and people who die with the cattle, yet walk with Men. That is: like the cattle, they die off so that nothing remains; yet neither fire nor [walls] can block them, like spirits; and no one may imprison them. In their increase <note>reproduction</note> they are like Men, and all their nature is the same. In their health they fall: not into the medicines of the earth upon which Man [dwells], but [those of] where they inhabit. They die like Men, but with the death of cattle: their flesh and bones are like other Men's bones, and no [soul] remains. Their gestures are human, their speech and ways are like all virtues, better and [worse], and likewise in form they are shaped differently and diversely, just as Men are. They [live like] Men, the work of their hands they measure, and they enjoy it themselves; [nature] allows them to use things, with wisdom to govern and equity [to act]. For although they are like cattle <note>i.e., lacking an immortal soul</note>, they nevertheless have all human reason, except for the judgment to serve God or walk in His ways, for they [lack a soul]. Therefore, like the cattle that act out of innate natural equity toward themselves, they do so in that place as well. And yet, above all other animals, they have the highest reason. They are creatures closest to God on Earth in understanding and gifts: they are the closest to Man, so near that they are called people and are held and esteemed as such. Thus there is no difference, except only for the spirit <note>the eternal soul</note>. A particularly wonderful creation, to be considered above all others.

---

### SECOND TREATISE
### On their Habitation.

<margin>C</margin> The habitations are of many kinds, that is, according to the four elements: one in the water, one in the air, one in the earth, one in the fire. Those in the water are Nymphs, those in the air are Sylphs, those in the earth are Pygmies, those in the fire are Salamanders. Now, as for them having "right" names, that is not the case; rather, such names as I present here are names given to them by those who did not truly know them. However, since they describe the things, I will let it remain at that. Although for the water-people *Undina* <note>Undine</note> is also a name, and for the air-people *Sylvestres* <note>Forest-people</note>, and for the mountain-people *Gnomi* <note>Gnomes</note>, and for the fire-people more often *Vulcani* <note>Vulcans</note> than Salamanders. Nevertheless, however it may be understood, let it remain so. Now you should know that if their regions are to be described, they must be divided into their parts: for the water-people have no business with the mountain-people, nor [the others] with them; likewise the *Sylvestres*, and likewise the Salamanders. Each [has its own] dwelling, but they appear to Man as stated above, so that he may know and see how wonderful God is in His works, that He lets no element be idle or empty, but has placed great wonders within them. Thus, four regions follow hereafter, and in these we include [how they differ] from one another in habitation, and also in person, essence, and kind; how far they are separated from one another, and yet are more similar to Man than to each other, and yet are all "people," as was contained in the first treatise.

<margin>D</margin> Now, as you know, there are four elements: Air, Water, Earth, and Fire. Now you know that we Men, the children of Adam, are and walk in the air, and are surrounded by it like a fish [in water]. [The fish] has its dwelling, and the water is in that place its "air" in which it lives: So it is [for the others]...

to the humans of the air, their water <note>The author is comparing how different beings perceive their environment; what is solid to us is "air" to them.</note> is misunderstood. Thus, every thing is created within its own elements to wander therein. Following this example, understand that the Undines <note>Water spirits or nymphs.</note> dwell in the water, and the water is given to them just as the air is given to us. And just as we marvel that they live in the water, so they marvel at us for living in the air. It is the same with the Gnomes in the mountains; the earth is their air and their *Chaos* <term>Chaos: Here used in the Paracelsian sense to mean the medium or atmosphere through which an elemental being moves and breathes.</term>. For every thing lives in its *Chaos*; that is, every thing dwells in its *Chaos*, walks, and moves within it. Now, the earth is nothing more than mere *Chaos* to the mountain-men <note>Gnomes or earth elementals.</note>. For they walk through solid walls, through cliffs, and through stone, just like a spirit; therefore, all those things are to them only *Chaos*—that is, nothing. This means that just as the air little hinders us from walking, so little are they hindered by the mountain, the earth, and the rocks. <margin>A</margin> He also provides for them: For it is not only possible for God to create the creatures known to us, but also in the fire, and in the waters, and in the earth. For He does not only clothe us, but also the Gnomes <note>original: "Geimen," likely a variant of Gnomi</note>, the Nymphs, the Salamanders, and the Forest-folk <note>original: "Syluestren"</note>: They are all under God’s protection and are all clothed and guided by Him. For God is not only powerful enough to provide for man, but also all others of whom man knows nothing; and man is slow in what he sees and experiences, so it is to him a wonder without fruit: That is, it does not grant him grace to see, but he remains choked and blinded, like one who has good eyes but lacks the grace to perceive.

But concerning their day, night, sleeping, and waking, it is a similar rest, sleep, and waking as with humans; that is, in the same measure as man. Therefore, they have the sun and the firmament just as well as we do. That is, the Little Mountain-men <note>Pygmies/Gnomes</note> have the earth as their chaos <note>In Paracelsian physics, "chaos" refers to the specific element an inhabitant breathes and lives in</note>. Now, to them it is only air and not earth, as it is to us. From this it follows that they can see through the earth just as we see through the air, and that the sun shines for them through the earth. For they have the air, and likewise have the sun and the moon and all the firmament before them.

Likewise the Undines <note>original: "Indianen," a common Paracelsian typo for Undinen/Water-beings</note>, whose water is their chaos: Now the water is not an obstruction to them against the sun, but just as we have the sun through the air, so they have it through the water. The Fire-beings <note>original: "Vulcanischen"</note> are to be understood in the same way; they also see through their chaos, just as the sun shines on us on earth and makes the earth fruitful: so that it is the same with them as with us. Therefore it follows that they have day, night, and the like. But as for rain, snow, and such things, they do not have them as we do, but they have them in other ways. These are the great wonders of God.

It follows now that they have the Plague, Fevers <note>original: "Febres"</note>, Pleurisy <note>original: "Pleureses"</note>, and all diseases of the firmament. For they have them and must in all ways rise and lie down with us, though they are not of Adam's seed. They have no soul, and they do not appear before the judgment of God in the resurrection; there they are beasts and not humans.

<margin>B</margin> But concerning their persons, you should know that they are distinct: The Nymphs are of human proportion, both women and men: The Forest-folk are the same, but coarser, taller, and stronger than both; the Mountain-men are small, about two spans high <note>roughly 18 inches</note>; the Salamanders are long, small, and thin. Now, however, they dwell in their chaos. As the Nymphs in the water, in flowing streams, so that they seize people who ride through or bathe therein. The Mountain-men dwell in the mountains, and there they make their dwellings. Therefore one often finds floors, passages, and such things in the earth, at the height of an ell <note>a historical unit of length</note> or similar, which were built by them for their maintenance and habitation. Thus they are found in many places and spots. Likewise, know of the Mountain-men that they dwell in the mountains, which is why strange buildings are found in those places; and likewise with us from the fire, and in the Etna mountains <note>Mount Etna, Sicily</note> there is shouting, noise, and work heard, which is found in the burning of the element: For they have their habitation there according to their secret <term>Arcana</term> <note>hidden spiritual or medicinal properties</note> qualities. To experience the ground of such things happens in the wild forests, where those who travel through them encounter them; in the mines near good ore and the like, they are seen; in the waters likewise; and by Etna, the Fire-beings. And much more could be said of these things, of their money, customs, and manners, which does not belong to this primary purpose, but

<margin>C</margin> will be described in its proper place.

### TRACTATUS III.
## How they come to us and become visible to us.

<margin>D</margin> That which God has created, He allows to become manifest to man and to come before him, so that the creatures are and become known to man. For thus God revealed the Devil to man, who is presented for man to recognize: Thus also He sent the Angels down from Heaven to man, so that man might truly see that God has Angels who serve Him. And such revelations happen, but rarely, only as much as is necessary to believe in them and hold to them. Thus it also happens with the things of which I write here; they also appear: Not that they should all dwell with us, or stay, or be bound to us, but God lets them wander and be with us only as much as is necessary for us to take knowledge of them, that God works wonderful deeds. Thus, when He sends an Angel to us, we experience that the Scripture speaks rightly of Angels. When we have knowledge of one, we do not need it constantly, because the seed of man grows so that it is not necessary to present these things every day. Thus God once presented these creatures to man and let them be seen, to walk with man, talk, and the like, so that man would know that such creatures exist in the four elements, which are wonderful to behold.
